title: CmdPal: Grid view is sensitive to preview pane timing
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.102

### Installation method

Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

Create a page with a grid or gallery view and give the items a details pane that takes a bit of time to load.

Browse the page for a while, and you'll notice that the delayed loading of the details pane for a newly selected item causes the entire layout to shift like mad.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

All items on the page shift when the details pane hides while its content is loading.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

All items on the page shifts when detail pane hides when content is being loaded.

title: [UI Tests] Power Display virtual monitor fixtures (UMDF/IddCx)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add test-only virtual monitor fixtures for Power Display UI tests using a UMDF indirect display driver (IDD/IddCx), if a feasibility spike confirms compatibility with Power Display's real Windows display discovery and DDC/CI APIs.

This is a separate follow-up to #51550 and #51784, not a prerequisite for the initial Power Display UI-test PR.

Start with two independently identifiable virtual displays, controllable arrival/departure, and stateful brightness emulation. Keep the driver and its provisioning outside PowerToys installers. Reuse the provisioning and cleanup practices from Grab and Move's UMDF fixture, not its HID implementation.

### Scenario when this would be used?

The initial suite verifies the no-supported-monitors path in Hyper-V, but cannot reliably exercise monitors-present inventory or supported-monitor brightness. Merely adding Windows display surfaces is insufficient: Power Display needs valid physical-monitor handles and usable DDC/CI capabilities.

Deterministic fixtures would allow local VM and remote CI coverage of:

- Two-monitor inventory, stable IDs, and independent per-monitor state.
- Identify overlays and placement on each connected display.
- Hot-plug/remove, Refresh, and return to a stable inventory.
- Brightness set/readback and persistence across rediscovery, with requests observed by the fixture rather than inferred solely from UI state.
- Controlled unsupported-capability and communication-failure cases without silent fallback or false success.

These tests would prove emulated Windows/DDC/CI integration, not physical-panel backlight behavior, the WMI hardware path, or physical mixed-DPI/multi-monitor signoff.

### Supporting information

#### Feasibility and implementation gates

- [ ] Build an architecture-matched, test-only IddCx prototype and expose two monitors in an isolated guest. Verify Windows enumeration and Power Display inventory through the existing production path.
- [ ] Prove `GetPhysicalMonitorsFromHMONITOR` returns usable handles and Power Display's Dxva2/DDC/CI requests reach `EVT_IDD_CX_MONITOR_I2C_TRANSMIT` / `EVT_IDD_CX_MONITOR_I2C_RECEIVE`. This routing is not yet verified; display enumeration alone is not success.
- [ ] Emulate the capabilities and MCCS/VCP responses Power Display actually requires, including brightness VCP `0x10`, independent state, stable identity, and deterministic monitor arrival/departure.
- [ ] Reuse Grab and Move's established architecture-specific VM/CI setup and verify the new IDD package signs, installs, and loads under that image's policy. The isolated ARM64 VM requires Secure Boot off; this is an existing working configuration, not an unresolved ARM64 blocker. Do not assume importing a certificate alone guarantees acceptance of the new IDD package.
- [ ] Adapt Grab and Move's pinned build inputs, short-lived signing, artifact hash validation, separate elevated provisioning, readiness checks, and ownership-journal cleanup. Export only public certificates to guests; never import execution-machine trust on the build host.
- [ ] Provide a transport-only probe with callback/readback evidence before relying on UI assertions. Record architecture, driver version/hashes, signing and boot policy, PnP readiness, and SetupAPI/Code Integrity diagnostics on failure.
- [ ] Run product/tests in the standard-user console desktop. Restrict fixtures to approved isolated guests and restore topology, owned devices/packages, and imported test trust after successful, failed, or interrupted runs.
- [ ] Validate the full Power Display suite on Windows 10 and Windows 11 x64 at Default and Constrained resources, then fresh remote CI, including Windows 11 ARM64 through the existing dedicated UMDF CI configuration and appropriately provisioned isolated VM. Report any new IDD-specific load/routing failures as BLOCKED, not green or silently skipped.

If native DDC/CI routing or an acceptable signing route cannot be established, document the blocker and separately evaluate an injectable backend. Do not silently substitute it while claiming end-to-end driver coverage.

#### Grab and Move reference approach

- #51634: **[UI Tests] Grab and Move new UI tests** introduces a separately provisioned UMDF virtual-HID fixture because shipping Grab and Move rejects injected input. The product filters remain unchanged and there is no `SendInput` fallback.
- [Grab and Move architecture/signing prerequisites](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/2fb32e34068d059abbb48f0d5a01498158d65dd1/doc/devdocs/modules/grabandmove.md#architecture-and-signing-prerequisites): its self-signed HID bundle was validated on Windows 10/11 x64 with ordinary boot policy and Secure Boot enabled, without `TESTSIGNING`. ARM64 also works: its dedicated UMDF CI configuration has already been added, and the isolated ARM64 VM requires Secure Boot off. Reuse the documented owner-preprovisioned `TESTSIGNING` image rather than treating ARM64 as an outstanding blocker. This existing HID setup is prior art, not proof that the new IDD package or DDC/CI routing will work unchanged.
- [Driver build/signing helper](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/2fb32e34068d059abbb48f0d5a01498158d65dd1/.pipelines/umdf-hid-smoke/Build-Smoke.ps1) and [provisioning/owned cleanup helper](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/2fb32e34068d059abbb48f0d5a01498158d65dd1/.pipelines/umdf-hid-smoke/Manage-SmokeDriver.ps1): trusted catalog/binaries, guest-only certificate installation, fixed device identity, explicit readiness, and removal of only journaled resources. The scripts do not change boot policy.
- [Dedicated ARM64 CI guidance](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/2fb32e34068d059abbb48f0d5a01498158d65dd1/doc/devdocs/development/ui-tests.md#dedicated-arm64-grab-and-move-ci-image): the dedicated ARM64 UMDF route is already implemented. Adapt that existing configuration for the IDD fixture while keeping its specially provisioned image isolated from ordinary CI jobs.

Driver-package signing is separate from PowerToys Runner/Settings authenticated IPC companion signing. Any driver requiring a boot-policy change must use an explicitly approved, owner-provisioned disposable image; do not weaken host or ordinary CI policy.

#### Power Display and platform references

- [Power Display physical-monitor discovery](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/6780ea86d804b83ee3d457a3a255c767945d68b1/src/modules/powerdisplay/PowerDisplay.Lib/Drivers/DDC/MonitorDiscoveryHelper.cs).
- [Microsoft IDD overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/display/indirect-display-driver-model-overview) and [IndirectDisplay sample](https://github.com/microsoft/Windows-driver-samples/tree/main/video/IndirectDisplay).
- [IddCx I2C transmit](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/iddcx/nc-iddcx-evt_idd_cx_monitor_i2c_transmit) and [I2C receive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/iddcx/nc-iddcx-evt_idd_cx_monitor_i2c_receive) callbacks.

title: Power Display: switching profiles does not apply color temperature — must manually re-select in menu
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.102.3001

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Power Display and switch between two existing profiles: one set to a Warm color temperature (User 1) and one set to a Normal color temperature (8200K).
2. Observe the monitor's actual color output.
3. Open the Color Temperature submenu in Power Display.
4. Manually click the color temperature option that is already checkmarked/selected.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

When switching profiles, the monitor should immediately change its color temperature to match the profile settings (e.g., switching from a Warm profile to a Normal profile should instantly make the screen cooler).

### ❌ Actual Behavior

1. Color Temperature Menu Display: The Color Temperature submenu shows hex codes next to the preset names (e.g., "8200K (0x07)", "User 1 (0x0B)"). I am not sure if this was present before the update, as I did not interact with these menus previously.

2. Profile Naming: Numbers in brackets appeared automatically next to my profile names after the update, like this: `"Warm. Low B&C (#1)"`, `"Normal. B10 (#4)"`. I did not name them this way; the program added them.

3. Functional Bug: When switching between profiles with different color temperatures (e.g., Warm [User 1] to Normal [8200K]), the monitor's actual color temperature does not change. The UI checkmark updates correctly to show the new preset is selected, but the screen remains at the previous color temperature. The only way to make it work is to manually open the color temperature menu and re-select the already checkmarked value.

4. Brightness works correctly: Brightness changes immediately when switching profiles. Only color temperature fails to apply on profile switch.

Context on my profiles:
- Profiles 1 & 2 ("Warm"): Use "User 1" preset (0x0B).
- Profiles 3–6 ("Normal"): Use "8200K" preset (0x07).

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-31-12-56-38.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34214249/PowerToysReport_2026-10-31-12-56-38.zip)

title: Mouse Buttons Remapping
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add Left mouse button , Right Mouse Button and Middle Mouse Button to Keyboard  Manager or make a Mouse Button Manager
You can implement it through the Select Key and Search Keys function .

### Scenario when this would be used?

Blender doesn’t let you Remap your inputs like Left Mouse Button or Alt 
It does have a numpad option where it lets you use Alt + Right Mouse Button to move your camera but you still need to press Middle Mouse Button + Alt to use Axis Snap so it ends up not solving my problem
I want to switch Middle Mouse Button with Left Mouse Button because i use Middle Mouse Button (MMB) a lot more than Left Mouse Button (LMB) which i find uncomfortable , thank you for listening .

My enhancement request is changing the app to allow for .reg files of a much greater size.

| Size | Reg File Name |

| 153MB | HKEY_CURRENT_USER.reg |

title: Print log of changes made in PowerRename
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

When I use the PowerRename feature, I would like to have the option to print a log of the changes I made to my file names within the folder. Examples of how you might log this in a file might be to print my "find" and "replace" terms and exporting "before" and "after" lists of the files in the folder to the log. Ideally it would show both. The most common reason for needing to rename files is that the file paths are getting too long, so another related helpful feature would be to print out file path lengths. 

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would be useful because when I rename files in bulk at work, we need a record of the "before" and "after" names to ensure that everyone on the team knows where to find them. I would generally be using this on files in shared drives that many other people need to be able to access.

title: Save and restore display arrangement layouts
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add a quick way to save and restore display arrangement layouts when using two or more displays.

A layout could store settings such as:

- The relative position of each display, for example left, right, above, or below another display
- Display orientation, such as landscape or portrait
- Which display is set as the main display

Users could create several named layouts and quickly switch between them from a PowerToys menu or shortcut, without manually rearranging the displays in Windows Display Settings each time.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I frequently change the physical arrangement of my laptop and external monitor depending on what I am doing. Sometimes I use both screens side by side in landscape orientation. When reading documents, I rotate the external monitor to portrait and keep the laptop in landscape. At other times, I rearrange them to free up desk space for writing.

Each change currently requires manually rearranging the displays and changing their orientation in Windows Display Settings.

PowerToys could allow me to save these configurations as profiles such as Side by side, Reading, and Desk space, then restore the appropriate display arrangement with a few clicks or a keyboard shortcut.

This would essentially provide display layout profiles for physical monitor arrangements, complementing tools such as FancyZones, which focus on arranging application windows rather than the displays themselves.

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: Mouse Utilites, Mouse Button Lock: Add visual feedback when lock engages
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement
A visual indication of when the Mouse Button Lock Feature has been engaged / is active.
This can probably be a fairly subtle visual cue near- or on the mouse cursor, since that is where the user is likely looking already.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When you hold down a mouse button to activate the Mouse Button Lock feature, to help know when the feature has been engaged.

### Supporting information

Even with the current ability to tweak "Hold Duration" it is very hard to gauge how long the button needs to be held.

The user is likely to hold down the mouse button longer than needed, adding back some of that strain that the feature aims to alleviate. The user can also become frustrated when moving the mouse too soon, before the lock has time to engage, forcing the user to start the process of holding down the mouse button in place again.

title: Mouse Without Borders won't reconnect after both PCs drop off the network
body:

0.102.3001

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

When both of my PCs lose their network connection at the same time and then come back online, Mouse Without Borders doesn't automatically start working again — I lose the ability to use my keyboard and mouse across the two screens.
I tried clicking Mouse Without Borders in PowerToys' Quick Access on each PC, but I still couldn't control the other machine (older versions used to recover just fine from this). I even went into Settings → Input & Output → Mouse Without Borders and clicked "Refresh connection" on both PCs, but that didn't bring it back either (the old version could recover this way).
The only thing that works is toggling the feature off and back on again, which is really annoying to deal with.

title: Right Alt + Copilot (F23) shortcut causes stuck modifiers and unexpected keyboard behaviour on virtual desktops
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.102.3001

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

## Bug description

After a recent PowerToys update introduced the new Keyboard Manager editor, my custom shortcut started causing abnormal keyboard behaviour when used with Windows Virtual Desktops.

**Shortcut configuration:**
- **Shortcut:** Right Alt + Copilot key (F23)
- **Mapped to:** Left Alt + F4
- **Purpose:** Close the currently active application.

The shortcut worked correctly before the update and before I started using virtual desktops.

After recreating the mapping in the new editor, triggering the shortcut while using a virtual desktop causes keyboard input to behave as though modifier keys are stuck. For example, pressing `F` in Microsoft Edge opens the Find feature instead of typing the letter. Pressing `Z` in Windows Start search has also unexpectedly produced the text `not`. Windows-key behaviour and virtual-desktop switching can become abnormal as well.

Disabling Keyboard Manager does not always immediately restore normal keyboard behaviour, but restarting Windows resolves the issue. However, the problem can recur when the shortcut is triggered again.

I inspected the configuration in both the new and Classic editors. The Classic editor showed two mappings targeting `Alt + F4`: one using `Right Alt + F23` and another using the full Copilot-key combination (`Win + Ctrl + Shift + Right Alt + F23`). I have not confirmed whether the duplicate mappings contribute to the issue.

**Possible causes to investigate:**
- A regression in the new Keyboard Manager editor.
- Incorrect handling or release of modifier keys when the Copilot key generates a multi-key combination.
- An interaction between duplicate mappings.
- An interaction with Windows Virtual Desktops or Windows keyboard-input handling.

The exact root cause is not yet confirmed.

**Expected behaviour:** The shortcut should close the active application and release all modifier keys correctly, without affecting subsequent typing, Windows-key behaviour or virtual-desktop switching.

Could you investigate whether Keyboard Manager can leave modifier keys in a stuck state when this shortcut is triggered, particularly with the new editor and Windows Virtual Desktops?

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

When I press `Right Alt + Copilot (F23)`, PowerToys Keyboard Manager should send `Left Alt + F4` once and close the currently active application window. All modifier keys should be released correctly after the shortcut executes. Normal keyboard input, Windows-key functionality, and virtual desktop switching should continue to work as expected, without triggering unintended application shortcuts or leaving any keys in a stuck state.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

After triggering the configured shortcut while using Windows Virtual Desktops, keyboard input behaves abnormally, as though one or more modifier keys remain pressed.

For example:
- Pressing `F` in Microsoft Edge opens the Find feature instead of typing the letter.
- Pressing `Z` in the Windows Start search unexpectedly produces the text `not`.
- Windows-key behaviour and virtual desktop switching can become abnormal.

Disabling PowerToys Keyboard Manager does not always immediately restore normal keyboard behaviour. Restarting Windows restores normal operation, but the issue can recur after triggering the shortcut again.

The problem appeared after a PowerToys update and recreating the shortcut in the new Keyboard Manager editor. The shortcut previously worked correctly. The exact cause, including whether the new editor, duplicate mappings or virtual desktops contribute to the issue, has not yet been confirmed.

title: [Mouse Jump] - performance improvement - blurred scheenshot placeholders
body: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement In order to be responsive, Mouse Jump has a built in rendering budget of 250ms when it's activated in order to render as much of the preview image as it can before showing the interim state to the user. When it shows this interim state it first draws any missing screenshots with a blank background image (colours configurable in Settings). This serves 2 purposes: * Minimise flickering by waiting 250ms to draw as much as it can * Be responsive by showing the preview to the user after 250ms anyway regardless of how much is already drawn Here's an exaggerated video of it in action: https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/1193763/231855964-51f54db2-e2df-457b-9f3a-73ca6e5c0536.mp4?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..F80aUq2FHZsRG7yvXDy3flxU8R0Sz_r47Xhpwx2QzTo The *perception* of performance could be improved by showing something different than the "blank background" for screens that haven't been drawn yet. The upstream FancyMouse retains the screenshots from the previous activation and shows a blurred version of these instead on the basis that the screen is probably very similar to what it was before, and when the new screenshot is available it transitions between the vlurred version and the new screenshot. As a safety net it expires the previous images after 2 minutes and draws the "blank background" instead. This does 2 things: * Reduces flicker even more by showing a blurred screenshot instead of the "blank background" and transitions this to the new screenshot when it becomes available * Makes the preview *appear* to initialise faster since the blurred images are very similar to the real screen in most cases ### Scenario when this would be used? Mouse Jump *feels* more responsive whenever the preview is activated with slow screen captures. ### Supporting information _No response_

title: Cross-Application QuickParts / Rich Text Snippets
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add a PowerToys utility that provides reusable text snippets (“Quick Parts”) across Windows applications.

Users could create and manage a library of frequently used text blocks, assign each a short trigger, name, or keyboard shortcut, and insert them into the active text field in virtually any application.

The experience could support:
- Plain-text and rich-text snippets where the target application supports formatting
- Searchable snippet library / picker
- Keyboard shortcuts or typed triggers
- Categories or folders for organizing snippets
- Variables or placeholders for content that changes between uses
- Optional import/migration from existing Outlook Quick Parts or other snippet libraries

The goal is to make reusable text a Windows-level productivity capability rather than something tied to a specific application.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I frequently reuse the same blocks of text across Outlook, Teams, Edge, Microsoft 365 apps, Copilot prompts, support forms, and other applications.

Outlook Quick Parts works well for reusable content inside Outlook, but that content is not available when I move into another application.

For example, I may have a standardized explanation, set of instructions, prompt, project description, troubleshooting response, or template that I use dozens of times. Today I either have to find an old message, maintain a separate document of snippets, or recreate the content.

With a PowerToys QuickParts/text-snippet utility, I could invoke a shortcut anywhere in Windows, search for the saved snippet, insert it at the cursor, and continue working.

For users who work across many applications all day, this would turn reusable text into a system-wide productivity primitive.


### Supporting information

The closest mental model is Outlook Quick Parts combined with a lightweight text expander, implemented as a PowerToys utility.

A simple MVP could focus on:
1. Create/edit/delete text snippets
2. Open a searchable snippet picker with a global keyboard shortcut
3. Insert the selected snippet into the active text field
4. Organize snippets by name/category
5. Store the library locally with backup/export/import support

Future enhancements could include:
- Typed abbreviations/triggers
- Dynamic placeholders such as date/time or clipboard contents
- User-defined fill-in fields before insertion
- Rich-text support
- Sync/roaming
- Import from Outlook Quick Parts
- Optional integration with PowerToys Command Palette

The key requirement is application independence: the same reusable snippet should work in Outlook, Teams, a browser, Notepad, Copilot, and other Windows applications without maintaining separate libraries.

title: [Mouse Without Borders] Service Mode fails in 0.102.3001.0 — works after rollback to 0.101.2362.0
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

PowerToys 0.102.3001.0

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

### Mouse Without Borders Service Mode regression in PowerToys 0.102.3001.0

We reproduced a Mouse Without Borders Service Mode issue on two computers running Windows 10 and Windows 11.

**Affected version:** PowerToys 0.102.3001.0  
**Last confirmed working version:** PowerToys 0.101.2362.0

**Observed behavior**

After upgrading to 0.102.3001.0, enabling **Use Service** fails with the following message:

`Mouse Without Borders could not switch service mode. Restart PowerToys and try again.`

The issue occurs on both computers and persists after a complete uninstall, reboot, and clean installation of the affected version.

Normal mouse sharing continues to work, but Service Mode cannot be enabled successfully.

**Diagnostic observations**

- Runtime logs repeatedly contain `Rejected Settings IPC client: untrusted-signature`.
- The inspected PowerToys executables have valid Microsoft Authenticode signatures.
- The MWB Windows service is not registered automatically.
- Manual service registration succeeds.
- When started manually, the service reports successful startup followed by a clean shutdown approximately 2–3 seconds later, with exit code 0.
- Occasional `settings.json` file-sharing errors were also observed, although their relationship to the Service Mode failure is unknown.

**Rollback verification**

Both computers were rolled back to PowerToys **0.101.2362.0** without changing their security configuration.

After rollback:

- Service Mode can be enabled without errors.
- Mouse and keyboard sharing work normally.
- Remote mouse and keyboard control work at the Windows lock screen.
- Remote mouse control works on a UAC consent prompt.

**Conclusion**

The results strongly suggest a regression introduced between PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 and 0.102.3001.0.

The repeated `untrusted-signature` messages may indicate an IPC signature-verification issue, but the exact root cause has not been established.

Please investigate whether changes to Mouse Without Borders Service Mode or IPC signature verification in 0.102.3001.0 could explain this behavior.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

When **Use Service** is enabled in Mouse Without Borders, PowerToys should activate Service Mode successfully without displaying an error.

Service Mode should allow remote mouse and keyboard control on the Windows lock screen and during UAC elevation prompts.

This functionality worked correctly in PowerToys **0.101.2362.0**.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

After upgrading to PowerToys **0.102.3001.0**, enabling **Use Service** fails with the following error:

`Mouse Without Borders could not switch service mode. Restart PowerToys and try again.`

The issue was reproduced on two computers running Windows 10 and Windows 11.

**Observations:**
- Normal mouse and keyboard sharing continues to work.
- Service Mode cannot be enabled successfully.
- The issue persists after a complete uninstall, reboot, and clean installation.
- Runtime logs repeatedly report `Rejected Settings IPC client: untrusted-signature`.
- The inspected PowerToys executables have valid Microsoft Authenticode signatures.
- The MWB Windows service was not registered automatically.
- Manual service registration succeeded, but the service stopped cleanly approximately 2–3 seconds after starting, with exit code 0.
- Occasional `settings.json` file-sharing errors were also observed.

**Rollback verification:**

After rolling back both computers to **0.101.2362.0**, without changing their security configurations:

- Service Mode enabled successfully.
- Remote mouse and keyboard control worked at the Windows lock screen.
- Remote mouse control worked during a UAC consent prompt.

These results strongly suggest a regression in PowerToys 0.102.3001.0. The exact underlying cause has not been established.

title: [Power Display] LG Flatron L194W (EdidId: GSM4B6B) DDC/CI probe locks up monitor I2C bus and causes monitor to disconnect from Windows (similar to #47968)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.102.3001

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect a secondary monitor **LG Flatron L194W** (`EdidId: GSM4B6B`, connected via DVI or DP-to-DVI) alongside a primary HDMI/DP monitor.
2. Enable **Power Display** in PowerToys (`v0.102.3001.0`).
3. Power Display starts monitor discovery (`DdcCiController.DiscoverFromHandleAsync`) and sends 3 consecutive DDC/CI capability probe requests (`FetchCapabilitiesWithFallbackAsync`) to `GSM4B6B`:
   ```text
   [Info] DdcCiController.cs::DiscoverFromHandleAsync::804
       DDC: probing capabilities [EdidId=GSM4B6B] [FriendlyName='L194W'] [DevicePath=\\?\DISPLAY#GSM4B6B#5&b3bfee9&7&UID155904#{e6f07b5f-ee97-4a90-b076-33f57bf4eaa7}]
   [Warning] DdcCiController.cs::FetchCapabilitiesWithFallbackAsync::453
       DDC: cap string fetch attempt 1 returned empty (handle=0x1); retrying in 1000ms
   [Warning] DdcCiController.cs::FetchCapabilitiesWithFallbackAsync::453
       DDC: cap string fetch attempt 2 returned empty (handle=0x1); retrying in 1000ms
   [Warning] DdcCiController.cs::FetchCapabilitiesWithFallbackAsync::477
       DDC: cap string still empty after 3 attempts (handle=0x1)
   ```
4. The monitor's internal scaler/I2C controller locks up upon receiving DDC/CI capability queries, causing the GPU driver to lose EDID/link communication and drop the display from Windows (`LiveKernelEvent` watchdog `1a8` / `1b8`, PnP status becomes `Unknown`).
5. Recovering the monitor requires physically unplugging the monitor's power cord for 30 seconds to reset its internal microcontroller.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

1. Add **`GSM4B6B`** (LG Flatron L194W) to `PowerDisplay.Models.BuiltInMonitorBlacklist.json` alongside `GSM7714` (#47968) and `LTM2C02` (#47556):
   ```json
   {
     "edidId": "GSM4B6B",
     "comments": "LG Flatron L194W locks up on DDC/CI probe"
   }
   ```
   *(Verified locally: patching `BuiltInMonitorBlacklist.json` in `PowerDisplay.Models.dll` to include `GSM4B6B` results in `[MonitorBlacklist] Skipping 'L194W' (EdidId 'GSM4B6B') — EdidId is on the blacklist` and completely resolves the issue.)*
2. Ideally, provide a user-configurable blacklist (or per-monitor DDC/CI opt-out in `settings.json`) so users can exclude incompatible monitors without waiting for hardcoded blacklist updates or losing the fix after every PowerToys update.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Because `GSM4B6B` is not in `BuiltInMonitorBlacklist.json`, Power Display probes it via DDC/CI on startup. This hangs the monitor's internal I2C/DDC controller, causing the display to completely disappear from Windows (either immediately when connected via DP adapter or across reboots/driver resets when connected via native DVI) until the monitor is physically power-cycled by unplugging AC power.

title: [Enhancement] Optional Context Menu Grouping
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

With the new customisable context menus coming in Windows 11 25H2/26H2, it would be really useful if there were a global setting that would group all of the context menu items in PowerToys under a "Microsoft PowerToys" submenu to optionally allow them to be grouped either in the new App extensions menu (which itself can become quite large) or moved to the main context menu, without again cluttering it.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Users wanting to simplify their context menus whilst retaining access to the features in PowerToys.

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: Automatic virtual desktop naming
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add a utility that automatically names Windows virtual desktops, so users don't have to rename each one by hand. Windows 11 supports custom desktop names, but every new desktop starts as "Desktop 1", "Desktop 2" and so on. These names say nothing about what's on the desktop.

Proposed behavior (each option could be a setting):
- **Name by foreground app or window title.** Use the name of the main app on the desktop, for example "Visual Studio Code" or "Chrome".
- **Name by rules.** Let users map a process name or window title pattern to a desktop name, for example `Code.exe` -> "Coding".
- **Name by template.** Support patterns such as `{app} - {index}`.
- **Keep manual names.** Never overwrite a name the user set by hand. Only unnamed desktops are renamed automatically.
- **Update when the content changes.** Refresh the name when the main window changes, or on a configurable interval.
- **Enable or disable the utility.** Add it to the PowerToys settings like the other modules.

### Scenario when this would be used?

- Developers and power users who keep several desktops open at once (code, browser, chat, design) and lose track of which is which. The Task View thumbnails are small and hard to tell apart.
- Users who create and close desktops all day. Renaming each new desktop by hand every time is tedious, so most people never do it and live with "Desktop 4".
- Workflows that always use the same apps per desktop, where a fixed rule such as `Code.exe` -> "Coding" would name the desktop correctly every time.
- Accessibility: readable names help people using screen readers or Narrator, who otherwise only hear "Desktop N".

### Supporting information

- Windows 11 supports renaming desktops in Task View, so a name can be stored per desktop. This module would set it automatically.
- Related PowerToys modules this could sit next to: FancyZones and Workspaces (both deal with window layout and app grouping), and Quick Accent / Command Palette if virtual desktop switching is exposed there.
- Similar behavior exists in third-party tools such as VirtualDesktopManager, Windows 11 Taskbar tweaks, and tiling window manager workspace naming (i3/sway, `workspace_name` by app).
- I'm happy to test early builds. [Add: any existing issue numbers you find that overlap, and your Windows version.]

title: Power Display: Volume (VCP 0x62) unavailable on Gigabyte M32U although the monitor responds to it
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.102.3001.0

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect a Gigabyte M32U monitor (DDC/CI enabled in the OSD) [via DisplayPort].
2. Enable Power Display, turn on "Max compatibility mode" in Power Display settings.
3. Open the per-monitor controls for the Gigabyte M32U: the "Volume" toggle is greyed out and cannot be enabled.
4. Run:   `PowerToys.PowerDisplay.CLI.exe set --monitor-number 1 --volume 30`

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Volume control is available for this monitor. The monitor responds to VCP 0x62 even though its capabilities string does not list it. With "Max compatibility mode" on (which is documented to ignore the capabilities string and probe VCP features directly) volume should be probed and enabled.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The "Volume" toggle stays disabled (`supportsVolume: false`) and the CLI returns:

```
Error: setting volume is not supported
  monitor: Monitor 1 (Gigabyte M32U)
  diagnostic: monitor's VCP capabilities did not advertise audio speaker volume (0x62)
```

The monitor's capabilities string (`capabilitiesRaw` from settings.json) does not contain 0x62:

```
(prot(monitor)type(LCD)model(GIGABYTE)cmds(01 02 03 07 0C E3 F3)vcp(02 04 05 06 08 0B 0C 10 12 14(01 02 04 05 06 08 0B) 16 18 1A 52 60(01 03 0F 11) 87 AC AE B2 B6 C6 C8 CA CC(01 02 03 04 06 0A 0D) D6(01 04 05) DF FD FF)mswhql(1)asset_eep(40)mccs_ver(2.2))
```

However, the monitor does respond to VCP 0x62. Reading it directly through the Windows Monitor Configuration API (`GetVCPFeatureAndVCPFeatureReply`, code 0x62) succeeds and returns current = 50, maximum = 100.

Twinkle Tray controls the volume of this same monitor without any problem.

Editing `capabilitiesRaw` / `supportsVolume` in settings.json does not help: the file is overwritten with the monitor's original capabilities on the next start.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

Suggested fix: when a VCP code (such as 0x62) is missing from the capabilities string, "Max compatibility mode" should still probe it directly, or there should be a per-monitor option to force-enable volume regardless of the capabilities string. Several monitors do not list 0x62 in their capabilities but respond to it anyway.

### Other Software

Twinkle Tray 1.17.2 (volume control works with the same monitor).
Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200.

title: [Mouse Without Borders] settings.json writes fail with sharing violation – writer and readers use incompatible FileShare modes
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Two Windows 10 (19045) machines connected via Mouse Without Borders, service mode OFF.
2. Keep the PowerToys Settings window open.
3. Press Ctrl+Alt+R (reconnect), or let the peer reconnect.
4. Check the log in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\MouseWithoutBorders\Logs\`.

With service mode ON the failure rate is much higher (two SYSTEM-side processes plus the user-side Settings app touching the same file). Saved configuration – security key, machine layout, Easy Mouse – is frequently lost across reboots, and the two machines end up with different security keys ("Magic number invalid / Checksum invalid" spam in the log).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Settings writes always succeed and configuration (security key, machine layout, Easy Mouse) persists across reboots.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Log shows repeated:
```
[Error] SettingsUtils.cs::SaveSettings::224
Exception encountered while saving MouseWithoutBorders settings.
System.IO.IOException (-2147024864): The process cannot access the file '...\MouseWithoutBorders\settings.json' because it is being used by another process.
   at System.IO.File.WriteAllText(String path, String contents)
   at System.IO.Abstractions.FileWrapper.WriteAllText(String path, String contents)
   at Microsoft.PowerToys.Settings.UI.Library.SettingsUtils.SaveSettings(String jsonSettings, String powertoy, String fileName)
```

**Root cause (Process Monitor, filtered to settings.json):**
- Writer – `PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe` opens with `Generic Write, OverwriteIf, ShareMode: Read`.
- Readers – `PowerToys.Settings.exe`, `PowerToys.QuickAccess.exe` and other threads of `PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe` itself open with `Generic Read, ShareMode: Read` (deny write).
- Each side denies the other, so whichever arrives second gets `SHARING VIOLATION`. When the writer is second, `SaveSettings` throws and the write is lost.
- After a change, Settings.exe and QuickAccess.exe re-read the file every ~110 ms, creating repeated windows where an MWB write fails.
- MWB also writes the same file twice within ~5 ms on reconnect.

```
51.2828601 MouseWithoutBorders.exe CreateFile  SUCCESS            Generic Write, OverwriteIf, ShareMode: Read
51.2831893 MouseWithoutBorders.exe WriteFile   SUCCESS            Length: 2,566
51.2840926 Settings.exe            CreateFile  SHARING VIOLATION  Generic Read, ShareMode: Read
51.2841107 MouseWithoutBorders.exe CreateFile  SHARING VIOLATION  Generic Read, ShareMode: Read
51.2876770 MouseWithoutBorders.exe CreateFile  SUCCESS            Generic Write, OverwriteIf, ShareMode: Read
51.2877630 Settings.exe            CreateFile  SHARING VIOLATION  Generic Read, ShareMode: Read
51.2884525 MouseWithoutBorders.exe CreateFile  SHARING VIOLATION  Generic Read, ShareMode: Read
51.2888006 Settings.exe            CreateFile  SHARING VIOLATION  Generic Read, ShareMode: Read
51.39 / 51.50 / 51.62 / 51.73  Settings.exe + QuickAccess.exe re-read the file (~110 ms cadence)
```

**Suggested fix:**
- Read with `FileShare.ReadWrite` (`new FileStream(path, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read, FileShare.ReadWrite)`) instead of `File.ReadAllText`.
- Write atomically: temp file + `File.Replace` / `File.Move(overwrite: true)`, with a short retry on `IOException`.
- Serialize/debounce MWB's own writes (double write on reconnect).

Related: #26537

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Suggested fix:**
- Read with `FileShare.ReadWrite` (`new FileStream(path, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read, FileShare.ReadWrite)`) instead of `File.ReadAllText`.
- Write atomically: temp file + `File.Replace` / `File.Move(overwrite: true)`, with a short retry on `IOException`.
- Serialize/debounce MWB's own writes (double write on reconnect).

Related: #26537

### Other Software

Bitdefender – not implicated: Process Monitor shows it only attempts a read-only section mapping and backs off (FILE LOCKED WITH WRITERS); it never holds the file.

body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.102.3001

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

# [Power Display] External DDC/CI monitor disappears after another PC reboots; restarting PowerToys restores detection

**PowerToys version:** 1.102.3001

**Affected module:** Power Display

**Environment**
- Laptop: Windows 11, Intel HD Graphics 630
- Internal display: AUO38ED
- External monitor: Lenovo ThinkVision P27q-30 (`LEN63A2`)
- Laptop connected to the monitor through HDMI
- Separate Windows desktop connected to the same monitor through DisplayPort
- Monitor input selection set to Auto
- Power Display CLI used to switch between HDMI (`0x11`) and DisplayPort (`0x0F`) using DDC/CI VCP `0x60`

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Start PowerToys on the laptop with Power Display enabled.
2. Confirm that `PowerToys.PowerDisplay.Cli.exe list` shows both the internal display and the Lenovo P27q-30.
3. Leave the laptop running while the external desktop uses the monitor through DisplayPort.
4. Reboot the external desktop.
5. Run `PowerToys.PowerDisplay.Cli.exe list` on the laptop.



**Impact**

Scripts relying on the Power Display CLI to change monitor input sources stop working until PowerToys is restarted.




### ✔️ Expected Behavior

**Expected behavior**

Power Display should continue detecting the Lenovo monitor, or automatically rediscover it after the DisplayPort signal changes.



### ❌ Actual Behavior

**Actual behavior**

Power Display lists only the internal laptop display. The Lenovo is missing, and input-switching commands fail because the external monitor is no longer enumerated.

Windows Plug and Play still reports the Lenovo as present, with status `OK`:

`DISPLAY\LEN63A2\...`

The following attempts did not restore Power Display detection:
- `DisplaySwitch.exe /extend`
- `pnputil /scan-devices`
- Windows graphics reset (`Win + Ctrl + Shift + B`)

However, **completely exiting PowerToys and launching it again immediately restores the Lenovo in the Power Display CLI list**, without disconnecting or reconnecting any HDMI cable.

This has been reproduced consistently after multiple reboots of the external desktop.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-28-16-40-28.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34087837/PowerToysReport_2026-10-28-16-40-28.zip)

### Additional Information

**Additional information**

Potential stale monitor enumeration or DDC/CI discovery state after an external display signal transition.

Related issues: #48977 and #47623.

- Transparency / Opacity: Make the window semi-transparent during the move operation (e.g., configurable opacity percentage).

- Blur Effect: Apply an acrylic/mica blur effect to the window background while dragging, matching modern Windows 11 design standards.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When reorganizing workspaces or dragging large windows across multiple monitors, having transparency or a blur effect lets the user see what is underneath the window in real-time, preventing visual obstruction and making the whole movement feel much smoother and more modern.
(I want this option to look good.)

title: File Explorer: keep preview pane width proportional to window size
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add an opt-in setting so the File Explorer preview/details pane keeps a fixed proportion of the window width instead of a fixed pixel width. Today the pane width is stored as a single global value, so resizing the window only changes the file list.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I work with design files, PDFs and images, often switching between a maximized window and a half-screen snap. A wide preview is ideal when maximized, but when the window shrinks, the pane keeps its width and squeezes the file list, so I have to drag the divider every time.

### Supporting information

Windows 7 behaved this way and Outlook still does. Previously requested in #3892 describes the same need.

title: Peek: replace [ComImport] shell interop in FileExplorerHelper (CsWinRT1033)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

After the CsWinRT 2.3.1 / `Microsoft.Windows.SDK.NET.Ref` 10.0.26100.87 upgrade, the CsWinRT AOT analyzer bundled in the SDK ref pack reports **CsWinRT1033** in `src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/Helpers/FileExplorerHelper.cs`:

> The type '...' used in a cast operation is a [ComImport] interface, which is not compatible with CsWinRT objects in AOT scenarios. Consider using the COM generators to define the interface, or manually handling the interface query on the underlying native object.

The helper casts shell objects (`ShellWindows`, `IWebBrowserApp`, `Shell32.IShellFolderViewDual2`) to `[ComImport]` interfaces (`IServiceProvider`, `IShellBrowser`, `IFolderView`, `IShellItemArray`). That relies on built-in COM interop, which isn't trim- or AOT-safe.

The upgrade PR suppresses CsWinRT1033 with a `#pragma` scoped to these helper methods so the version bump can land on its own. This issue tracks removing that suppression by moving the helper to source-generated COM interop (CsWin32 / `[GeneratedComInterface]` / `ComWrappers`) or by querying the interfaces on the native pointer directly.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Peek.UI can't be made trim- or AOT-safe while it relies on these casts. Removing the suppression also keeps the analyzer active for any new `[ComImport]` usage in Peek.UI.

### Supporting information

- Analyzer reference: https://github.com/microsoft/CsWinRT/tree/master/src/Authoring/WinRT.SourceGenerator/AnalyzerReleases.Shipped.md
- Affected file: `src/modules/peek/Peek.UI/Helpers/FileExplorerHelper.cs` (`GetItemsInternal`, `GetItemsFromDesktop`, `GetItemsFromFileExplorer`, `GetShellItemArray`)
- When fixing, remove the `#pragma warning disable/restore CsWinRT1033` and its TODO comment.
- Verify Peek still opens from both the desktop and File Explorer (including tabbed Explorer windows) with single and multiple selections.

title: Command Palette / Window Walker: support space-separated keywords matched in any order
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

When searching in Command Palette (including the Window Walker extension), the query is matched as a single fuzzy string, so the order of the words matters. Space-separated keywords are not treated as independent terms.

I'd like the query to be split on whitespace, with each token fuzzy-matched independently against the item title (and subtitle where applicable). An item should match if all tokens match, regardless of their order.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I often have many windows open with similar titles, for example:

- `Project X - Visual Studio Code`
- `Project Y - Visual Studio Code`
- `Project X - Microsoft Edge`

Typing `code x` or `x code` should find the first window. Today, only the word order that appears in the title works, so I have to remember the exact order of words in the title.

The same applies to other Command Palette items such as apps and commands.

### Supporting information

Expected behavior:

| Query | Title | Match? |
|---|---|---|
| `code project` | Project X - Visual Studio Code | Yes (currently no) |
| `project code` | Project X - Visual Studio Code | Yes |
| `edge y` | Project X - Microsoft Edge | No (y is not present) |

Scoring suggestion: rank results higher when tokens appear in order or contiguously, but don't exclude out-of-order matches.

Related issues (not duplicates):
- #2048 Implement logical search in Windows Indexer plugin (PowerToys Run)
- #25426 Run: prioritize contiguous matches over characters appearing split up
- #47915 Exclude words from result of command palette

title: Build: move all C++ projects from packages.config to PackageReference (tracking)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Move every C++ project (`.vcxproj`) from `packages.config` to `PackageReference`, with versions in `Directory.Packages.props`, a few slices at a time. #51324 is slice 1. Once the last slice merges, the `packages.config` restore path can be retired: `RestorePackagesConfig=true`, the `packages\` folder, and the pipeline's `packages.config` restore.

Today `main` has 93 `packages.config` files. Each of those vcxproj also carries version-pinned `<Import Project="…\packages\<Id>.<Version>\…">` lines and an `EnsureNuGetPackageBuildImports` target, so bumping C++/WinRT or WIL means editing every one of them.

### Scenario when this would be used?

- Bumping a native package becomes a one-line change in `Directory.Packages.props`.
- Every C++ project gets the same version of each package.
- C++ and C# projects restore the same way.

### Supporting information

#### What #51324 (slice 1) does

- Converts the 12 `src/common` projects: COMUtils, Display, logger, notifications, BackgroundActivator, BackgroundActivatorDLL, SettingsAPI, EtwTrace, Themes, updating, UnitTests-CommonLib, UnitTests-CommonUtils.
- Unifies WIL on 1.0.260126.7 in `Directory.Packages.props`.
- No source or pipeline changes. CI already restores both styles (`-restore /p:RestorePackagesConfig=true`), so converted and unconverted projects build side by side.
- All 126 x64 binaries match before and after, compared with `dumpbin` (machine, subsystem, imports, exports, lib members).

#### What's left

These numbers come from running the script below with `-WhatIf` on #51324's branch (`41a6f71580`, 2026-10-27), which leaves 81 `packages.config` files.

**63 projects the script converts as-is**, in suggested slices:

| Slice | Projects | Count |
|---|---|--:|
| Module interfaces | AdvancedPaste, AlwaysOnTop, Awake, CmdNotFound, CmdPal, EnvironmentVariables, FancyZones, Hosts, MeasureTool, MouseWithoutBorders, PowerAccent, PowerDisplay, PowerOCR, ShortcutGuide, Workspaces and ZoomIt `*ModuleInterface`, plus Microsoft.Launcher | 17 |
| Shell extensions and context menus | FileLocksmith (CLI, CLI unit tests, ContextMenu, Ext, Lib), ImageResizer (Ext, ContextMenu, Lib), PowerRename (Ext, Lib, ContextMenu, test app, unit tests), NewPlus (both context menus), Preview Pane (FileExplorerDllExporter, powerpreview), RegistryPreviewExt | 18 |
| Window management | AlwaysOnTop, FancyZones, FancyZonesLib, FancyZones unit tests, Workspaces (Launcher, Lib, Lib unit tests, SnapshotTool, WindowArranger), GrabAndMove, AltWindowCycle | 11 |
| Input | Keyboard Manager (Common, dll, Engine, EngineLibrary, EngineTest, EditorTest), MouseUtils (CursorWrap, MouseButtonLock, MouseHighlighter, MouseJump, MousePointerCrosshairs) | 11 |
| Other | ColorPicker, LightSwitchService and its unit tests, ActionRunner, PowerToys.Update, BugReportTool | 6 |

**17 projects that need a manual change first.** The script skips each of these and prints why:

| Blocker | Projects | What's needed |
|---|---|---|
| **NU1201**: C# projects reference them with a plain `ProjectReference`, and NuGet rejects a native `PackageReference` project there | GPOWrapper (35 C# consumers), PowerToys.Interop (36), CalculatorEngineCommon, FileLocksmithLibInterop, KeyboardManagerEditorLibraryWrapper, PowerAccentKeyboardService, ZoomItSettingsInterop | `ReferenceOutputAssembly=false` plus `CsWinRTInputs` on the C# side, as MeasureToolUI already does. These are C# project changes across dozens of csproj |
| **No central version** for `robmikh.common` 0.0.23-beta | CropAndLock, CropAndLockModuleInterface, ZoomIt | Add a `PackageVersion`. CropAndLockModuleInterface imports the package without listing it |
| **Two projects in one folder** that would share `obj\project.assets.json` | AutoHideCursor + AutoHideCursorWorker; ModuleTemplate + ModuleTemplateCompileTest | Give each project its own `MSBuildProjectExtensionsPath`, or move one into its own folder |
| **Installer** | PowerToysSetupCustomActionsVNext (`WixToolset.DUtil`, `WixToolset.WcaUtil` 5.0.2) | Add central versions; convert it last, after an installer build check |
| **Legacy Keyboard Manager editor** (XAML Islands packages) | KeyboardManagerEditor, KeyboardManagerEditorLibrary | None here; this editor is being removed instead of converted |

**3 `packages.config` files that don't belong to C++ projects:** the root one (MSBuildCache), `.pipelines\packages.config` (pipeline telemetry), and `installer\PowerToysSetupVNext\packages.config` (empty). Look at these before retiring the `packages.config` restore.

#### Why this isn't one PR

- **Size.** About 80 projects is roughly 250 files of project XML. A recent cleanup (#51088) was too big to review and had to be split. Slicing by area keeps each diff readable, and a slice that breaks something can be reverted on its own.
- **17 projects aren't mechanical.** Each blocker above needs a different kind of change and often a different reviewer: C# interop references, a new central package, project layout, the installer, or a module that's being removed. Mixing them into a mechanical conversion would hide the parts that need careful review.
- **There's no flag day.** Both restore styles already work side by side in CI, so slices can merge in any order without breaking the build.
- **Each slice gets checked properly.** Every slice gets the same before/after binary comparison and a build of everything that depends on it. That's practical for one area at a time, not for the whole native tree at once.
- **Fewer conflicts.** Many open PRs touch vcxproj files. Small slices merge quickly and rebase cleanly.

#### Checklist

- [ ] Slice 1: `src/common` (12), #51324
- [ ] Module interfaces (17)
- [ ] Shell extensions and context menus (18)
- [ ] Window management (11)
- [ ] Input (11)
- [ ] Other (6)
- [ ] NU1201 interop projects (7)
- [ ] `robmikh.common` (3)
- [ ] Two-project folders (4)
- [ ] Installer custom actions (1)
- [ ] Legacy Keyboard Manager editor (2): removed instead of converted
- [ ] Retire the `packages.config` restore

#### The conversion script

This script started in #51324. It was taken out of that PR so the repo doesn't carry a one-time migration tool. To use it:

1. Save it as `tools\build\convert-packages-config.ps1`. It finds the repo root from its own location. Don't commit it.
2. Dry run: `.\tools\build\convert-packages-config.ps1 -Path src\modules\fancyzones -WhatIf`. It lists what it would convert and why it skips the rest.
3. Convert: `.\tools\build\convert-packages-config.ps1 -Path src\modules\fancyzones`. Then review the diff, restore with `NUGET_PLUGIN_PATHS` pointing at an empty folder, and build.

For each project it adds versionless `PackageReference` items, removes the pinned `packages\` imports, the `EnsureNuGetPackageBuildImports` target and the `packages.config` item, and deletes `packages.config`. It fails if a package has no central version.

<details><summary>convert-packages-config.ps1</summary>

```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Converts C++ projects (.vcxproj) from packages.config to PackageReference with central package versions.

.DESCRIPTION
For every .vcxproj under -Path that has a sibling packages.config, this script:
  - adds the native PackageReference properties and one versionless PackageReference per package
    (versions come from Directory.Packages.props),
  - removes the version-pinned <Import> lines into the packages folder,
  - removes the EnsureNuGetPackageBuildImports target and the packages.config item (.vcxproj and .vcxproj.filters),
  - removes '<...>packages\<Id>.<Version>\include' include directories for referenced packages
    (the package's own targets already add them),
  - deletes packages.config.

Packages imported by the project, or whose include folder it hard-codes, are added even when
missing from packages.config. The script fails if a package is not listed in Directory.Packages.props,
and reports any remaining hard-coded 'packages\' paths for manual follow-up.

Projects are skipped (with a warning) when a .csproj consumes them through a ProjectReference
without ReferenceOutputAssembly=false, because NuGet then fails restore with NU1201, or when
their folder holds another project that would share obj\project.assets.json.

.PARAMETER Path
One or more folders (searched recursively) or .vcxproj files to convert.

.EXAMPLE
.\tools\build\convert-packages-config.ps1 -Path src\common

.EXAMPLE
.\tools\build\convert-packages-config.ps1 -Path src\modules\fancyzones -WhatIf
#>

[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess = $true)]
param (
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)]
    [string[]]$Path
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$repoRoot = (Resolve-Path "$PSScriptRoot\..\..").Path
[xml]$centralProps = Get-Content (Join-Path $repoRoot 'Directory.Packages.props') -Raw
$centralVersions = @{}
foreach ($pv in $centralProps.Project.ItemGroup.PackageVersion) {
    if ($pv.Include) { $centralVersions[$pv.Include] = $pv.Version }
}

$packageFolderPattern = 'packages\\(?<folder>[A-Za-z][^\\"<>;]*\.\d+(?:\.\d+)+(?:-[^\\"<>;]+)?)\\'

# Package folders are '<Id>.<Version>'; prefer the ids from packages.config since ids can end in digits.
function Resolve-PackageId([string]$folder, $configPackages) {
    foreach ($package in $configPackages) {
        if ($folder -eq "$($package.id).$($package.version)") { return $package.id }
    }

    return [regex]::Match($folder, '^(?<id>.+?)\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:-.+)?$').Groups['id'].Value
}

$nugetBlock = @'
  <PropertyGroup Label="NuGet">
    <!-- Tell NuGet this is PackageReference style -->
    <RestoreProjectStyle>PackageReference</RestoreProjectStyle>
    <!-- Tell NuGet we're a native project -->
    <NuGetTargetMoniker>native,Version=v0.0</NuGetTargetMoniker>
    <!-- Tell NuGet we target Windows (use your existing WindowsTargetPlatformVersion) -->
    <NuGetTargetPlatformIdentifier>Windows</NuGetTargetPlatformIdentifier>
    <NuGetTargetPlatformVersion>$(WindowsTargetPlatformVersion)</NuGetTargetPlatformVersion>
  </PropertyGroup>
'@

function Read-TextFile([string]$file) {
    $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($file)
    $hasByteOrderMark = $bytes.Length -ge 3 -and $bytes[0] -eq 0xEF -and $bytes[1] -eq 0xBB -and $bytes[2] -eq 0xBF
    $text = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($bytes)
    if ($hasByteOrderMark) { $text = $text.Substring(1) }
    $newline = if ($text.Contains("`r`n")) { "`r`n" } else { "`n" }
    return [pscustomobject]@{ Text = $text; HasByteOrderMark = $hasByteOrderMark; Newline = $newline }
}

function Write-TextFile([string]$file, [string]$text, [bool]$hasByteOrderMark) {
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($file, $text, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($hasByteOrderMark)))
}

function Remove-PackagesConfigItem([string]$text) {
    $item = '<None Include="packages\.config"\s*(?:/>|>(?:(?!</None>).)*</None>)'
    $text = [regex]::Replace($text, '(?ms)^[ \t]*<ItemGroup>\s*' + $item + '\s*</ItemGroup>[ \t]*\r?\n', '')
    return [regex]::Replace($text, '(?ms)^[ \t]*' + $item + '[ \t]*\r?\n', '')
}

# NuGet fails restore (NU1201) when a managed project references a native PackageReference project
# and consumes its output, so those projects need C#-side changes before they can move.
$managedReferences = @{}
foreach ($csproj in Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $repoRoot 'src'), (Join-Path $repoRoot 'tools') -Recurse -Filter *.csproj) {
    [xml]$csprojXml = Get-Content $csproj.FullName -Raw
    foreach ($reference in $csprojXml.SelectNodes('//*[local-name()="ProjectReference"]')) {
        $include = $reference.GetAttribute('Include')
        if ($include -notlike '*.vcxproj') { continue }

        $referenceOutputAssembly = $reference.GetAttribute('ReferenceOutputAssembly')
        $metadata = $reference.SelectSingleNode('*[local-name()="ReferenceOutputAssembly"]')
        if ($metadata) { $referenceOutputAssembly = $metadata.InnerText }
        if ($referenceOutputAssembly -eq 'false') { continue }

        $include = $include.Replace('$(RepoRoot)', "$repoRoot\").Replace('$(SolutionDir)', "$repoRoot\")
        $target = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath([System.IO.Path]::Combine($csproj.DirectoryName, $include))
        $managedReferences[$target] = @($managedReferences[$target]) + $csproj.Name | Where-Object { $_ }
    }
}

$projects = foreach ($p in $Path) {
    $resolved = (Resolve-Path $p).Path
    if ((Get-Item $resolved).PSIsContainer) {
        Get-ChildItem -Path $resolved -Recurse -Filter *.vcxproj
    } else {
        Get-Item $resolved
    }
}

$converted = 0
$warnings = @()
foreach ($project in ($projects | Sort-Object FullName -Unique)) {
    $packagesConfig = Join-Path $project.DirectoryName 'packages.config'
    if (-not (Test-Path $packagesConfig)) { continue }

    $relative = $project.FullName.Substring($repoRoot.Length + 1)
    $siblings = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $project.DirectoryName -File | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.vcxproj', '.csproj', '.wixproj' })
    if ($siblings.Count -gt 1) {
        $warnings += "${relative}: skipped, folder has several projects that would share obj\project.assets.json."
        continue
    }

    if ($managedReferences.ContainsKey($project.FullName)) {
        $warnings += "${relative}: skipped, referenced by $(($managedReferences[$project.FullName] | Sort-Object -Unique) -join ', ') (NU1201)."
        continue
    }

    $file = Read-TextFile $project.FullName
    $text = $file.Text
    $nl = $file.Newline

    # Packages from packages.config plus any package the project imports or includes directly.
    $packageIds = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
    [xml]$config = Get-Content $packagesConfig -Raw
    $configPackages = @($config.packages.package)
    foreach ($package in $configPackages) {
        if (-not $packageIds.Contains($package.id)) { $packageIds.Add($package.id) }
        if ($centralVersions.ContainsKey($package.id) -and $centralVersions[$package.id] -ne $package.version) {
            $warnings += "${relative}: $($package.id) moves from $($package.version) to central $($centralVersions[$package.id])."
        }
    }

    $usedPackages = @([regex]::Matches($text, '<Import\s+Project="[^"]*' + $packageFolderPattern)) + @([regex]::Matches($text, $packageFolderPattern + 'include\\?;'))
    foreach ($match in $usedPackages) {
        $id = Resolve-PackageId $match.Groups['folder'].Value $configPackages
        if ($id -and -not $packageIds.Contains($id)) {
            $packageIds.Add($id)
            $warnings += "${relative}: $id is used but missing from packages.config; added."
        }
    }

    $missing = @($packageIds | Where-Object { -not $centralVersions.ContainsKey($_) })
    if ($missing.Count -gt 0) {
        $warnings += "${relative}: skipped, add PackageVersion entries to Directory.Packages.props first: $($missing -join ', ')."
        continue
    }

    # Drop version-pinned imports, the EnsureNuGetPackageBuildImports target and the packages.config item.
    $text = [regex]::Replace($text, '(?ms)^[ \t]*<Import\s+Project="[^"]*' + $packageFolderPattern + '[^"]*"[^>]*/>[ \t]*\r?\n', '')
    $text = [regex]::Replace($text, '(?ms)^[ \t]*<Target Name="EnsureNuGetPackageBuildImports".*?</Target>[ \t]*\r?\n', '')
    $text = Remove-PackagesConfigItem $text

    # Package targets add their own include folders, so hard-coded ones are no longer needed.
    $text = [regex]::Replace($text, '[^;<>"]*' + $packageFolderPattern + 'include\\?;', '')

    $references = ($packageIds | Sort-Object | ForEach-Object { "    <PackageReference Include=""$_"" GeneratePathProperty=""true"" />" }) -join $nl
    $insert = ($nugetBlock -replace "`r?`n", $nl) + $nl + "  <ItemGroup>$nl$references$nl  </ItemGroup>$nl"
    $globals = [regex]::Match($text, '(?ms)^[ \t]*<PropertyGroup Label="Globals">.*?</PropertyGroup>[ \t]*\r?\n')
    if (-not $globals.Success) {
        throw "${relative}: no <PropertyGroup Label=""Globals""> found to anchor the PackageReference items."
    }

    $text = $text.Insert($globals.Index + $globals.Length, $insert)

    foreach ($leftover in [regex]::Matches($text, '[^;<>"]*' + $packageFolderPattern + '[^;<>"]*')) {
        $warnings += "${relative}: hard-coded package path remains: $($leftover.Value.Trim())"
    }

    if ($PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($relative, "Convert $($packageIds -join ', ') to PackageReference")) {
        Write-TextFile $project.FullName $text $file.HasByteOrderMark

        $filters = "$($project.FullName).filters"
        if (Test-Path $filters) {
            $filtersFile = Read-TextFile $filters
            $filtersText = Remove-PackagesConfigItem $filtersFile.Text
            if ($filtersText -ne $filtersFile.Text) {
                Write-TextFile $filters $filtersText $filtersFile.HasByteOrderMark
            }
        }

        Remove-Item $packagesConfig
        Write-Host "Converted $relative ($($packageIds -join ', '))"
        $converted++
    }
}

foreach ($warning in $warnings) {
    Write-Warning $warning
}

Write-Host "Converted $converted project(s)."
```

</details>

title: CmdPal Dock: page popup opened from an extension band is offset to the left and clipped at the screen edge
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version
0.102.2933.0 (Command Palette 0.13.12934.0)

### Installation method
Per-user installer (PowerToys (Preview), %LOCALAPPDATA%\PowerToys)

### Area(s) with issue?
Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce
1. Single monitor, 1920×1200, Dock enabled.
2. Pin a band from a third-party extension: each button is a ListItem inside a WrappedDockItem, and its command is a ContentPage (markdown content).
3. Click a button of that band.
4. Repeat with Dock size Compact, then Default.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior
The page popup opens anchored to the clicked button and stays fully on screen.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
The popup opens to the left of the button and runs past the left edge of the screen, so its left part is cut off. Same with Compact and Default Dock sizes. The Command Palette logs show nothing relevant (only "Backdrop clip is unavailable").

### Additional Information

title: Persistent Screen Annotations Anchored to UI Elements
body: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement I would like to propose a new feature for Microsoft PowerToys that allows users to draw persistent annotations on applications and webpages. The idea is to let users draw a rectangle, box, arrow, highlight, or other simple markup around a specific word, field, button, section, or UI element and optionally add a small note. The important part is that the annotation should remain associated with the original screen/UI element, rather than simply remaining at a fixed position on the screen. For example, suppose I am reviewing a long web-based form containing 30–50 fields. I notice an incorrect word in one of the fields and draw a red rectangle around it. I may also add a small note explaining what is wrong. I then continue scrolling down through the form to review other fields. When I scroll back up, the annotation should still be correctly positioned over the original word or field. In other words, the annotation should remain persistent and context-aware, so that scrolling through a long application does not cause the annotation to become detached from the item that was originally marked. This feature would be useful not only for webpages but also for Windows applications, software interfaces, dashboards, data-entry systems, forms, and other applications where users need to inspect and review information. **_I am specifically proposing this as a PowerToys feature, not as a browser extension._** ### Scenario when this would be used? A common use case is reviewing a large form or data-entry application. For example: - I open a form containing many fields. - I find an incorrect word or piece of information. - I draw a red box around that specific item using PowerToys. - I add a short note such as "Incorrect — should be X." - I scroll down and continue reviewing the remaining fields. - I may scroll through several screens of content. - When I return to the original location, the annotation is still correctly positioned over the item I marked. This could be useful for proofreading, QA testing, data verification, UI review, accessibility review, software testing, documentation review, and checking large amounts of information. The main problem with ordinary screen-annotation tools is that the annotation is often tied to a screen coordinate or visual overlay. When the underlying content moves because of scrolling, resizing, dynamic loading, or other changes, the annotation can become separated from the item it was intended to identify. A PowerToys implementation could potentially provide a more persistent annotation experience by associating the annotation with the underlying UI elemen t or content whenever technically possible. ### Supporting information The goal is not to create a browser-specific annotation tool or browser extension. I am suggesting a general-purpose PowerToys utility for persistent on-screen annotations that could work across Windows applications. For applications where the underlying UI structure can be detected, an annotation could potentially be associated with an identifiable UI element, control, text location, or other accessible object. Where that is not technically possible, the feature could fall back to positional screen coordinates. The key behavior I am looking for is: "Mark something → scroll away → scroll back → the marking is still attached to the thing I originally marked." For example, if I draw a red rectangle around a particular field in a long form, scrolling should move the rectangle together with that field rather than leaving the rectangle behind at its previous screen position. This would make PowerToys useful not only for taking quick screen annotations, but also for reviewing, inspecting, testing, and marking up dynamic Windows interfaces. I understand that implementing this reliably across every application may have technical limitations. Even a solution that supports UI-element anchoring where Windows accessibility/UI information is available, with a positional fallback for other applications, would be extremely useful.

title: Marking on Sites
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like a feature that allows users to draw annotations—such as rectangles, boxes, arrows, highlights, or notes—directly on specific words, fields, or UI elements of a webpage.

The key requirement is that these annotations should remain anchored to the original content or UI element, rather than being tied to a fixed screen/viewport position.

For example, if I draw a red rectangle around an incorrect word in a long Google Form and add a correction note, the rectangle and note should remain associated with that exact word or field even when I scroll far down the page and later scroll back up.

The annotation should not move, drift, or become misaligned simply because the webpage has been scrolled.

Ideally, this should work across different websites and web applications, including forms, dashboards, internal company software, data-entry systems, and other long, scrollable interfaces.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would be particularly useful when reviewing large forms or web applications containing many fields. For example, a user may need to verify 30–50 fields and identify incorrect information, missing data, formatting problems, or other issues.

The user could draw a box around an incorrect word or field, add a small note explaining the correction, and then continue reviewing the rest of the page. As they scroll through the application, all previous annotations should remain attached to the corresponding content.

This would make it much easier to perform detailed data checking, proofreading, QA testing, content review, and user-interface review without losing track of previously identified issues.


### Supporting information

Many browser-based annotation tools allow users to draw boxes, highlights, or notes on webpages, but the annotations can behave like overlays positioned relative to the viewport or rendered page coordinates. As a result, they can become misaligned or difficult to associate with the original content when the page changes, scrolls, dynamically loads content, or reflows.

The desired behavior is closer to content-aware or DOM-anchored annotations: an annotation should be associated with the underlying word, field, DOM element, or other identifiable piece of content. If the user scrolls away and returns, the annotation should still appear at the correct location.

This would be especially valuable for QA, proofreading, data verification, form review, accessibility review, and testing complex web applications.

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

### PowerToys version
0.102.2933 (same version on both machines)

### Summary
Two Windows PCs on the same home network cannot pair with Mouse Without Borders. The secondary machine fails after about 24 seconds with "Could not load or update pairing. Try again." The primary machine's device layout shows the secondary with a red (Error) border, and Refresh connections cycles Negotiation (blue) → Connecting (orange) → Error (red).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Enable Mouse Without Borders on both PCs (same version 0.102.2933).
2. On the primary PC (CyberStore), generate a security key.
3. On the secondary PC (JuliaLeon), enter the security key and the primary's hostname (CyberStore) and click Connect.

- Both PCs on the same private Wi-Fi network and subnet, same gateway.
- Network profile set to Private on both.
- MouseWithoutBorders allowed through Windows Firewall (Private and Public) on both; firewall rule deleted and recreated by PowerToys.
- Test with Windows Firewall completely disabled on the primary: same error.
- Exact hostname and security key (tested exact case and uppercase); same key shown on both machines; did not regenerate the key mid-process.
- IP address mapping on both machines.
- PowerToys run as administrator on both.
- No third-party antivirus; VPN disconnected during tests.

The two PCs should pair, and the mouse cursor should move between the two screens. The secondary PC (JuliaLeon) should appear as connected in the device layout.

The pairing never completes. The secondary PC fails after about 24 seconds with "Could not load or update pairing. Try again." and its device layout stays empty.
