title: [FancyZones] App zone history of a Microsoft Store app is lost after each update of the app
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.102.2933.0 - Stable

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

1. Turn on "Move newly created windows to their last known zone".
2. Snap the new Outlook (`olk.exe`) to a zone and close it.
3. Let Outlook update itself, then open it.

On 22 October 2026 Outlook updated itself at 10:16 and its process path changed from `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.OutlookForWindows_1.2026.1001.200_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\olk.exe` to the same path with `1.2026.1013.100`. When it opened again, the log had `Get olk.exe zone history` and no `App zone history found`.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

After an update the app opens in the zone it had before.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

FancyZones finds no history for the new version and leaves the window where the app puts it. `app-zone-history.json` held entries for 9 versions of Outlook and 8 versions of Teams (`ms-teams.exe`).

### Additional Information

From the code on main: `AppZoneHistory` keys its entries by the full process path. The path of a packaged app has the package version in its folder name, so each update gives the app a new key. #17027 (closed) shows the same for Windows Terminal: the reporter's history held entries for versions 1.4, 1.8 and 1.12.

A fix with unit tests is in commit [f99a2865d](https://github.com/vdvoorder/PowerToys/commit/f99a2865d10a2a50205c98ccc99bf811952c898e) on my fork, based on main at `a5e83e5e2`:

- `AppZoneHistory` keys a path under `WindowsApps` by the package family name instead of the full package folder name: `WindowsApps\Microsoft.OutlookForWindows_8wekyb3d8bbwe\olk.exe`. Other paths don't change.
- When the file holds several versions of one app, the history of the newest version is loaded. The next save writes one entry per packaged app.
- An older FancyZones that reads the saved file doesn't find these entries, so a downgrade loses the history of packaged apps once.
- #41656 also changes the key, by adding the `AppUserModel_ID` to the path. The two changes touch the same functions.
- Two new tests in `AppZoneHistoryUnitTests`: `AppHistoryKeyIgnoresPackageVersion` and `AppZoneHistoryParseKeepsNewestPackageVersion`. With the change, the FancyZones unit tests (Release x64, each test class in its own `vstest.console.exe` process) give 298 of 299 passed and 0 failed; `WindowProcessingUnitTests::NonRootWindow` had no result after a crash of `vstest.console.exe`, as on main without the change. The build has 0 warnings.

### Other Software

Outlook for Windows (the new Outlook), versions 1.2026.1001.200 and 1.2026.1013.100; Microsoft Teams (`ms-teams.exe`).

title: [FancyZones] Laptop panel without an active display device gets its display name as id and keeps it after the lid opens
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Stable

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a laptop on a dock with one external monitor, with a custom layout on the laptop panel.
2. Close the lid, so the external monitor is the only active display.
3. Unplug the dock while the lid stays closed.
4. Open the lid later.

Observed twice: on 7 October 2026 after the external monitor was removed, and on 11 October 2026 after the dock was unplugged, both with the lid closed. Each time FancyZones identified the monitors again after a display or work area change, tried 100 times without finding a display device for `\\.\DISPLAY1`, and then logged `Initialize layout on` with the work area id `\\.\DISPLAY1`. On 11 October the lid opened two and a half hours later, and FancyZones logged no display change then or later.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The laptop panel keeps its monitor id and its layout, and the windows stay in its zones.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

FancyZones creates the work area again with the display name `\\.\DISPLAY1` as id. `applied-layouts.json` had the default layout (priority grid, 3 zones) for that id, so the zoned windows moved to its zones. After the lid opened the work area kept the display name as id, and kept the default layout until I applied my layout to it by hand.

### Additional Information

From the code on main:

- `MonitorUtils::IdentifyMonitors` retries 100 times when a display has no active display device and then gives it its display name as id. The retries came with #27005 for #19738, whose text says "This change doesn't solve the layout reset problem completely".
- `FancyZones::UpdateWorkAreas` then creates the work area with that id, and `WorkArea::InitLayout` applies the layout saved for it, or the default layout.
- FancyZones identifies the monitors only after a display or work area change. Opening the lid sent none here, so nothing corrected the id. In #14857 a maintainer found the same: Windows sends no message when a laptop lid is closed or a monitor is turned off.

A fix with unit tests is in commit [72ffbb665](https://github.com/vdvoorder/PowerToys/commit/72ffbb665f1c9a8992c45a7a9510a5ec16c84e8d) on my fork, based on main at `a5e83e5e2`:

- A display without display device keeps the device id and the serial number of the work area that has the same monitor handle and the same work area rectangle, when the number of monitors didn't change.
- A timer checks once a second whether such a display has a display device again, and then updates the work areas once.
- With the fix in my own build, on 12 October 2026 the panel was 62 seconds without display device after the lid opened from standby. FancyZones kept the device id, logged `A display has a display device again or is gone, update the work areas`, and didn't create the work area again.
- Not covered: FancyZones starting while the display has no display device; a display whose monitor handle or work area rectangle changed, which gets the display name until the timer sees the display device; two monitors with the same handle value and the same work area rectangle, which it can't tell apart.
- The timer runs as long as a display stays without display device.
- The new class `MonitorIdentificationUnitTests` has 37 tests of the functions that pick the ids and the displays to check. The timer itself has no unit test. With the change, the FancyZones unit tests (Release x64, each test class in its own `vstest.console.exe` process) give 333 of 334 passed and 0 failed; `WindowProcessingUnitTests::NonRootWindow` had no result after a crash of `vstest.console.exe`, as on main without the change. The build has 0 warnings.

### Other Software

No other software is involved.

title: [FancyZones] Closed windows stay in the work area's window list and are snapped again after a layout or display change
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Stable

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

I didn't run these steps. They follow from the code.

1. Turn on "During zone layout changes, windows assigned to a zone will match new size/positions".
2. Snap a window to the first zone and close it.
3. Apply another layout to that monitor.

By the code, FancyZones then logs this per closed window, after `Initialize layout on <work area>`:

```
[error] SetWindowPlacement failed, Invalid window handle.
[error] SetWindowPlacement failed, Invalid window handle.
[error] Failed to stamp window Invalid window handle.
```

The log of normal use has:

- On 14 September 2026, 11 `Initialize layout on` lines within 4 minutes were each followed by 55 of these groups.
- On 17 September the number rose from 16 to 26 per such line.
- 1340 groups in total come within a minute after such a line or a display change, on 10 days (13 September to 10 October 2026).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

A closed window leaves the window list of its work area.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

A closed window stays in the list and is snapped again after a layout or display change, which logs three errors. I observed no other effect.

### Additional Information

From the code on main:

- `WorkArea::UpdateWindowPositions` calls `Snap(window, zones, true)` for every entry of `LayoutAssignedWindows`. `FancyZones::RefreshLayouts` and `FancyZones::UpdateWorkAreas` call it when the setting for that event moves windows.
- For a closed window, `Snap` assigns the handle to its zones again. `SizeWindowToRect` and `StampZoneIndexProperty` log the errors. The entry stays.
- The handler of `WM_PRIV_WINDOWDESTROYED` only ends a drag. `LayoutAssignedWindows::CycleWindows` removes a closed window when window switching reaches it. No other code does before the work areas are created again.

A fix with unit tests is in commit [23eb0d219](https://github.com/vdvoorder/PowerToys/commit/23eb0d219ea01b5279b19c5d924e9e5c58934913) on my fork, based on main at `a5e83e5e2`:

- `UpdateWindowPositions` removes an entry from the list when `IsWindow` is false for it, and continues with the next one.
- It doesn't change the handler for a destroyed window, `CycleWindows`, or the app zone history.
- A closed window leaves the list in a pass of `UpdateWindowPositions`, not at the moment it's closed. When Windows has given the handle value to a new window, that window is snapped to the zones of the closed one, as before.
- The new class `WorkAreaZonedWindowUnitTests` has four tests. Three fail without the change; the fourth checks behaviour that doesn't change. With the change, the FancyZones unit tests (Release x64, each test class in its own `vstest.console.exe` process) give 300 of 301 passed and 0 failed; `WindowProcessingUnitTests::NonRootWindow` had no result after a crash of `vstest.console.exe`, as on main without the change. The build has 0 warnings.

### Other Software

No other software is involved.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Open a dialog box to allow the shortcuts of the currently selected application to be saved to a (human readable) file, such as .txt or .csv; possibly triggered by a right click on the application icon.

title: FancyZones: "Move newly created windows to the current active monitor" re-shows a window the owning app has already hidden
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 (also present in earlier versions)

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

1. Two or more monitors. FancyZones enabled, "Move newly created windows to the current active monitor" on.
2. Put the mouse cursor on a non-primary monitor.
3. Run a GUI-subsystem program that calls `AllocConsole()` and then immediately `ShowWindow(GetConsoleWindow(), SW_HIDE)`. A 30-line one, with build instructions and a window-event recorder, is here: https://github.com/Kjm520/google-drive-fs-terminal-bug/tree/main/for-powertoys

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Conhost shows the console window, the app hides it a few milliseconds later, and it stays hidden. If FancyZones moves the window to the active monitor, the move should preserve the window's visibility state, or skip windows that are not visible when the move runs.


### ❌ Actual Behavior

About 10 to 20 ms after conhost's first show, FancyZones moves the window to the cursor's monitor and shows it again, undoing the app's hide. Event sequence from a SetWinEventHook recorder: `SHOW`, `HIDE`, `LOCATION` (moved one monitor), `SHOW`.


### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

Measured (full log in the repo, [supporting/console-window-events-2026-10-24.log](https://github.com/Kjm520/google-drive-fs-terminal-bug/blob/main/supporting/console-window-events-2026-10-24.log)):
- option on, cursor on a non-primary monitor: re-shown in every run (12 of 12 with Google Drive, all harness runs)
- option off: stays hidden, 5 of 5
- option on, app in FancyZones' excluded apps: stays hidden, 5 of 5
- single monitor: stays hidden, 8 of 8
- app hides 150 or 400 ms after AllocConsole, i.e. after the move: stays hidden, 6 of 6

Real-world impact: Google Drive for desktop (GoogleDriveFS.exe) allocates a console for its logger and hides it this way (how this was encountered originally). With the option on, every Drive child restart leaves a black console window titled with the exe path on the cursor's monitor; closing it kills Drive's child process, and seven closes take Drive down. Steps with Drive, if installed: option on, cursor on a non-primary monitor, end the GoogleDriveFS.exe process whose command line contains `--crash_handler_token`; the parent restarts it and the window appears. With GoogleDriveFS.exe in FancyZones' excluded apps it does not. Full analysis: https://github.com/Kjm520/google-drive-fs-terminal-bug

Related: #32957 asks for per-app exceptions to this option; this is a different problem (visibility not preserved), though exclusion is the current workaround for both.

### Other Software

Google Drive for desktop 132.0.0.0 (affected app). Not required to reproduce.

title: Paste and Rename File
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like to request a new **"Paste and Rename"** feature for Windows File Explorer, integrated through Microsoft PowerToys.

Currently, when copying files to a destination where files with the same names already exist, Windows provides options such as Replace and Compare. I suggest adding another option called **"Paste and Rename"**, allowing users to paste files with customized new names while keeping the existing files completely untouched.

**Requested functionality:**

1. **Paste and Rename:** When a filename conflict occurs, provide an option to rename the incoming file before pasting it.
2. **Rename Dialog:** Open a small window displaying the original filename, proposed new filename, and editable name field.
3. **Batch Renaming:** Support renaming multiple files during a single copy/paste operation.
4. **Prefix and Suffix:** Allow users to add custom text at the beginning or end of filenames, either to all selected files at once or individually.
5. **Advanced Naming Options:** Support automatic date/time, sequential numbering, and customizable filename patterns.
6. **Live Preview:** Show the final filenames before confirming the paste operation.
7. **File Extension Protection:** Preserve extensions such as .js, .html, .css, and .json automatically.
8. **Conflict Validation:** Prevent accidental overwriting if the newly entered filename also exists.
9. **Keep Both Files:** Ensure the existing files remain completely unchanged.

This could be integrated into the existing Windows file conflict dialog or provided through a PowerToys File Explorer extension.

Although PowerToys already provides PowerRename, this feature would allow users to rename files **during the paste operation**, rather than renaming files afterward.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This feature would be extremely useful for developers, IT professionals, designers, and anyone who frequently copies files into folders containing existing files.

**Example: Software development backups**

Suppose I am working on a Node.js project and want to back up my `server.js` file before implementing a new feature.

I have a folder called `BackupFiles` that already contains a file named `server.js`.

When I copy another `server.js` into this folder, instead of replacing the existing file, I want to select **"Paste and Rename"** and enter a meaningful backup filename.

**Example:**

- Original filename: `server.js`
- Destination folder: `BackupFiles`
- New filename: `241026-before-archive-feature-server.js`

Both files would remain available without replacing or modifying the previous backup.

**Batch example:**

When copying multiple development files such as `server.js`, `app.js`, and `style.css`, I could apply the prefix `241026-before-update-` to all incoming files in one operation.

This would help developers maintain organized, descriptive backups before making changes, reduce the risk of accidental overwriting, and eliminate unnecessary manual renaming.

### Supporting information

**Suggested user interface and workflow:**

1. User copies one or more files into a destination folder.
2. Windows detects that files with the same names already exist.
3. The conflict dialog displays an additional option: **"Paste and Rename".**
4. Selecting this option opens a compact rename window with the original filenames and editable destination filenames.
5. Users can rename files individually or apply common naming rules to multiple files.

**Suggested advanced options:**

- Add Prefix: `241026-before-update-`
- Add Suffix: `-backup`
- Insert current date/time automatically.
- Add sequential numbers when multiple files have the same name.
- Apply renaming to all conflicting files or selected files only.
- Preview filenames before confirming.
- Remember the last-used naming pattern for future operations.

**Important:** This feature should not affect or replace the existing Windows copy/paste functionality. It should simply provide another convenient option when filename conflicts occur.

**Why this belongs in PowerToys:**

PowerToys already offers PowerRename for advanced filename management. Extending this capability to the copy/paste conflict workflow would make it even more useful.

The main difference is that users could customize incoming filenames **before the files are pasted**, eliminating an additional renaming step.

I believe this would be a valuable productivity improvement for Windows users, especially software developers who frequently create versioned backups of their project files.

title: [Workspaces] Cannot uncheck "Launch as administrator" for a captured Win32 app when the checkbox is disabled
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.102.2933

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Workspaces

### Steps to reproduce

The following was observed with UnrealGameSync, a regular Win32 EXE whose embedded manifest declares `<requestedExecutionLevel level="asInvoker" />`.

1. Run UnrealGameSync with administrator privileges.
2. Run PowerToys as administrator and capture a workspace containing the UnrealGameSync window.
3. Open the application's settings in the workspace editor.
4. Try to clear "Launch as administrator" so the workspace launches the application normally.

The checkbox is checked and disabled, so it cannot be cleared. The application header also displays "Administrator".

The saved entry contains:

```json
{
  "application": "UnrealGameSync",
  "is-elevated": true,
  "can-launch-elevated": false
}
```

Screenshot to attach: `ugs-admin-checkbox.png` supplied alongside this draft.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

An already checked "Launch as administrator" option should be clearable, even if PowerToys cannot determine the application's elevation capability.

For ordinary Win32 EXEs, failure to find the application in the Windows application list should not prevent the user from selecting normal launch in the editor.

The user should be able to make this change through the editor without manually editing `workspaces.json`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The checkbox is checked but disabled. The workspace retains `is-elevated: true`, and the editor provides no way to turn it off.

This also makes the new signature confirmation particularly disruptive: when Windows cannot establish signature trust for an application configured to launch as administrator, Workspaces asks for confirmation on each launch. Users affected by this disabled checkbox cannot choose normal launch through the editor to avoid that unnecessary elevation request.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[ugs-admin-checkbox.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e14c8d48-a757-4901-936f-f93f3f658a8a)

### Additional Information

- Windows 10 Pro 22H2, build 19045.6456.
- PowerToys is configured to always run as administrator.
- UAC is disabled on this machine (`EnableLUA=0`). Both Explorer and UnrealGameSync were confirmed to hold elevated tokens.
- UnrealGameSync's embedded execution level is `asInvoker`; the inspected per-user and machine-wide compatibility-layer registry entries did not contain a matching override for it.
- UnrealGameSync was not found in this machine's `shell:AppsFolder` enumeration.

### Other Software

_No response_

body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Please add an option to preserve Awake's behaviour from before #49388.

With that change, Awake allows displays to turn off while Windows is locked, even when "Keep screen on" is enabled. I understand why some users prefer this, but I'd like to be able to choose.

A setting such as "Allow displays to turn off while locked" would cover both preferences. Disabling it should keep "Keep screen on" effective while locked, including after resuming from hibernation.

If adding an option needs more work, please consider reverting the change until that option is available.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I use Awake for long-running development tasks, including Codex, Claude and GitHub Copilot sessions. I lock Windows when I step away and expect Awake to keep doing what I selected.

My setup is a Windows 11 Modern Standby laptop connected to a USB-C dock with two external monitors. After resuming from hibernation and leaving Windows locked, the monitors turn off when the lock-screen timeout expires and the laptop's power LED starts flashing.

That leaves me unsure whether my development tasks are still running. Keeping the displays on is the behaviour I selected, and I'd like to retain it without downgrading PowerToys or changing my Windows power plan.

### Supporting information

Related change: #49388
Original feature request: #49386

I haven't confirmed that background tasks actually stop. In an earlier SleepStudy, the screen-off interval showed PowerToys.Awak maintaining a power request for essentially the entire interval, with no separate Sleep segment recorded.

This request is specifically about making the locked-screen display behaviour configurable. Please also clarify in the UI and documentation what Awake guarantees while Windows is locked, particularly on Modern Standby systems.

title: Add CLI trigger argument to Window Hopper for automation and custom hot corners
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Provide a command-line interface (CLI) execution argument for `PowerToys.WindowHopper.exe` (or a dedicated `.CLI.exe` wrapper) that programmatically triggers the Window Hopper UI overlay. 

Crucially, when invoked via this CLI flag, the overlay behavior should switch to **persistent execution mode**. Instead of closing immediately when a shortcut modifier key is released, the Window Hopper UI grid should remain open on the screen until the user explicitly clicks a window to switch to it, or presses `Esc` to cancel. This would closely mirror the persistent behavior of Windows Task View (`Win + Tab`) or macOS App Exposé.

*   **CLI Trigger Support:** Running a command like `PowerToys.WindowHopper.exe --trigger` (or similar syntax) cleanly activates the utility overlay from any environment (PowerShell, CMD, third-party automation tools).
*   **Persistent Window Overlay:** The overlay window pops up and remains stuck to the screen without requiring the user to mock or hold down a hardware modifier key like `Alt`.
*   **Dismiss on Select or Escape:** The UI automatically closes and yields focus once an app instance is clicked or the action is canceled via keyboard input.

#### Why this is distinct from tracking Issue #1305 (Native Hot Corners)
Instead of requesting a brand-new, native PowerToys Hot Corners module—which has historically been closed as a duplicate—this request is an incremental, developer-focused API enhancement to an *existing* feature (

### Scenario when this would be used?

This functionality is highly important for power users looking to achieve native-feeling workflow automations and multi-window management gestures. 

Specifically, this feature allows users to integrate PowerToys with third-party automation software—such as the open-source **[HotCornersWin](https://github.com/flexits/HotCornersWin)** utility—to cleanly emulate macOS's popular **App Exposé** feature. 

When a user slams their mouse cursor into a chosen corner of the screen, the macro tool would fire the CLI command, presenting all open windows of the active application cleanly in a grid that stays on screen until a selection is made. Currently, simulating this with raw keyboard input APIs (`SendKeys` or C# `keybd_event` / `SendInput` hooks) in scripting tools like PowerShell is highly fragile, as the simulated keypress releases `Alt` almost immediately, making it impossible to comfortably browse or choose windows programmatically.

### Supporting information

*   Providing a CLI argument pattern aligns directly with existing PowerToys architectural standards, similar to hooks available in utilities like *Advanced Paste* or *FancyZones*.
*   Third-party utilities like `HotCornersWin` natively accept executable paths and arguments via the Windows Run dialog structure, making a simple CLI argument the absolute most universally compatible and elegant way to build out this automation loop.

title: [FancyZones] Per-Monitor Layout Cycling via Mouse Wheel & Monitor-Specific Layout Management
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

We would like to request two main enhancements for FancyZones regarding multi-monitor setups and layout control:

Per-Monitor Layout Pools & Mouse Wheel Cycling: Allow users to create and assign specific subsets of layouts to an individual monitor (e.g., 3 specific custom layouts for Monitor 2, instead of sharing global layouts across all screens). While dragging a window (or while holding the activation key like Shift), scrolling the mouse wheel up or down should cycle only through the layouts scoped to the specific monitor where the window/cursor currently resides.

Smart Layout-Switching Options: When switching layouts, provide an option to either automatically reorganize existing open windows into the new zones or keep them as they are without forcing an automatic rearrangement.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would be used constantly by multi-monitor users who have displays with different sizes, resolutions, or orientations (such as combining a main horizontal monitor with a vertical/portrait secondary monitor).

For instance, a user might want a simple 2-zone split on their primary screen, but want quick access to 3 different productivity layouts on their secondary screen while coding or managing chats. Being able to hover a window over that secondary screen, scroll the mouse wheel, and instantly cycle only through that monitor's dedicated layouts—without affecting the rest of the setup—would make the workflow incredibly fast and seamless.

### Supporting information

title: [Mouse Without Borders] Option to leave the cursor where it left the screen instead of moving it to the center / top-center
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

When the cursor leaves a machine for another one, Mouse Without Borders moves the local cursor to one of two hard-coded points:

- the center of the primary screen, when "Hide mouse at the screen's edge" is off;
- the top-center of the primary screen (4 px from the top), when it is on.

See `Common.HideMouseCursor`:
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/Common.cs#L1485

Please add a third choice: leave the cursor where it left the screen, i.e. at the exit edge at the same height. If the cursor has to be moved away from the edge for input tracking, park it a few pixels inside the exit edge.

This could be a "Cursor position on the inactive machine" dropdown with "Screen center", "Top edge (current 'Hide mouse at the screen's edge')" and "Where it left the screen".

### Scenario when this would be used?

Two PCs share one ultrawide monitor in Picture-by-Picture mode: each PC shows on its own half, and both halves are visible at the same time. The halves are arranged in one row in the Mouse Without Borders layout.

When I move to the other PC, the cursor of the PC I left jumps to the middle of its half and stays there, in plain view, while I work on the other half. With "Hide mouse at the screen's edge" on, it jumps to the top-center instead and still leaves a visible artifact (see #47873).

On a physical two-screen setup the cursor that "went to the other screen" stays at the border. Keeping it at the exit edge would look the same here and would not distract from the active half.

### Supporting information

- PowerToys 0.102.2933.0, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, PowerToys running elevated, Mouse Without Borders as a service.
- Settings: devices in a single row, Move mouse relatively off, Wrap mouse on.
- Related: #47873 (top-center parking leaves a visible artifact), #26338 (cursor goes to the top of the screen instead of hiding; a comment there suggests bottom-center as less visible).

title: Add a Native Offline Translate Command Using Existing Windows/Office Translation Models
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like PowerToys to provide a system-wide Translate command that uses existing on-device translation capabilities available in Windows or Microsoft Office, where supported.

This request is not for another LLM provider or an integration with Ollama, Foundry Local, or a cloud translation API with MS Copilot or Github Copilot. 

The goal is to reuse existing lightweight translation models that come as ONNX or a supported Windows/Office translation API, rather than requiring users to download, configure, or maintain a separate model runtime infrastructure and authentication. 

### Scenario when this would be used?

**Proposed workflow**

1. As CLI application to pass a file from Notepad, as extension or invocation in VS Code, Visual Studio, or pick a file and pass Microsoft Word or Excel document directly.
2. Quick launch short cut for keyboard combination (for example, Win+Shift+T or customisable).
3. Set Default language target or provide drop down as available from the Window system languages so its easy to pick which is the destination language without much configuration, if there is only 1 available it should go to that if not it should provide neat drop down before it runs 

### Supporting information

**Key requirements**

**Offline operation:** Translation should work without an internet connection once the necessary language resources are available locally.
**System-wide availability as provided for that device:** Support text in common Windows applications, including text editors, IDEs, and Office applications through language setup done during device setup, so use always has Work Language and Client Language profile available for translate 
**No external translation services:** In local-only mode, selected text must not be sent to cloud APIs.
**No separate model runtime:** Prefer translation capabilities already provided by Windows or Office, without requiring users to install a third-party inference runtime.
**Language selection:** Allow users to choose source and target languages, with automatic source-language detection where supported.
**Native Windows experience:** Integrate with PowerToys keyboard shortcuts, popups, and existing utilities where practical.

title: Autorun task is deleted and recreated with hardcoded PT03S delay on every elevated launch, making the tray icon startup race unworkaroundable
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

General

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable "Run at startup" and "Always run as administrator" in PowerToys settings (so the runner launches elevated via the `\PowerToys\Autorun for <username>` scheduled task).
2. In Task Scheduler, edit the logon trigger delay of that task from 3 seconds to 1 minute, to work around the tray icon / taskbar initialization race at logon (cf. #35250).
3. Reboot.
4. Inspect the task trigger again: the delay has been silently reset to `PT3S`, and the tray icon intermittently fails to appear after logon.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Either the user-customized trigger delay is preserved, or there is a supported way to work around the taskbar-not-ready race at logon.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

On every elevated launch, the runner deletes and recreates the autorun task with a hardcoded 3-second delay, silently discarding any user customization. On my machine this intermittently results in PowerToys starting before the taskbar is ready: the process runs fine (modules work, hotkeys work), but the tray icon fails to register. Verified on every reboot in v0.100.2.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-22-00-15-20.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33777697/PowerToysReport_2026-10-22-00-15-20.zip)

### Additional Information

### Root cause (source analysis, tag v0.100.2)

1. `src/runner/general_settings.cpp` → `apply_general_settings()` (called from `WinMain` on **every** launch). When `startup` is true and the process is elevated, the existing task is **always deleted and recreated** — the "task exists, just enable it" branch in the create helper is effectively unreachable in this flow:

```cpp
if (startup)
{
    if (is_process_elevated())
    {
        delete_auto_start_task_for_this_user();
        create_auto_start_task_for_this_user(run_as_elevated);
    }
```

2. `src/runner/auto_start_helper.cpp` → `create_auto_start_task_for_this_user()` hardcodes the delay:

```cpp
// Timing issues may make explorer not be started when the task runs.
// Add a little delay to mitigate this.
hr = pLogonTrigger->put_Delay(_bstr_t(L"PT03S"));
```

Note the irony: the 3-second delay exists precisely to mitigate the explorer-not-ready race, but it is evidently not enough on all systems — and because the task is recreated on every launch, users cannot increase it themselves. The reset also wipes `LastRunTime` bookkeeping on every launch, making the task look like it "never ran" in Task Scheduler.

### Possible directions

- Skip delete+create when the existing task already points to the current executable with the expected principal (the enable-only branch already exists but is unreachable);
- and/or expose the trigger delay as a user setting;
- and/or increase the default delay.

### Other Software

- OS: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, version 26H2 (OS Build 26300.9711), all Windows updates installed
- Reproduces on every reboot since at least v0.100.2

title: Always On Top: border window covers the whole primary monitor and blocks all mouse input
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

0.101.2362.0 (not yet tested on v0.102.2933.0, released 2026-10-21)

### Utility with the bug

Always On Top

### Steps to reproduce

1. Two-monitor setup on Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300.
2. Accidentally pressed Win+Ctrl+T (intending Ctrl+T).

The specific window that got pinned is not known.

### ✔️ Expected behavior

The pinned-window border is drawn around the pinned window only and never intercepts mouse input.

### ❌ Actual behavior

A red border appeared around the entire primary monitor. Every click anywhere on that monitor played the Windows error sound and did nothing; the primary monitor was unusable with the mouse. The second monitor kept working normally.

Inspecting top-level windows showed the culprit:

- Process: `PowerToys.AlwaysOnTop.exe`
- Window class: `AlwaysOnTop_Border`, no title
- Rect: `-15,-15`, `2355x1470` (the full primary monitor plus the 15 px frame thickness)
- Extended style: `0x80088` (WS_EX_LAYERED | WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW | WS_EX_TOPMOST), without `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT`, so the topmost overlay was not click-through and swallowed all input.

Always On Top settings were defaults: frame enabled, thickness 15, accent color, opacity 100, sound enabled, round corners enabled.

### Workaround

Ending `PowerToys.AlwaysOnTop.exe` in Task Manager removed the border and restored input immediately.

### Other Software

Windows 11 Home 10.0.26300, dual monitors.

Introduce a PowerToys utility that allows users to assign a customizable keyboard shortcut to toggle Windows Do Not Disturb mode on or off.

When activated, a Windows toast notification should appear indicating the new state:

- 🔔 Do Not Disturb Disabled

### Scenario when this would be used?

```
Settings → System → Notifications
Quick Settings panel
```

This can be inconvenient for:

- Teachers during lessons
- Presenters
- Streamers
- Software developers
- Office workers
- Students during exams or study sessions

Users often need to quickly silence notifications and then restore them afterward.

Examples:
```
Ctrl + Alt + D
Win + Shift + D
Alt + F12
```

```
Shortcut pressed
```

```
Shortcut pressed
```

## Benefits

- Useful for education environments and workplaces

All notifications are instantly silenced.

Notifications are restored.

title: [Mouse Without Borders] Service mode: SYSTEM process leaks Token/Event/Thread handles at a constant rate (~10k handles/day)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2 - Stable

### Installation method

Other (please specify in "Steps to Reproduce")

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Two Windows 11 PCs on the same wired LAN (1 Gb Ethernet), both running PowerToys 0.100.2 with Mouse Without Borders enabled and **Service mode ON**. All other MWB options are off, including Share clipboard and Transfer file.
2. Leave both machines running normally for several days.
3. Every 15 minutes, sample the handle count and the per-object-type handle breakdown of the `PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe` processes (in service mode there are two, both running as SYSTEM). I used `NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemExtendedHandleInformation)` grouped by object type from a scheduled script; Process Explorer's handle view shows the same thing.

Installation method: per-user install (%LOCALAPPDATA%\PowerToys); I'm not certain which update channel it was installed/updated through.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Handle count and private memory of the service-mode MWB processes stay roughly flat over days of uptime, as they do on the second PC.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

On one of the two PCs, the SYSTEM-level `PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe` instance that owns the TCP connections (port 15100) leaks handles at a **constant ~105 handles per 15 minutes (~7/min, ~10,000/day)** - the same rate at 3 AM with the machine idle as during active daytime use, so it looks timer-driven rather than input-driven.

Only three object types grow, in a fixed ~3:2:1 ratio:

| Handle type | start | +44 h | +92 h |
|---|---|---|---|
| Token | 31 | 4,930 | 9,848 |
| Event | 209 | 3,330 | 6,636 |
| Thread | 60 | 1,618 | 3,271 |
| Process | 317 | 318 | 318 |
| File | 107 | 108 | 108 |

That works out to roughly one set of *3 Token + 2 Event + 1 Thread* handles leaked every ~26 s, while the process's live thread count stays flat (~19). It looks like a short-lived worker thread running under a duplicated/impersonation user token whose thread, token and event handles are never closed.

Other observations:
- Total handles reached ~20,400 after ~3.5 days of uptime; on the previous boot it peaked near 29,000.
- When `PowerToys.MouseWithoutBordersHelper.exe` restarts, the leaked handles are released (observed 20,453 -> 1,015 and 9,205 -> 955), so the leaked objects seem tied to the helper / user session.
- Private bytes of the same process also grow, but in steps during daytime use rather than linearly: 38 MB -> 692 MB over ~3.5 days, flat overnight (previous boot reached 566 MB).
- The second SYSTEM MWB process and the helper do not leak (sawtooth between ~800 and ~1,060 handles).
- The connection between the PCs was stable the whole time (2 established connections, no TIME_WAIT churn on 15100/15101).
- The other PC (same PowerToys version, same MWB settings, service mode) does **not** leak: ~800 handles / ~35 MB after 4.5 days.

Current workaround: a daily scheduled restart of the MWB service and PowerToys.

Happy to collect more data (e.g. handle stacks or a dump of the process) if that helps.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OS: Windows 11, build 10.0.26200 (x64); Memory Integrity (HVCI) enabled
Installation: per-user
Running as admin: No (PowerToys runs non-elevated; MWB in Service mode)
Affected PC: laptop, AMD Ryzen 7 4800H, 32 GB RAM, typically ~330 running processes
Unaffected PC: mini PC on the same LAN, same PowerToys version and MWB settings

### Other Software

ProtonVPN client installed and running on the affected PC. No other mouse/keyboard-sharing software. The affected PC runs many Chrome profiles and some Java automation processes.

title: Monaco preview shows an empty editor for any file that is not valid UTF-8 (decodeURIComponent throws on the base64-decoded bytes)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

0.101.2362

### Installation way

PowerToys auto-update

### Running as admin

No

### Area(s) with issue?

File Explorer: Preview Pane

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable "Source code files (Monaco)" in File Explorer add-ons.
2. Put a `.cpp` (or `.txt`, any Monaco-owned extension) whose bytes are NOT valid UTF-8 in a folder: a GBK/GB2312-encoded source file, or a plain ASCII file with a single Windows-1252 `é` (byte 0xE9).
3. Select it with the preview pane open.

A pair that isolates it: the same 41 KB `.cpp` saved as GBK (original, has Chinese UI strings) and converted with `iconv -f GBK -t UTF-8`. The UTF-8 copy renders with full syntax color; the GBK original shows an editor with line number `1` and no text. An ASCII copy with the non-ASCII lines stripped also renders, so size (under the 50 KB limit) and language detection are not involved.

Smallest case: a three-line ASCII `.cpp` containing ONE Windows-1252 byte (`// café` with 0xE9) shows the empty editor; the same three lines as UTF-8 with a BOM render. Results of the eight variants tried:

| file | bytes | result |
|---|---|---|
| original .cpp, GBK | 41,372 | empty editor |
| same, converted to UTF-8 | 41,624 | renders |
| same, non-ASCII lines stripped | 41,120 | renders |
| first 20,000 bytes of the GBK original | 20,000 | empty editor |
| 49,000 bytes of ASCII | 49,000 | renders |
| 3 lines ASCII + one 0xE9 byte | 111 | empty editor |
| 3 lines UTF-8 with BOM, one é | 86 | renders |
| 2 KB ASCII | 2,149 | renders |

### Expected behavior

The file is shown, decoded with the charset the handler detected (or at worst with replacement characters), like Notepad, VS Code and the Windows TXT previewer do.

### Actual behavior

The pane shows a Monaco editor with line number `1` and an empty document. No error, nothing in the handler log (`LocalLow\Microsoft\PowerToys\FileExplorer_localLow\Monaco\logs\...`: "Reading requested file ended", "Remove loading elements", no exception).

### Why (from the code)

`MonacoPreviewHandlerControl.cs` detects the encoding with `CharsetDetector.DetectFromFile`, reads the file with it, then puts `Convert.ToBase64String(encodingToUse.GetBytes(fileContent))` into `[[PT_CODE]]` in `Assets\Monaco\index.html`. The page decodes it with

```js
var code = decodeURIComponent(atob(base64code).split('').map(function (c) {
    return '%' + ('00' + c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16)).slice(-2);
}).join(''));
```

That `decodeURIComponent` idiom only works for UTF-8 bytes. For any other encoding the bytes that the C# side re-encoded with `encodingToUse` are not valid UTF-8 percent-sequences, `decodeURIComponent` throws `URIError: URI malformed`, and the script never calls `setValue`, so the editor stays empty. The detected encoding is thrown away at exactly the step where it was needed.

A fix would be either to always produce UTF-8 on the C# side (`Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(fileContent)` after reading with the detected encoding), or to pass the encoding name to the page and use `new TextDecoder(name).decode(bytes)`.

### Additional information

Windows 11 26100.9711. Related: #26716 (Windows-1252 detected as UTF-8, mojibake) and #26792 (blank .txt with Monaco on) describe neighbors of this; this report is the empty-editor shape with the decode step identified.

title: [Quick Accent] Combining-mark characters in the Pinyin set render as tofu on zh-CN systems
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2 - Stable

### Installation method

Other (please specify in Steps to Reproduce)

### Area(s) with issue?

Quick Accent

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11 build 26200, display language **Simplified Chinese** (so the default UI font is Microsoft YaHei). PowerToys 0.100.2, per-user install under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PowerToys`.
2. PowerToys Settings → Quick Accent → enabled. Character sets: **Pinyin** (French is also enabled, irrelevant here).
3. Hold <kbd>E</kbd> and press the activation key.
4. The 6th and 8th candidates are drawn as empty boxes (tofu).
5. The same happens on <kbd>A</kbd> (four boxes in a row), <kbd>M</kbd>, <kbd>N</kbd>, and on the number keys <kbd>1</kbd> / <kbd>4</kbd>.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Every candidate in the picker should be legible. The affected entries are a base letter plus a **combining** diacritic, so the diacritic should be drawn above the base letter.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

They are rendered as `.notdef` boxes. The character data itself is correct: selecting a boxy entry inserts the right code points, and the result displays correctly once pasted into Word or Notepad. Only the picker preview is broken.

### Additional Information

**Root cause.** The affected entries are combining sequences, defined in `src/modules/poweraccent/PowerAccent.Common/CharacterMappings.cs` (Pinyin set):

```csharp
[LetterKey.VK_A] = ["ā", "á", "ǎ", "à", "ɑ", "ɑ\u0304", "ɑ\u0301", "ɑ\u030c", "ɑ\u0300"],
[LetterKey.VK_E] = ["ē", "é", "ě", "è", "ê", "ê\u0304", "ế", "ê\u030c", "ề"],
[LetterKey.VK_M] = ["m\u0304", "ḿ", "m\u030c", "m\u0300"],
[LetterKey.VK_N] = ["n\u0304", "ń", "ň", "ǹ", "ŋ", "ŋ\u0304", "ŋ\u0301", "ŋ\u030c", "ŋ\u0300"],
[LetterKey.VK_1] = ["\u0304", "ˉ"],
[LetterKey.VK_4] = ["\u0300", "ˋ"],
```

On a zh-CN system the flyout appears to render candidate text with the CJK UI font (Microsoft YaHei / SimSun). Those fonts do contain the base letters (ê, ɑ, m, n, ŋ) but **do not contain U+0300, U+0301, U+0304 or U+030C**, and no font fallback is applied inside the flyout, so those code points fall through to `.notdef`.

**This is not a missing system font.** On the same machine I verified with fontTools that `Segoe UI`, `Segoe UI Variable`, `Arial`, `Calibri`, `Cambria`, `Consolas`, `Tahoma` and `Times New Roman` all contain those four combining marks (98 font files in total), and 15 font families additionally provide GPOS MarkToBase anchors for `U+0251`, so the marks would be positioned correctly if one of those fonts were used.

**Locale dependent.** With an English UI the same entries probably look fine because Segoe UI ends up being used, which may be why this went unnoticed.

**Suggested fix.** Give the candidate `TextBlock`s an explicit font stack with fallback (e.g. `Segoe UI` ahead of the CJK fallback), or pick a font known to cover every code point in the candidate string before rendering. Filtering out unrenderable entries would be a worse UX than fixing the font.

**Related but different:** #21969 (added pinyin characters), #22631 (pinyin accents), #34283 (missing IPA characters / bad placement).

### Other Software

Windows 11 build 26200 (25H2), Simplified Chinese UI. Fonts present: Microsoft YaHei, SimSun (both lack U+0300/0301/0304/030C); Segoe UI, Arial, Calibri, Cambria, Consolas, Tahoma, Times New Roman (all contain them).

title: [New PowerToy] Quick Convert: press Shift while dragging a file to convert it
body: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement While you drag files (from File Explorer or the desktop), pressing **Shift** opens a small wheel of target formats under the cursor. Dropping the files on a format converts them, and the new file appears next to the original. You don't open an app, there's no dialog, and the original is never touched. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90d056ac-2168-4789-80ad-64d62727da69 | Dragged file | Formats on the wheel | |---|---| | Image (PNG, JPG, BMP, GIF, TIFF, HEIC*, WebP*) | PNG, JPG, BMP, TIFF, GIF | | Video (MP4, MOV, WMV, AVI, MKV*) | MP4, WMV, AVI, or audio only: MP3, M4A, WAV | | Audio (MP3, WAV, M4A, WMA, FLAC) | MP3, M4A, WAV, WMA, FLAC | | PDF | PNG or JPG per page | \* when the codec is installed in Windows. There's an optional **Liquid Glass** style: the wheel refracts what's behind it like a glass lens (curved bevel, magnifying hub, slight color dispersion at the edges, specular rim), and the selection is a glass droplet that slides between formats on a spring. The default style matches the other PowerToys overlays. ### Scenario when this would be used? Converting one file today means opening an editor or a web converter, or installing a third-party tool. Common cases: a site only accepts JPG, someone sent a HEIC, you need the audio from a screen recording, or you need a PDF page as an image. Image conversion has been requested many times (#2686, #7001, #13276, #18420, #20131, #25913, #31472, #47902), and media conversion in #3442. ### Supporting information I have a working prototype on my fork: https://github.com/dark13b/PowerToys/tree/feature/quick-convert-wheel. The video above was recorded with it. How it's built, so it stays small and within PowerToys' existing patterns: - **No new dependencies and no ffmpeg.** It uses only codecs that ship with Windows: WIC for images, Media Foundation (`MediaTranscoder`) for audio/video, and `Windows.Data.Pdf` for PDF pages. Everything runs locally. - **Reuses shared PowerToys pieces:** `TransparentWindow` and `TransientSurface` (Common.UI.Controls) for the overlay, and the interop `KeyboardHook` for the trigger. - **Low false-positive trigger:** the wheel opens only when Shift is pressed while the mouse button is held **and** the shell's drag image (`SysDragImage`) is visible. So Shift during a box selection or a text selection does nothing. The Shift press is swallowed, so Explorer doesn't switch the drag to "move", and the drop is always accepted as a copy. - **Safe output:** files are created with unique names (`photo (2).jpg`), and a failed conversion removes its partial file. Open questions where I'd like your direction before I wire up the rest (module interface, Settings page, installer, GPO, OOBE): 1. Is a separate utility right, or would you rather see this somewhere else, for example a Command Palette extension or an extension of Image Resizer? A smaller, image-only part is proposed separately for Image Resizer (#2686), from the branch `dark13b:feature/imageresizer-output-format`. 2. Is Shift a good default trigger, or should it be configurable from the start? 3. Should the optional Liquid Glass style stay? To refract the real content, it captures the window under the wheel with Windows.Graphics.Capture while the wheel is open. The capture is borderless, stays local, and stops when the wheel closes. If that's a concern, the wheel can use the standard style only.

title: Keyboard Manager shortcut that uses WIN key breaks when enabling Grab And Move with modifier set to WIN key
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362 - Stable

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a shortcut map that uses Win key (eg: Win+Q mapped to Alt+F4) 
2. Enable Grab And Move Module with Win key set as the modifier 
3. Restart system 
4. Try Win+Q in any application to close app

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The shortcut will be engaged and the application will close as a result of respecting the mapped Alt+F4

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Windows Search pop us for no reason. Only after the shortcut is pressed multiple times will it, by a slim chance, be engaged

_No response_

title: New+: add an action to create a directory junction (virtual folder) pointing to a real folder
body:
### Description

New+ is great for templates, but the one file-system object it cannot produce is a **virtual folder** (NTFS directory junction). I'd like to suggest two related interactions, both driven from the existing New+ context menu.

**1. Create a virtual folder in the current directory**

- Right-click the folder background (or desktop) -> `New+` -> `Virtual folder...`
- A folder picker opens; user selects a real directory as the target
- A directory junction is created in the current location, immediately entering inline rename mode (same behavior as existing templates)
- Press Enter -> done

**2. Turn an existing empty folder into a virtual folder**

- Right-click an empty folder -> `New+` -> `Convert to virtual folder`
- A folder picker opens; user selects a real directory
- The empty folder is replaced by a directory junction pointing at that target

### Related

#2527 proposes a separate "PowerSymlink" utility for `mklink /D`. This request is narrower: add the capability inside the existing New+ flow, reusing its picker/rename UX.

### Environment

- PowerToys 0.102.2862.0
- Windows 10 22H2 (10.0.19041)
- Also relevant for Windows 11 users who rely on junctions to expose project folders on other drives

title: CmdPal: One hung command blocks all later invocations (EXT26.I1)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Show when an invocation is stalled and offer explicit recovery, such as restarting the extension or CmdPal. A timeout does not stop `Invoke`: late results must not affect the new session, and commands with unknown completion must not be retried automatically. Preserve serialization unless safe isolation is provided.

### Scenario when this would be used?

- `StartInvoke` ignores new invocations while `_handleInvokeTask` is occupied.

body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

### Area(s) with issue?

### Steps to reproduce

1. Hide a dock or remove its monitor with initialized bands in all three groups. (EXT26.C1)
2. Separately hold queued `SetupBands` publication and initialization, dispose the owner, then release that work. (EXT26.C2)

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Close setup admission, drain all three groups, and clean their bands. Reject pending publication and initialization and clean unpublished candidates, with remote cleanup off the UI thread. Repeated disposal must be harmless; a new dock must still initialize normally.

Draining current collections alone does not cover queued candidates.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

This issue covers two related problems:

- **Owned bands are left alive.** `DockViewModel.Dispose` only detaches the manager event and marks the owner disposed. It does not drain or clean `StartItems`, `CenterItems`, or `EndItems`. (EXT26.C1)
- **Queued work survives disposal.** `SetupBands` queues publication and initialization separately, without checking owner disposal. Pending work can repopulate the collections or attach new band subscriptions afterward. (EXT26.C2)

### Additional Information

(EXT26.C1, EXT26.C2)

An isolated owner-disposal test reproduced zero cleanup across all three groups (EXT26.C1). Queued setup was checked in source; no real dispatcher or monitor transition was tested (EXT26.C2).

2. Separately, pass an already-completed activation task and an already-canceled token to `StartExtensionWhenReadyAsync`.

title: CmdPal: Old providers can replace or remove current commands (EXT26.L1-L3)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` (`ef43bf8ff5f3`)

### Installation method

Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

1. Replace provider A with B using the same ProviderId, then raise ItemsChanged from A. (EXT26.L1)
2. Pause A's command load, register B and its commands/bands, then let A's load finish. (EXT26.L2)
3. Queue removal of A, register B with the same ID before removal runs, then release the queued work. (EXT26.L3)

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

- Retire old wrappers and detach their handlers. Old notifications must be ignored even if unsubscribe fails.
- Check the current wrapper before starting a refresh and again when publishing, with the final check and update synchronized against replacement. Clean rejected results without touching the replacement's objects.
- Keep the original provider lifetime through queued removal; matching only its ID is insufficient.

Unsubscribing alone does not stop a refresh or removal that is already in progress.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

This issue covers three related problems:

- **Old wrappers keep sending updates.** `CommandProviderWrapper` subscribes to `ItemsChanged` and forwards it as `CommandsChanged`. Reload and removal discard the wrapper without unsubscribing or retiring that notification path, so it can remain referenced and keep queuing refreshes. (EXT26.L1)
- **A late refresh overwrites the replacement.** `UpdateCommandsForProvider` awaits A's load, then replaces items by `ProviderId` without checking that A is still current. If B was registered meanwhile, A's results replace B's commands and bands, and B's objects are cleaned. (EXT26.L2)
- **A queued removal deletes the replacement.** `ExtensionService_OnProviderRemoved` queues work that reduces removed wrappers to provider IDs. If B is registered before that work runs, it can remove B's wrapper and clean B's commands and bands. (EXT26.L3)

### Additional Information

(EXT26.L1, EXT26.L2, EXT26.L3)

Stale refresh and queued removal reproduced in isolated tests (EXT26.L2, EXT26.L3). Subscription lifetime was checked in source; live retention was not measured (EXT26.L1).

https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/ef43bf8ff5f3678f860a05227ea668825b967bf6/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/CommandProviderWrapper.cs#L84-L125

title: [Quick Accent] Select accents with number keys (macOS-style)
body: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement Add an opt-in Quick Accent setting "Select with number keys" (default off). While the Quick Accent toolbar is shown, pressing 1–9 or 0 (top row or numpad) inserts the 1st–10th character immediately, like the macOS press-and-hold accent picker. When the setting is on, the toolbar shows small 1–9 / 0 hints under the first ten characters. Details: - Works with every activation key (Space, Left/Right arrow, Both, Press and hold). - Ctrl / Alt / Win combinations keep their normal meaning (no insertion). - Holding the letter or the number key after selecting does not type extra characters. - A number with no character at that position closes the toolbar without inserting anything. - With the setting off, behaviour is unchanged (digits keep working as Quick Accent letters). - Best hold duration is 400 ms ### Scenario when this would be used? Typing in languages with many variants per letter (e.g. Vietnamese, Polish, Czech, Turkish, Romanian), where reaching the 5th–10th character needs many Space/arrow presses. Also for users coming from macOS, where numbered accent selection is muscle memory. ### Supporting information I have a working implementation on my fork: https://github.com/Kinoman31-dot/PowerToys/tree/quick-accent-number-keys It changes 14 files: the Quick Accent keyboard listener (new SelectCharByIndex event and UpdateSelectWithNumberKeys setting), PowerAccent.Core and its settings service, the toolbar UI (number hints and sizing), the Settings page (new toggle, en-us strings) and the DSC docs. Validated locally with Visual Studio 2026: - x64 Debug and x64 Release builds of the full solution, plus the per-user WiX installer - Unit tests: PowerAccent.Core.UnitTests 35/35, PowerAccent.Common.UnitTests 20/20, Settings.UI.UnitTests 474/474 - Installed the local build and checked the feature manually I'm happy to open a PR if the team agrees with the approach. Claude and Copilot helped. Claude wrote the program, copilot built it for me to test it.

title: Light Switch: Add default theme selector and interval inversion for independent App/System rules
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Enhance **Light Switch** to allow users to define a permanent Default Mode (Dark or Light) as a baseline, with an inverted scheduling model where the utility only triggers a temporary switch during a specified time interval.

Currently, Light Switch's behavior assumes a Light mode baseline and treats the schedule as the trigger to turn Dark mode on. Additionally, while System and Apps can be toggled separately, the scheduling logic forces a uniform state change.

The requested enhancement would work as follows:
1. Global Default Baseline: Allow the user to select whether their permanent baseline state is Dark or Light. 
2. Interval-Based Inversion: Instead of scheduling "when Dark mode is active," allow users to set a specific time interval (e.g., 09:30 to 18:00) to temporarily flip into the opposite mode. 
3. Granular Component Filtering during the Interval: Within that scheduled interval, respect the user's specific Behavior checkboxes (e.g., leaving "System" unchecked so the taskbar and system UI stay locked in Dark mode, while checking "Apps" so only the applications switch to Light mode during those working hours). Outside of that window, everything reverts immediately back to the default baseline.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Permanent Dark System UI with Daytime Light Apps: A user wants their system UI (Taskbar, Start menu, window frames) to remain in Dark mode 24/7 to reduce eye strain, but wants their desktop apps to automatically switch to Light mode only during working hours (09:30 to 18:00) for daytime legibility, before automatically returning to full Dark mode in the evening.

### Supporting information

Currently, the schedule forces a global override based on a light-first default assumption, making it impossible to anchor a 24/7 dark baseline and punch a temporary "light hole" for specific components during office hours.

title: [FancyZones] Unassigned "Rotate windows across monitors" shortcut hook gets stuck during drag operations
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.101.2362

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

When "Rotate windows across monitors" is turned ON in FancyZones without an assigned shortcut, drag-and-drop operations across various system applications can cause the low-level key listener hook to freeze in an active state.

While File Explorer (e.g., dragging network paths like Z:\... to Quick Access) provides a reliable way to reproduce the issue, it is not isolated to Explorer. Once stuck, subsequent key presses are intercepted by FancyZones, triggering the monitor rotation overlay numbers (1, 2, 3) across screens and causing key presses to act as unintended system shortcuts (e.g., pressing S opens Snipping Tool, pressing F opens Search).

1. Open PowerToys Settings, then select FancyZones.
2. Enable Rotate windows across monitors, but leave the Rotation mode shortcut unassigned (+ Assign shortcut).
3. Perform a drag-and-drop operation (e.g., dragging a path/folder to Quick Access in File Explorer, or dragging items in other apps).
4. Release the drag.
5. Try typing normal letter keys on the keyboard.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Drag-and-drop operations complete normally without locking keyboard listeners, allowing normal typing to continue.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The low-level keyboard hook loses track of key-release events during the drag. Letter keys are intercepted:

- The monitor rotation overlay numbers (1, 2, 3) display across screens.
- Pressing modifier keys causes the overlay numbers to temporarily disappear, but pressing any letter key immediately brings the overlay back.
- Individual key presses act as Win shortcuts (e.g., S triggers Snipping Tool, F triggers Search).
- Standard key-reset methods (tapping Win, pressing Esc, or clearing virtual key states) do not resolve it.

Workarounds:
- Assigning an explicit shortcut to "Rotate windows across monitors" completely prevents/resolves the issue.
- Disabling "Rotate windows across monitors" in FancyZones settings also prevents the issue from occurring.

Video Demonstration: https://streamable.com/ntxmw5

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-18-02-21-12.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33624871/PowerToysReport_2026-10-18-02-21-12.zip)

### Additional Information

- Monitor setup: 3 displays
- OS Version: Windows 11

### Other Software

_No response_

title: Power Display does not start at login: named pipe connection times out after 5 s and the process is killed
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362 - Stable

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Power Display in PowerToys settings.
2. Enable "Run at startup" in General.
3. Reboot / sign in to Windows.
4. Power Display is not running (no flyout with Win+Ctrl+Shift+P).
5. Open PowerToys settings > Power Display > "Launch": it starts immediately.

Logs (PowerDisplay\ModuleInterface\Logs\v0.101.2362\log_2026-10-18.log):

[09:04:13.809277] [trace] Starting PowerDisplay process
[09:04:13.845439] [trace] Successfully started PowerDisplay process
[09:04:18.865493] [error] Error waiting for PowerDisplay to connect to named pipe
[09:04:18.881660] [error] Named pipe initialization failed; terminating PowerDisplay process
...
[09:05:09.948918] [trace] Launch action received   <- manual "Launch" from Settings
[09:05:09.997041] [trace] Successfully started PowerDisplay process
[09:05:10.583907] [trace] PowerDisplay successfully connected to named pipe   (~0.6 s)

Reproduced on every cold login: 2026-10-14, 10-15, 10-16, 10-18. The first start after boot always fails after ~5.05 s, and a manual launch later always connects in under 1 s.

The PowerDisplay app log (PowerDisplay\Logs\0.101.2362.0\Log_*.log) has no entry for the failed start; the first "PowerDisplay starting" line is the manual launch. So the process doesn't get as far as logging before being killed, which suggests it is slow during early session startup (system load, WinUI 3 bootstrap or DDC/CI init) rather than failing outright.

Workaround: delaying the PowerToys autorun scheduled task by 45 s (default is 3 s).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Power Display starts automatically with PowerToys at login, like the other modules.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The runner starts PowerToys.PowerDisplay.exe, but the process doesn't connect to the named pipe within 5 s on a cold login. The module interface then terminates it and never retries, so Power Display stays off until I click "Launch" in Settings.

Suggested fix: increase the named pipe timeout, retry the launch once or twice, or don't kill the process on timeout if it is still alive.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

OS version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300
.NET version: (bundled with PowerToys)
System language: French
User installation (per-user, %LOCALAPPDATA%\PowerToys)
Running as admin: no (PowerToys not elevated)
Monitor: BenQ EX3210R (DDC/CI)
PowerToys autorun: scheduled task, logon trigger, default 3 s delay

title: Host Windows Cannot Remain Above VMware Sessions Despite "Always on Top"
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

There are situations where a window from the host operating system needs to remain visible on top of a VMware session. The current 'Always on Top' functionality does not achieve this, as host windows are still obscured by the VMware display layer, preventing them from remaining accessible while working within the virtual session.
This applies to both single-monitor and multi-monitor VM configurations. At a minimum, host windows configured as 'Always on Top' should be allowed to remain visible on secondary and tertiary monitors while the VMware session is active on other displays.

### Scenario when this would be used?

A user is working within a VMware session while referencing information displayed in a host OS application, such as documentation, a ticketing system, a chat window, an authentication prompt, or monitoring tools. The host window needs to remain visible above the VMware session to avoid repeatedly switching focus between applications.


### Supporting information

_No response_

title: CmdPal: Refine SupersedingAsyncValueGate lifecycle
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

`SupersedingAsyncValueGate<T>` can lose a request when its worker becomes idle, leaving the returned task incomplete. In Bookmarks, this can leave an item stuck at "Refreshing".

Results can also be applied after disposal returns, and cancellation callbacks that acquire other locks can cause deadlocks.

Related: [#51369](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/51369) covers the non-generic gate.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Reliability

title: AI Usage Meter - Show available account limits and reset times from the system tray
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

A small tray popover that shows AI usage, remaining allowances, and reset times as available for configured AI providers in their native units.  

Begin with a flexible contract for provider interfaces, so users can create a custom interface for their specific meter from work, etc. in addition to pre-configured meters provided by PowerToys, to reduce the demand for custom integration of every potential provider and to enable e.g. workplace/team-specific tracking.  This may also be necessary because at the moment it seems neither Claude nor ChatGPT expose a metering endpoint publicly, though ChatGPT has enabled Sign-in with ChatGPT and 3P consumption with select partners in recent weeks.

Longer-term, existing provider-configuration patterns from e.g. Advanced Paste might be reusable and shared.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Increasingly, I need to treat token consumption like any other system resource: network connectivity, RAM and CPU, and free disk space -- and make decisions about how I use my system with that awareness.  AI use is no different, whether it's local (and consumes material resources) or in the cloud (which has marginal cost or limits).

When I look at the system tray, an icon tells me I'm running hot on my consumption, vs my regular pacing or limits, so I take a little more care in model selection per task and avoid having my work interrupted or running into overage charges.  

I can also see both my personal ChatGPT subscription usage alongside Copilot usage from work, which reminds me to use the correct providers in the correct context, similar to my work and personal OneDrive accounts.

### Supporting information

These tools are growing in popularity, but they're quite fragmented, especially for Windows.  I conducted a search across repositories for various ai meter apps -- they are all seeing scope creep, introducing additional complex features, and straying from a simple utility job to be done.
