title: [Mouse Without Borders] Service mode fails to connect when username contains spaces (unquoted path)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362 - Stable

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run PowerToys on a Windows machine where the user profile username contains spaces (e.g., `C:\Users\John Doe\`).
2. Pair Mouse Without Borders with a remote machine. Verify connection works normally in user mode.
3. Enable "Use Service" in PowerToys Settings > Mouse Without Borders (to enable control on elevated/UAC windows).
4. Attempt to connect from the remote machine or press "Refresh connection".

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

When "Use Service" is enabled, the elevated processes spawned by `PowerToys.MWB.Service` should load the user's actual settings from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\MouseWithoutBorders\settings.json`, preserving the configured `SecurityKey`, `MachineMatrixString`, and `MachinePool`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The connection fails immediately. The remote machine cannot connect.

An orphaned directory is created at `C:\Users\<FirstWordOfUsername>\Microsoft\PowerToys\MouseWithoutBorders\settings.json` (e.g. `C:\Users\John\` instead of `C:\Users\John Doe\AppData\Local\`).
- This orphaned `settings.json` is generated from scratch with a newly generated random `SecurityKey` and an empty `MachineMatrixString: []`.
- The elevated service-spawned process (`NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`, running on Desktop `default` and `winlogon`) binds to TCP ports `15100` and `15101` using this orphaned configuration file.
- The remote machine attempts to handshake using the user's real `SecurityKey` and machine name from the user's actual `%LOCALAPPDATA%` configuration.
- Because the keys and allowed machine list mismatch, the elevated process rejects the connection.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

### **Root Cause**
In `src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Service/Worker.cs` (`RunMeUnderSystemAccount`), `userLocalAppDataPath` is passed to `CreateProcessAsSystemAccountOnSpecificDesktop` without quotes:
```csharp
me + " \"default\" " + userLocalAppDataPath
```
When the user's profile path contains spaces, `PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe` splits the arguments by space, taking only the first word as `Helper.UserLocalAppDataPath`, creating and reading from `C:\Users\<FirstWord>\`.

### **Temporary Workaround**
Create an NTFS Directory Junction pointing the truncated directory to the real LocalAppData path:
```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "C:\Users\<FirstWordOfUsername>\Microsoft\PowerToys\MouseWithoutBorders" -Target "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\PowerToys\MouseWithoutBorders"
```

### Other Software

None

title: New+: template folder and template items are leaked every time the context menu is built
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

main (7b6789c)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Area(s) with issue?

New+

### Steps to reproduce

Found by reading the code (`src/modules/NewPlus`), no end-user repro:

1. Each time the New+ submenu is built, `shell_context_sub_menu` does `templates = new template_folder(root)` (`shell_context_sub_menu.cpp`) and never deletes it.
2. `template_folder::rescan_template_folder` allocates a `new template_item` for every template, and `~template_folder` only calls `list_of_templates.clear()` on the raw pointers, so the items are never freed either.
3. The Windows 10 menu (`shell_context_menu_win10.cpp`) does the same `templates = new template_folder(...)` in every `QueryContextMenu` call, overwriting (and leaking) the previous one.

Every time the user right-clicks a folder background, Explorer leaks one `template_folder` plus one `template_item` per template, for as long as Explorer runs.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The objects created for a menu are released when the menu is gone.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

They are never released. The reason a plain `delete` isn't enough is that `shell_context_sub_menu_item` keeps a raw `const template_item*`, and Explorer can invoke those items after the enumerator is released, so freeing the folder with the enumerator would be a use-after-free.

### Additional Information

I have a fix that makes the items `std::shared_ptr` (menu items share ownership, the Windows 10 menu owns its folder with `std::unique_ptr`). It builds for both the Windows 11 and Windows 10 extension projects. I'm happy to open a PR if this is welcome. Follow-up to #51141, which covers other small defects in the same extension.

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add a utility (or expand existing window management tools) that allows users to minimize any application window directly to the System Tray (notification area) by **right-clicking the minimize button** on the window's title bar, similar to the classic tool **RBTray**.

**Expected behavior:**
- Right-clicking the standard Minimize button of any active window immediately hides the window from the Taskbar and places its icon in the System Tray.
- Left-clicking or right-clicking the icon in the System Tray restores or manages the window.
- Option in PowerToys settings to enable/disable this feature, customize hotkeys, or set rules for specific applications.

### Scenario when this would be used?

As a power user, I often run multiple background applications (e.g., terminal sessions, server monitoring, media players, or long-running scripts) that don't natively support minimizing to the system tray.

- **Taskbar clutter reduction:** Keeping these windows open clutters the Taskbar, making multitasking inefficient.
- **Workflow efficiency:** Being able to quickly right-click the minimize button is intuitive, fast, and eliminates the need to open secondary menus or navigate to specialized tray-minimizing software.
- **Integration:** Having this functionality natively in PowerToys would eliminate the need to rely on outdated 3rd-party software like RBTray.

### Supporting information

- **Reference tool:** RBTray (https://rbtray.sourceforge.net/)
- Similar concepts exist in other tools, but a native, maintained PowerToys implementation would provide better compatibility with modern Windows 11 / Windows 10 window frames and dark mode themes.

title: New+: several robustness bugs in the shell extension (Next() slot index, REG_SZ size, missing null checks, MAX_PATH buffers)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

main (e1bb0cc)

### Installation method

Built from source

### Area(s) with issue?

New+

### Steps to reproduce

Found by reading the New+ shell extension code (`src/modules/NewPlus/NewShellExtensionContextMenu`). These are code defects, not a single end-user repro:

1. `shell_context_sub_menu::Next` writes every fetched command to `apUICommand[0]` instead of `apUICommand[i]`. A caller asking for more than one item gets only the first slot written, yet `S_OK` is returned, and each overwrite leaks a reference.
2. `disable_built_in_new_via_registry` passes the character count (without the terminating null) as the byte size of the `REG_SZ` value, so a truncated, unterminated string is stored when New+ is configured by policy to hide the built-in New menu. `disable_/enable_built_in_new_via_registry` also return `true` on failure and `false` on success (callers currently ignore the result).
3. `get_path_from_unknown_site` / `get_path_from_folder_view` don't check the HRESULT or null result of `QueryInterface`, `QueryService` and `GetFolder` (the New+ menu is also shown in places where there is no `IFolderView` service), and leak the string returned by `StrRetToStr`.
4. `template_item::copy_object_to` copies paths into `wchar_t[MAX_PATH + 1]` using `wcsncpy_s` with the source length as the count. A path of 261+ characters hits the CRT invalid parameter handler (Explorer terminates), and a path of exactly 260 characters writes one `wchar_t` past the buffer when adding the second terminating null.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

None of the above should crash Explorer, leak, or store a malformed registry value.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

See above. I have a small fix for each, built with the repo's x64 Debug settings (`/W3 /WX`, `/analyze`) but not run inside Explorer, and I'm happy to send it as a PR if this is welcome.

### Additional Information

I looked for an existing issue or PR covering these and found none. Related but separate: New+ also never frees the `template_folder`/`template_item` objects created per menu enumeration (menu items hold raw `template_item*`); that needs a shared-ownership change, so I'm leaving it out of this report.

### Other Software

_No response_

title: Possibility for Power Display profiles to be automatically activated at particular time of a day
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

It would be great to have a feature that automatically switches between different profiles with preset display settings at various times of the day. This requires adding an activation time option to the profile settings.

### Scenario when this would be used?

My situation could be illustrative. I sit in front of a window and have to adjust the brightness of my two displays several times a day, depending on the sun's position and how bright it is. For this, I created 7 profiles in Power Display (Dawn, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Evening, Dusk, Night) to change the displays' settings quickly and not fiddle with each display separately. Still, I have to do it 5-7 times a day. It'd be very helpful to just set a particular time for each profile so it can be automatically activated during the day.

title: Proposal: Modernized “PowerToys 2026 Pro Edition” Icon (High‑Resolution, Scalable Redesign)
body: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement Summary I’m proposing a refreshed PowerToys icon designed for 2026 and beyond — a modernized, high‑resolution emblem that preserves the original geometry while giving it depth, clarity, and visual identity across all DPI scales. The current PowerToys icon is functional but intentionally flat. My redesign elevates the existing pictograph into a more expressive, recognizable symbol that remains crisp and distinctive from 16×16 up to 256×256. Design Intent The goal was to keep the familiar PowerToys layout (four vertical bars + three squares) while enhancing: Depth and curvature for a more modern Windows 11/12 aesthetic Color separation that remains readable even at small sizes Circular glow rhythm that gives the icon presence without noise High‑resolution clarity that survives Explorer scaling and thumbnail compression The result is an icon that feels like a natural evolution — a “PowerToys 2026 Pro Edition” identity. Why This Matters The icon remains fully recognizable at all scales (verified through Explorer’s scroll‑wheel size sweep). It maintains the original PowerToys geometry, so it’s familiar to users. It visually communicates that PowerToys is a modern, powerful, expert‑grade toolset. It aligns with the design language of current Windows UI (glow, depth, soft curvature). This is a branding/UI enhancement that strengthens PowerToys’ identity without altering functionality. ### Scenario when this would be used? ### Supporting information _No response_

title: Command Palette > Dock
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I liked the idea of the Dock being available to display my PC stats on the right-hand side of the screen.  Unfortunately, the bar goes the whole way across the screen.  So I set it to auto-hide so it disappears and transparent so it just displays the info I want to see.  But then when you are using, say the browser, and hover over a tab, the transparent bar reappears and blocks you from selecting the browser tab.  So as much as I'd like to see the stats at a glance, the way it is at the moment makes it unusable.  So if you could, I would have just a small bar for only where the stats are and leave it at that.  That way it doesn't interfere with the normal operation, and I can hover over where I'd expect to see the stats, and they just appear.

title: FancyZonesCLI set-layout ignores --monitor and fails to apply custom layouts on multiple identical monitors
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.102.2803 Preview

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install/run PowerToys v0.102.2803.0 with FancyZones enabled.

2. Configure three monitors. In my environment these are three identical Dell DEL4362 displays at 2560x1440.

3. Open PowerShell and confirm the monitors are detected:
   & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\PowerToys\FancyZonesCLI.exe" get-monitors

4. Set all monitors to the same starting layout (in my test, priority-grid).

5. Attempt to apply a built-in layout to only Monitor 1:
   & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\PowerToys\FancyZonesCLI.exe" set-layout columns --monitor 1

6. The CLI reports:
   Layout 'columns' applied to monitor 1.

7. Check the result:
   & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\PowerToys\FancyZonesCLI.exe" get-active-layout

8. Observe that "columns" was applied to ALL THREE monitors instead of only Monitor 1.

9. Next, list the available custom layouts:
   & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\PowerToys\FancyZonesCLI.exe" get-layouts

10. Choose a valid custom-layout UUID returned by that command. In my test:
    Meeting - Center
    UUID: {5B5C93B2-9C7E-4E47-BB02-26BD08B05AB8}

11. Attempt to apply that custom layout only to Monitor 2:
    & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\PowerToys\FancyZonesCLI.exe" set-layout "{5B5C93B2-9C7E-4E47-BB02-26BD08B05AB8}" --monitor 2

12. The CLI reports:
    Layout '{5B5C93B2-9C7E-4E47-BB02-26BD08B05AB8}' applied to monitor 2.

13. Check the result again:
    & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\PowerToys\FancyZonesCLI.exe" get-active-layout

14. Observe that the requested custom layout was NOT applied to Monitor 2. In my test, all three monitors instead reported the built-in "priority-grid" layout.

Additional potentially relevant detail:
All three displays report the same model (DEL4362) and serial number (6TJLB84), but FancyZonesCLI correctly enumerates them as three monitors with different Monitor Instance IDs:
Monitor 1: ...UID4353
Monitor 2: ...UID4355
Monitor 3: ...UID4357

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

When using the --monitor parameter, FancyZonesCLI should apply the requested layout only to the specified monitor and leave the layouts on all other monitors unchanged.

For example:

set-layout columns --monitor 1

should apply the built-in Columns layout only to Monitor 1.

Likewise:

set-layout "{custom-layout-UUID}" --monitor 2

should apply that custom layout only to Monitor 2.

FancyZonesCLI should also report success only when the requested layout has actually been applied to the specified monitor.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

When using a built-in layout with --monitor, the command reports success but applies the layout to all three monitors instead of only the specified monitor.

For example:

set-layout columns --monitor 1

reports:
Layout 'columns' applied to monitor 1.

However, get-active-layout shows that all three monitors have been changed to Columns.

Custom layouts fail differently. When I specify a valid custom-layout UUID returned by get-layouts, the CLI again reports that the layout was successfully applied to the specified monitor, but the requested custom layout is not actually applied.

For example:

set-layout "{5B5C93B2-9C7E-4E47-BB02-26BD08B05AB8}" --monitor 2

reports that the layout was applied to Monitor 2, but get-active-layout subsequently shows all three monitors using priority-grid instead.

Therefore, there appear to be two issues:
1. --monitor does not restrict built-in layout changes to the specified monitor.
2. Custom layouts are not applied correctly despite the CLI reporting success.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-08-14-07-06.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33219547/PowerToysReport_2026-10-08-14-07-06.zip)

### Additional Information

Windows 11 Enterprise, build 26300

User

title: PowerToys Run Value Generator: UUID v3/v5 of a non-ASCII name is wrong, and different names give the same UUID
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2 (stable). The code is unchanged on `main` (c340835).

### Installation method

Not relevant here; the behavior is in the plugin code (see below).

### Area(s) with issue?

PowerToys Run

### Steps to reproduce

1. In PowerToys Run, type `# uuidv5 ns:DNS café.com`.
2. Then type `# uuidv5 ns:DNS caf?.com`.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Two different UUIDs, matching other implementations, which hash the name as UTF-8. For example Python's `uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_DNS, "café.com")` and the same computation in Node.js both give `31ec427b-2d6c-5aaf-bbbb-d1c7b7b33948`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Both names give `3fb190a8-507d-5e15-9776-3955d4bc66be`, which is the UUID of `caf?.com`. `uuidv3` behaves the same way.

`GUIDGenerator.V3AndV5` converts the name with `Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(uuidName)`, which replaces every non-ASCII character with `?`. Any name with accented letters, CJK or emoji therefore gets a UUID that no other implementation produces, and names that differ only in those characters collide. ASCII names are unaffected, so the existing `abc` test vectors still hold.

I reproduced this by calling `V3`/`V5` in the installed 0.101.2 plugin assembly and in `GUIDGenerator.cs` built from `main`; both return the values above. Using `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes` fixes it, and all existing vectors still pass. I have that change ready with two new test rows and can open a PR if this approach works for you.

### Additional Information

`src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Community.PowerToys.Run.Plugin.ValueGenerator/Generators/GUID/GUIDGenerator.cs:74`

title: ≤0.100.x clients can never detect v0.101.x — 4-part release tag unparseable by old VersionHelper (silent "up to date")
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2 - Stable

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

General

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PowerToys v0.100.2 (Stable) — any build ≤0.100.x behaves the same.
2. Wait for a scheduled update check, or restart PowerToys / open Settings > General to trigger one.
3. `GET https://api.github.com/repos/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/latest` currently returns `tag_name: v0.101.2362.0` — a four-part version, non-prerelease, with a "Latest" badge and release assets present. Verify with:
```ps1
(Invoke-RestMethod https://api.github.com/repos/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/latest).tag_name
```
4. Settings reports "PowerToys is up to date" and no update is offered.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

v0.100.2 detects v0.101.2362.0 as a newer release and offers/downloads the update.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The update check reports "up to date" with no error in the UI or logs.

Root cause: `VersionHelper::fromString` in builds ≤0.100.x only accepts 3-part versions. The 4-part tag `v0.101.2362.0` fails to parse, so `extract_version_from_release_object` returns `nullopt`, `github_version` remains equal to `current_version`, and `get_github_version_info_async` returns `version_up_to_date` — silently, with no logged error. See `src/common/updating/updating.cpp` (~lines 119-130).

Four-part version support was added in PR #49414 (commit 558e633c, merged 2026-08-06), which shipped *after* v0.100.2. The same PR that introduced the new Insider channel also changed `resolveBuildMetadata.ps1` to emit `major.minor.YDDDB.0` tags — so the new release tag format is unparseable by every build shipped before that PR.

Note: the v0.101 release notes mention "we're working through an issue with the update rollout, so this release may take a little longer than usual to reach everyone." For clients on ≤0.100.x this is not a delay — the update will *never* be detected. The rollout banner understates the impact for this population.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-10-08-17-13-52.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33197652/PowerToysReport_2026-10-08-17-13-52.zip)

### Additional Information

- Note on the attached report: no error appears in the logs for this issue (see Actual Behavior for why). The ZIP is attached to confirm via `UpdateState.json` that an update check did run and reported up-to-date, and to rule out GPO/network factors (`gpo-configuration-info.txt`).
- This is fundamentally a release/server-side problem, not a fixable client bug: shipped ≤0.100.x binaries cannot be patched. As of filing (2026-10-08), no commits since PR #49414 have touched `VersionHelper::fromString` or `updating.cpp`, and the release train has advanced to 0.102 (commit e1bb0cca) — meaning future tags will remain 4-part and unparseable by ≤0.100.x. Every remaining ≤0.100.x install is affected, not just this machine.
- A possible mitigation would be publishing a 3-part-tag bridge release on GitHub so old clients can detect it, or documenting manual upgrade instructions prominently for affected users.
- OS version: Windows 11, 10.0.26200 (Build 26200)
- .NET version (dotnet --list-runtimes):

Not confirmed.

Quick Accent

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable Quick Accent.
2. Under **Language sets**, select **French** only. Under **Special sets**, **Currency** is also enabled. The supplied settings screenshot shows all other language and special sets unchecked.

title: Quick display scale (DPI) switcher as a module or Command Palette extension
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

A small utility for switching Windows display scaling (e.g. 100% ↔ 250%) in one action, without opening Settings > System > Display. It would be a spiritual successor to QuickRes tray icon friend to CRTs (RIP), but for UI scale rather than resolution.

Proposed behavior:
- User-defined presets (e.g. 100%, 150%, 250%) that can be applied with one click, hotkey, or command
- Per-monitor support, defaulting to the primary display
- Optionally, a "toggle back to previous scale" action

I'm open to either form factor: a standalone PowerToys module (tray icon + settings page) or a Command Palette extension. I'd appreciate maintainer guidance on which is preferred.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I frequently share my 4K desktop in Teams calls. At 100-150% scale, my shared screen looks tiny to attendees on smaller displays and text is hard to read. Raising the scale to around 250% for the call fixes that, but doing it through Settings takes several clicks, and I have to repeat the process to change it back afterward. Changing resolution instead isn't a good alternative, since it blurs the display, while scale keeps it sharp.

Other likely scenarios: presenting or screen sharing, recording tutorials or demos, and docking a laptop between displays with very different pixel densities.

### Supporting information

Open questions for maintainers:
1. Is this a better fit as a standalone module or a Command Palette extension?
2. As far as I know, Windows has no documented API for changing DPI scale. Community tools (search "SetDPI") do it using undocumented DisplayConfigGetDeviceInfo / DisplayConfigSetDeviceInfo info types. Is relying on those acceptable for PowerToys?

I'm interested in implementing this but before investing I wanted to confirm it's a good fit and get guidance on the preferred approach. I'm happy to start with a prototype of the scaling logic and share it here.

title: Reloading extensions can drop all of an extension's commands when one item fails
body:
sorry, I'm filing an AI bug report of something I saw in passing. I'll come back to it. If you're a human that isn't me, you can go ahead and ignore the rest of this. This is more just a reminder to myself to come back and fix this.


-----

`COMException 0x800706BA` from `IWeakReference.Resolve` in `add_PropChanged`

**Command Palette version:** 0.12.12175.0 (`Microsoft.CommandPalette_0.12.12175.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`)

**Repro**

1. Install an extension that implements `ICommandProvider4.GetCommandItem` 
2. Pin a couple of its nested commands to the top level. Each pinned item has many `MoreCommands`.
3. Run **Reload Command Palette extensions** once or twice.

**Expected:** the extension's commands load.


**Actual:** the log shows `Loaded 0 command(s) and 0 band(s) from <extension>`, and none of its commands appear. Other extensions failed on the same reload: `Microsoft.CmdPalAzureExtension` and `Microsoft.PowerToys.SparseApp`. Restarting `Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe` fixes it.


**Log**

```
[Error] CommandProviderWrapper.cs::LoadTopLevelCommands::241
    Failed to load commands from extension GitHubExtension_8wekyb3d8bbwe
System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (-2147023174):   // 0x800706BA RPC_S_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE
   at ABI.WinRT.Interop.IWeakReference.global::WinRT.Interop.IWeakReference.Resolve(Guid)
   at ABI.WinRT.Interop.EventSourceCache.GetState(Int32)
   at ABI.WinRT.Interop.EventSourceCache.GetState(IObjectReference, Int32)
   at ABI.Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.INotifyPropChangedMethods.<>c__DisplayClass5_0.<Get_PropChanged2>b__0(Object)
   at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ConditionalWeakTable`2.GetValue(...)
   at ABI.Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.INotifyPropChanged...add_PropChanged(TypedEventHandler`2)
   at Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.CommandItemViewModel.InitializeProperties()
   at Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.CommandContextItemViewModel.InitializeProperties()
   at Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.CommandItemViewModel.SlowInitializeProperties()
   at Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.DefaultContextMenuFactory.UnsafeBuildAndInitMoreCommands(IContextItem[], CommandItemViewModel)
   at Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.CommandItemViewModel.BuildAndInitMoreCommands()
   at Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.TopLevelViewModel.InitializeProperties()
   at Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.CommandProviderWrapper.InitializeCommands(...)
   at Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels.CommandProviderWrapper.LoadTopLevelCommands()

```



**Where**


Subscribing to `PropChanged` on a context item fails. My guess is that CsWinRT's `EventSourceCache` still holds a weak reference to an event source from the extension process that was killed during reload. `CommandItemViewModel.cs`:



```c#
// CommandItemViewModel.InitializeProperties()
        // TODO: Do these need to go into FastInit?
        model.PropChanged += Model_PropChanged;   // <-- throws 0x800706BA
        Command.PropertyChanged += Command_PropertyChanged;

```

Nothing catches the exception per item, so one bad context item takes down every command from that provider. `CommandProviderWrapper.cs`:


```C#
// CommandProviderWrapper.InitializeCommands()
var make = (ICommandItem? i, TopLevelType t) =>
{
    CommandItemViewModel commandItemViewModel = new(new(i), pageContext, contextMenuFactory: contextMenuFactory);
    TopLevelViewModel topLevelViewModel = new(commandItemViewModel, t, ...);
    topLevelViewModel.InitializeProperties();   // <-- any throw here aborts the whole provider
    return topLevelViewModel;
};
...
topLevelList.AddRange(objects.Commands.Select(c => make(c, TopLevelType.Normal)));
...
foreach (var pinnedCommand in objects.PinnedCommands)
{
    var pinnedItem = make(pinnedCommand, TopLevelType.Normal);

```


The exception goes up to `LoadTopLevelCommands`'s `catch (Exception e)`, which logs it and leaves the provider with no commands.


**Suggested fix**



1. **Isolate failures per item.** In `InitializeCommands`, wrap each `make(...)` call for commands, pinned commands, fallbacks, and bands in try/catch. Log the failure and skip that item, so one bad item doesn't empty the whole provider.

2. **Make each context item's setup tolerant.** In `DefaultContextMenuFactory.UnsafeBuildAndInitMoreCommands`, or around the `PropChanged +=` subscription, catch `COMException` per context item. A failed subscription should mean only that the item won't live-update, not that loading fails.

3. **Investigate the root cause.** Find out why event-source state from the previous extension process survives the reload. On extension restart, the old proxies should be released and their event registrations dropped, or a retry should resolve fresh state.

title: ZoomIt: Live Zoom waits about 0.3 seconds before it starts zooming
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel
0.100.2

### Installation method
WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?
ZoomIt

### Steps to reproduce
1. Set a Live Zoom hotkey in ZoomIt.
2. Press the hotkey to start Live Zoom, then press it again to end it.
3. Press the hotkey again.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior
The zoom animation starts right after the hotkey is pressed.

### ❌ Actual Behavior
Every time, about 0.3 seconds pass before the first zoom step. Nothing on screen changes during that time.

I measured this by reading Live Zoom's zoom level from the ZoomIt process (the address comes from `WM_USER_GET_ZOOM_LEVEL`) about every millisecond after the key press. The first zoom step came 0.27 to 0.32 seconds after the key press.

### Additional Information

**Cause**

On Windows 7 and later, `LiveZoomWndProc` destroys the Live Zoom window when Live Zoom ends. This happens in `WM_SHOWWINDOW` (wParam FALSE) and in the `zoomLevel == 1` branch of `WM_TIMER`. The next hotkey creates the window again. `WM_CREATE` calls `MagInitialize` and creates the `WC_MAGNIFIER` child before the first zoom step can run. The same code is in `main` today.

**Possible fix**

- Hide the window instead of destroying it. The code already does this for Windows versions older than Windows 7 (`ShowWindow(SW_HIDE)` and timer 1 to destroy it later).
- While the window is hidden, the magnifier child still has the `MS_SHOWMAGNIFIEDCURSOR` style, and that style keeps the normal mouse pointer hidden after Live Zoom ends. The existing `MagShowSystemCursor(TRUE)` call in `WM_SHOWWINDOW` does not bring it back. So the style has to be turned off when the window is hidden and turned on when it is shown. The existing `WM_USER_MAGNIFY_CURSOR` message already does this.
- Some code checks `g_hWndLiveZoom != nullptr` to mean "Live Zoom is active", for example when recording starts and in the record crop path. That code would need to check `IsWindowVisible(g_hWndLiveZoom)` instead.

**Test**

I tried this on 0.100.2 by patching `PowerToys.ZoomIt.exe` locally. I kept the window hidden instead of destroying it, and I toggled `MS_SHOWMAGNIFIEDCURSOR` in `WM_SHOWWINDOW`. Results:

| | 0.100.2 | With the change |
|---|---|---|
| Hotkey to first zoom step | 0.27–0.32 s | 0.01–0.02 s |
| Mouse pointer after Live Zoom ends | drawn | drawn, at the moment the window is hidden |
| Keyboard focus | stays in the active app | stays in the active app |
| ZoomIt CPU while the window is hidden | – | 0 ms in 10 s |

The first Live Zoom after ZoomIt starts still has the delay, because the window does not exist yet.

If this approach is acceptable, I would like to submit a PR against `main`.

### Other Software
Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200

title: Add support for pinning apps to a specific monitor taskbar
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add support for pinning applications to the taskbar of a specific monitor in a multi-monitor setup.

Windows 11 currently supports the setting "Taskbar where window is open", which correctly shows a running application's taskbar button on the monitor where the window is located.

However, there is currently no way to permanently pin an application specifically to a secondary monitor's taskbar.

The expected behavior would be:

- Allow a user to pin an application to Monitor 1, Monitor 2, etc.
- The pinned application should remain visible on that monitor's taskbar even when the application is closed.
- The application should not automatically become pinned on the other monitors.
- Optionally, launching the application from that taskbar could open the application on the same monitor.

For example:

Monitor 1:
Outlook, Teams, Chrome

Monitor 2:
Visual Studio, SSMS, Remote Desktop

Each monitor would maintain its own set of pinned applications.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would be useful for users with multi-monitor workstations who organize different applications by monitor.

For example, I use one monitor for general applications and another monitor for development or work-related applications.

Windows already allows running application buttons to appear on the "Taskbar where window is open", but once the application is closed, there is no persistent shortcut on that secondary monitor.

Being able to pin applications independently to each monitor would make it much faster to launch applications in a multi-monitor workflow and would allow each monitor's taskbar to act as a dedicated application launcher.

### Supporting information

Windows 11 already provides multi-monitor taskbar behavior through:

Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors > When using multiple displays, show my taskbar apps on > Taskbar where window is open

This works well for running applications, but pinned applications are not independently configurable per monitor.

The requested feature would extend the existing multi-monitor taskbar behavior by allowing persistent per-monitor pinned applications.

Similar functionality is available in third-party multi-monitor tools such as DisplayFusion, which suggests there is demand for this type of workflow.

title: [Mouse Without Borders] Current issues grouped by cause (tracking overview)
body:
## Summary

Mouse Without Borders (MWB) has 358 open issues as of 2026-10-07: 266 bug reports, 89 feature requests and 3 documentation requests. Most are single reports with little follow-up, and many describe the same few underlying problems. This issue aggregates them: it groups the reports by cause, cross-links the ones that belong together, and points at the code that appears responsible. The aim is that a new report can be matched to an existing one instead of being filed again. It is an index, not a new bug report.


## Scope and method

- **Data:** every open issue labelled `Product-Mouse Without Borders` (341), plus 17 open issues that name MWB in the title or in the "Area(s) with issue?" field but carry no product label. Collected through the GitHub search API on 2026-10-07.
- **Grouping:** by reading titles and descriptions. Reports without enough detail to place are counted under "Unclear or other". Counts are approximate.
- **Code references:** checked against `main` at 4e6b2506570f459a71bf413d96b96ec471664cf0 (2026-10-06). Call relationships (who calls a method, who writes a field) were checked with a code graph built from the same commit. Each cause below says whether the code behaviour is confirmed, and whether its link to the reports is confirmed or only suspected.
- **Not done:** causes 1 to 11 were not reproduced on a two-machine setup for this write-up, and no bug report archives were analysed.
- **Tooling:** compiled with AI assistance. Every code reference was checked against the linked commit.
- **Updated 2026-10-21:** causes 12 to 15 added, and causes 5, 6 and 7 updated, from debugging one pair of machines on 0.100.2. The new references use the same commit; the files they point to are unchanged in 0.102.2862.0.

Volume for context: 82 MWB issues were opened since 2026-04-07 (67 still open) and 86 labelled ones were closed in the same period, 47 of them as duplicates. Open issues by year opened: 2023: 76, 2024: 94, 2025: 99, 2026: 89.

## At a glance

## How a drop plays out in the code

Three behaviours explain most of what the "drops" and "stops working" reports describe, whatever the trigger:

- **Control snaps back to the local machine.** When the machine being controlled has no connected socket, `SkSend` logs "No active connection found" and, once that has lasted about five seconds, hands control back to the local machine ([Common.cs:953-965][sk-fallback], [MachinePool.cs:101-127][disconnect-grace]).
- **Crossing the edge then does nothing, silently.** `PrepareToSwitchToMachine` cancels the switch when `IsConnectedTo` fails, and the tooltip that would say so is commented out ([Event.cs:171-177][cancel-switch]).
- **Recovery needs a new outbound connection.** That is `UpdateTCPClients` ([SocketStuff.cs:797-837][update-clients]). Cause 1 covers what triggers it, and cause 2 the most common reason the sockets go away.

## Causes with code references

### 1. Reconnection is event-driven and can stop

- **Symptom:** after sleep, lock, a network blip or a peer being off for a while, the machines stay disconnected until "Refresh connections" or a restart.
- **Reports:** #50583 (analysis), #49816, #50438, #30720, #26945, #38132, #33655, #31700, #45538. Closed but same family: #27389, #43285.
- **Code:**
  - The timer-driven retry in `HelperTimer_Tick` only runs while `PleaseReopenSocket` is positive. It is armed at start-up (9) and on a network availability change while the desktop is active (10), is decremented on each attempt (attempts are at least 30 seconds apart) and is set to 0 as soon as one socket is established ([frmScreen.cs:425-450][retry-loop], [InitAndCleanup.cs:138-140][init-retry]).
  - Every other reconnect is event-driven. `UpdateClientSockets` runs after a failed send, a failed test send, an incoming connection, certain received packages, a matrix change and once two seconds after each reopen. A machine that has no socket to its peer at all produces none of these on its own, because the periodic awake beat only writes to sockets that exist ([Common.cs:901-971][sk-send]).
  - `UpdateTCPClients` returns immediately while `InvalidKeyFound` is set ([SocketStuff.cs:797-837][update-clients]).
  - Each outbound attempt resolves the peer name again through `Dns.GetHostEntry`. If that fails and there is no IP mapping, no connection is attempted ([SocketStuff.cs:948-961][dns-resolve], [SocketStuff.cs:1047-1055][dns-fail]).
  - On a network availability change, `ScheduleReopenSocketsDueToNetworkChanges` closes all sockets and, if the desktop is not active (lock screen), sets `PleaseReopenSocket = 0` ([InitAndCleanup.cs:253-277][net-change]). The power-mode handler does not re-arm it ([InitAndCleanup.cs:144-154][power-mode]). This is the sequence described in #50583.
  - `NetworkAvailabilityChanged` is the only network event observed. Address changes (a new DHCP lease, a Wi-Fi roam, a VPN going up or down) are not.
  - A silent peer is detected late. Sockets set a 500 ms send timeout but no keep-alive and no receive timeout ([SocketStuff.cs:1283-1286][sock-opts]), and `IsAlive` treats a machine as alive while a test send on its socket does not throw, regardless of heartbeats ([MachinePool.cs:304-307][is-alive], [Common.cs:822-891][test-send]; `HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` is 1,500,000 ms at [MachineStuff.cs:32][heartbeat]).
- **Status:** code behaviour confirmed. Which of these paths each report hit is not confirmed.
- **Direction:** keep a low-rate periodic `UpdateTCPClients` for machines in the matrix that have no connection; re-arm on resume and on return to the desktop; add keep-alive or enforce the heartbeat timeout; show the "no active connection" message instead of cancelling silently; let "Refresh connections" in Settings signal the same reconnect event as the Dashboard (suggested in #50583).

### 2. Every desktop switch closes all connections

- **Symptom:** control is lost for several seconds around each User Account Control (UAC) prompt, lock or Ctrl+Alt+Del on either machine, and the cursor ends up back on the local machine.
- **Reports:** #40466, #26405, #46076, #26147.
- **Code:**
  - When the process's desktop is not the input desktop, `HelperTimer_Tick` closes every socket ([frmScreen.cs:322-353][desktop-close]) and reopens them on return ([frmScreen.cs:357-423][desktop-reopen]). A comment in `FlagReopenSocketIfNeeded` describes the same sequence ([SocketStuff.cs:1239-1255][flag-reopen]).
  - A reopen rebuilds everything. `ReopenSockets` closes and recreates both listeners and all connections on the UI thread, then stops and reinstalls the keyboard and mouse hooks ([Common.cs:1230-1289][reopen]).
  - In service mode two processes, one per desktop, hand the same ports back and forth. If a listener cannot bind (`WSAEADDRINUSE`), `TcpServer` retries for three seconds ([TcpServer.cs:46-96][tcp-server]). The `SocketStuff` constructor then sleeps ten seconds and, up to five times, kills the other MWB processes and restarts the service ([SocketStuff.cs:304-339][addr-in-use], [Program.cs:501-528][start-service]).
- **Status:** confirmed, and the first part is by design. Listed because it turns each prompt into a full reconnect cycle, and the port-conflict path can stretch that well beyond ten seconds. A comment on #49147 reports a bind retry repeating about every 12 seconds, which matches that path.
- **Direction:** keep connections across a desktop switch, or hand them over between the two processes without closing the listeners.

### 3. Network sends run inside the low-level mouse hook, one packet per mouse event

- **Symptom:** rubber-banding and lag with high polling-rate mice, and cursor stalls.
- **Reports:** #36878, #46504, #26949, #31539, #43769.
- **Code:** `MouseHookProc` calls `MouseEvent` synchronously ([InputHook.cs:205-334][hook-proc]). `Event.MouseEvent` builds a package for every event and calls `Common.SkSend` ([Event.cs:97-121][mouse-event]), which takes `TcpSocketsLock` and writes to the socket ([Common.cs:901-971][sk-send]) with a 500 ms send timeout. Move events are not coalesced, and the same lock is taken by every other sender (heartbeats, clipboard, test sends).
- **Why it matters:** a low-level hook callback has a deadline (`LowLevelHooksTimeout`, at most 1000 ms). Windows silently removes a hook that exceeds it, and the documentation recommends handing the work to another thread ([LowLevelMouseProc][ll-docs]). MWB only reinstalls its hooks as a side effect of `ReopenSockets` ([Common.cs:1270-1288][reopen-hooks], [frmInputCallback.cs:55-86][hook-install]); nothing checks whether a hook is still alive.
- **Status:** call chain confirmed.
- **Direction:** queue events to a sender thread; coalesce moves and cap the send rate (a limit is requested in #36878).

### 4. Service mode starts the process pair twice

- **Reports:** #44177. Closed as duplicate: #44065.
- **Code:** `Worker.StartAsync` calls `RunMeUnderSystemAccount` once and then, because `isLoggingOff` and `isByWindows` are constant `false`, always takes the `else` branch and calls it again ([Worker.cs:118-163][worker]). Each call starts one process for the default desktop and one for the Winlogon desktop ([Worker.cs:53-110][worker-pair]). The service is also restarted at run time by the port-conflict path in cause 2, so this is not limited to start-up.
- **Status:** confirmed. Two long-lived processes are the designed pair, so seeing two is not by itself the defect that #44177 describes; the extra launches are short-lived. Their effect on connection drops is not confirmed.
- **Direction:** remove the second call.

### 5. `settings.json` handling can lose settings

- **Symptom:** "being used by another process" errors in Event Viewer; the security key, device layout or other settings reset; "keys do not match" after a period of working.
- **Reports:** lock errors: #26537, #48708, #47039. Settings or key reset: #32342, #37996. Closed as duplicate: #33801.
- **Code:**
  - Reads use `ReadAllText` and writes use `WriteAllText` directly on the live file, with no temporary file and no cross-process coordination ([SettingsUtils.cs:187-231][utils-file]). MWB, the Settings app and, in service mode, a second MWB process all open the same file.
  - `SaveSettings` catches every exception and only logs it, so the caller cannot tell that a save failed. MWB's five-attempt retry loop waits for an `IOException` that therefore never arrives ([Setting.cs:154-191][setting-save]).
  - A failed read is logged and skipped, with no retry ([Setting.cs:59-144][setting-read]).
  - If the file cannot be parsed (empty or truncated after a failed write, for example on a full disk as in #37996), `GetSettingsOrDefault` writes a default settings object over it ([SettingsUtils.cs:92-116][utils-default]). The MWB defaults have an empty security key, an empty machine matrix and an empty machine pool ([MouseWithoutBordersProperties.cs:165-195][props-default]).
  - A watcher reloads the file on every change, and a different security key makes MWB reopen all sockets with it ([Setting.cs:193-210][setting-watch], [Setting.cs:112-123][setting-key]). A reset file therefore leads straight to a drop.
- **Status:** code behaviour confirmed. That this is what reset the settings in the linked reports is a hypothesis.
- **Direction:** write to a temporary file and replace; open with sharing and retry on read; keep a backup instead of overwriting an unparseable file with defaults; surface save failures. `SettingsUtils` is shared by all modules, so this is wider than MWB. #51080 is open for the first three.

### 6. Outbound connections race every address the name resolves to

- **Symptom:** MWB connects over the wrong adapter (Wi-Fi instead of Ethernet, a VPN adapter) or appears to ignore the IP mapping.
- **Reports:** #43841, #29619, #31578. Closed: #45139, #40764, #30005. Mapping ignored (see below): #43841, #43274, #35490.
- **Code:** `StartNewTcpClient` starts one connection thread per address: the mapped addresses if an IP mapping exists, and also every IPv4 and IPv6 address that DNS returns ([SocketStuff.cs:926-946][name2ip], [SocketStuff.cs:1035-1046][dns-all]). The first connection to finish its handshake wins and the others are closed ([SocketStuff.cs:1980-2004][keep-first], [SocketStuff.cs:1421-1428][dup-check]). An IP mapping therefore only adds a candidate; it does not select the adapter.
- **Mapping ignored:** a single-line IP mapping is never used. `StartNewTcpClient` joins the policy rules and the user's rules with `+ Separator +`, and `Separator` is a `string[]` ([SocketStuff.cs:904-907][name2ip-join], [SocketStuff.cs:1258][separator]), so C# inserts the text "System.String[]" between them and the first user rule's name never matches. With several lines only the first user rule is lost, and a policy list loses its last line. The block is skipped when there are no user rules, so policy rules are never used on their own. This dates from #33571 (July 2024). Fix: #51127. Workaround on current releases: put a throwaway first line such as `placeholder 0.0.0.0` above the real rules.
- **Status:** confirmed.
- **Direction:** treat an IP mapping as exclusive, or prefer it whenever it connects.

### 7. Different versions cannot pair, and the error blames the key

- **Symptom:** "keys do not match" or "invalid key" between machines on different PowerToys versions.
- **Reports:** #50295 (0.101.2362.0 with 0.100.x). Request to report version mismatch: #29794, open since 2023. #50116 was listed here at first; it has a more specific cause (cause 13).
- **Facts:** #48742 (per-connection salt and IV) and #49600 (PBKDF2 iterations raised from 50,000 to 100,000) changed the wire format and the derived key, and both state that all paired machines must run the same version. Both first shipped in 0.101.2362.0 (checked in `Encryption.cs` at the release tags), so 0.100.x and 0.101.x cannot pair. On unparseable packages the tooltip says "Ensure the security keys are the same in both machines" ([SocketStuff.cs:1336-1342][invalid-tooltip]).
- **Status:** confirmed.
- **Direction:** exchange a protocol version in the handshake and report a version mismatch explicitly.

### 8. Settings cannot talk to MWB in recent preview builds

- **Reports:** #50795 (0.101.2652.0 and 0.101.2684.0).
- **Code:** since #50480 the Settings app verifies the pipe server. If its own binary is signed, it rejects the peer unless both binaries carry the same signer certificate, compared byte for byte ([NamedPipePeerVerification.cs:257-265][pipe-signer], [NamedPipePeerVerification.cs:299-327][pipe-same]). The reporter shows that the shipped `PowerToys.Settings.exe` and MWB binaries are signed with different certificates.
- **Status:** the code condition is confirmed. The certificate difference is the reporter's finding.

### 9. Input is blocked or ignored depending on the foreground window

- **Symptom:** the cursor will not leave the machine while an elevated or full-screen window has focus. On the controlled machine the cursor moves but clicks do nothing on dialogs, pop-ups or elevated windows.
- **Reports:** #33346, #49178, #50617 (closed automatically; the author has since confirmed it on 0.101.2362.0), #49864, #50966, #43786, #36530, #45215, #36926, #41927.
- **Background:** User Interface Privilege Isolation (UIPI) stops a process from injecting input into a window of higher integrity, and `SendInput` reports no error when that happens ([SendInput][sendinput-docs]). Reports from the controlling side are consistent with the same isolation applying to MWB's hooks when PowerToys is not elevated.
- **Code:** on the controlled machine, move events go through `InputInjector.InjectMouseInput` while button, wheel and keyboard events go through `SendInput` ([InputSimulation.cs:51-106][send-input]). The two paths can therefore behave differently for the same target window, which matches "moves but cannot click".
- **Status:** the split is confirmed. Whether it explains the click reports needs confirmation. Some reporters state that running elevated or in service mode did not help (#49178, #46450, #43786).
- **Direction:** establish which of these are UIPI working as designed (and document "Use Service" as the remedy) and which are defects.

### 10. The clipboard listener is not restarted in place

- **Symptom:** clipboard sharing stops until PowerToys restarts. In #49147 each later copy also drops the connection.
- **Reports:** #49147 (analysis), #45825, #31230, #36141.
- **Code:** `AcceptConnectionAndSendClipboardData` leaves its accept loop on any accept failure ([SocketStuff.cs:1567-1631][accept-loop]) and is never restarted in place. A new listener is only created when `ReopenSockets` rebuilds the `SocketStuff` object ([SocketStuff.cs:475-495][create-socket], [Common.cs:1230-1289][reopen]). Separately, `MainTCPRoutine` closes the main socket after more than five unparseable packages ([SocketStuff.cs:1323-1365][err-count]).
- **Caveat:** the "Not listening" log line quoted in #49147 is also what the loop logs when the listener is stopped normally during a reopen, so on its own it does not show an abnormal failure.
- **Status:** loop behaviour confirmed. Whether it is what stops clipboard sharing in the reports is not confirmed; #49147 notes that restarting the helper process also restores it.
- **Direction:** restart the listener in place and log why it stopped.

### 11. Reported regression in 0.100.0

- **Reports:** #48551 (two commenters date frequent drops to the 0.100.0 update, and one confirms that 0.99.1 works on the same setup), #49816, #50438.
- **Facts:** between 0.99.1 and 0.100.0 only three commits touched `src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders`: the .NET 10 upgrade (#41280), a dependency clean-up (#47233) and a logger refactor (#44553). The refactor changes `LogDebug` from a method with an empty Release body to `[Conditional("DEBUG")]`, which should be behaviour-neutral unless a call site relied on its arguments being evaluated. That leaves the runtime change or changes in shared libraries.
- **Status:** unconfirmed. Needs a bisect by someone who can reproduce.

### 12. One mouse move the system refuses drops the connection

- **Symptom:** on the controlled machine the connection drops and comes back within seconds, again and again. #43292 ties it to the pointer reappearing after it was hidden, for example by "Hide pointer while typing" or over a video in a browser.
- **Reports:** #43292 (stack trace and trigger).
- **Code:** mouse moves on the controlled machine go through `InputInjector.InjectMouseInput` ([InputSimulation.cs:51-106][send-input]). When it throws, nothing catches the exception until the per-package `catch` in `MainTCPRoutine`, which marks the socket as failed, closes it and stops reading ([SocketStuff.cs:1540-1558][main-catch]). The exceptions seen are `COMException (0x8007007A)` and `UnauthorizedAccessException`.
- **Evidence:** on one pair of machines on 0.100.2, the controlled machine's log showed 20 drops in 28 minutes, each starting with this exception, while its network and power stayed steady. Turning off "Hide pointer while typing" did not stop the drops (three more in the next ten minutes, not checked against the log), and #43292 notes that WinUI and WebView2 apps hide the pointer regardless of that setting.
- **Status:** call chain confirmed, and confirmed as the cause of the drops on that setup.
- **Direction:** send a move the injector refuses through `SendInput`, which button, wheel and keyboard events already use. A fix with tests is on a branch ([3ebfda4][injector-fix]); its pull request will follow.

### 13. A key entered in the original window is switched back

- **Symptom:** "keys do not match" whatever key is entered; the original window later shows the previous key.
- **Reports:** #50116 (details in [this comment][key-revert-comment]).
- **Code:** OK in the original window changes only the key in memory ([frmMatrix.cs:506-522][ui-key]). The same click saves the machine layout, which writes `settings.json` with the old key ([frmMatrix.cs:103-104][ui-save]), and the settings watcher then switches the key in use back to the saved one ([Setting.cs:112-123][setting-key]). The setup wizard does the same ([SetupPage2a.cs:88-103][wizard-key]).
- **Status:** confirmed in code, from 0.100.2 to 0.102.2862.0. Fixed on main by #51305 (merged 2026-10-20), which saves the key in both places.
- **Direction:** until the fix ships, pair from the Mouse Without Borders page in PowerToys Settings, which saves the key ([Program.cs:304-340][settings-pair]).

### 14. Device tiles in Settings keep their last colour

- **Symptom:** a device tile stays orange (Connecting) or pink (Timeout) long after the attempt ended, so it looks as if MWB is still trying.
- **Code:** Settings polls the connection state every 500 ms and repaints only the machines in the reply ([MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs:512-533][tile-paint]). The reply lists the machines that have a client socket ([Program.cs:283-302][socket-state]), and a failed socket is removed at the next status update ([SocketStuff.cs:2006-2016][drop-failed]). A machine with no socket left, after a failed attempt is removed or after the sockets are rebuilt, is missing from the reply, so its tile keeps the last colour it was given.
- **Status:** confirmed in code.
- **Direction:** paint machines that are missing from the reply as not connected, and explain the colours (there is no legend, and the tooltip shows only the name).

### 15. In service mode, turning MWB off and on does not restart it

- **Symptom:** with "Use Service" on, turning Mouse Without Borders off and on in Settings does not clear a stuck state; restarting the machine does.
- **Code:** turning the module off ends the service and MWB processes by name ([dllmain.cpp:463-479][mwb-shutdown], [dllmain.cpp:536-552][mwb-disable]). In service mode those processes run as SYSTEM, and a PowerToys runner that is not elevated cannot open them for termination, so they keep running.
- **Evidence:** on the controlled machine of the setup in cause 12, the same SYSTEM process kept logging across an off and on toggle, and no new start was logged.
- **Status:** code path confirmed. Whether the runner was elevated on that machine was not checked.
- **Direction:** in service mode, ask the service to stop and restart its processes.

## Other clusters in brief

- **Cannot connect or pair (46):** mostly name resolution, subnets, firewall rules and key entry. Most specific: #47673 (non-ASCII device names), #39759 (name case), #50773 and #50760 (Connect page; #50776 is open for it), #31700, #29619.
- **Cursor, layout, multi-monitor (38):** #27450 (pointer speed differs across devices, the most upvoted bug), #33538, #27911, #27783 (move-relatively regression with a bisect), #30714.
- **Keyboard and shortcuts (28):** stuck or lost modifiers (#29803, #49149, #48314); AltGr and layout-specific characters (#48704, #31852, #35514); keyboard stops while the mouse works (#35255, #49282).
- **Service mode, lock and sign-in screen (21):** the service will not start or toggle (#27897, #32291, #49094); no control before the first sign-in (#50705, #40018, #29060).
- **Elevation and the layout editor (11):** PowerToys ends up elevated and the device layout cannot be edited (#50259, #50701, #48047); "Use Service" greyed out (#48137, #41228).
- **Crashes, freezes, system side effects (13):** whole-system freezes (#48362, #45471); network adapter problems (#47782, #42184, #30831); 16.8 GB of memory (#42183); display woken up (#36063).
- **Clipboard beyond cause 10:** rich text (#47828); Excel cells pasted as pictures (#49176); switching by hotkey does not carry the clipboard (#50829).

## Suggested order

- [ ] Keep retrying outbound connections for machines that have none, and say so when a crossing is cancelled (cause 1)
- [ ] Re-arm reconnection on resume and on return to the desktop (cause 1)
- [ ] Send a mouse move the injector refuses through `SendInput` instead of dropping the connection (cause 12; a fix is on a branch)
- [ ] Use single-line IP mappings, and policy mappings without user rules (cause 6, #51127)
- [ ] Remove the duplicate service launch (cause 4)
- [ ] Report a version mismatch explicitly (cause 7)
- [ ] Relax the signer comparison for the Settings pipe (cause 8)
- [ ] Make settings file reads and writes robust (cause 5, #51080)
- [ ] Keep connections across desktop switches, or hand them over without closing the listeners (cause 2)
- [ ] Move sends off the hook thread and coalesce moves (cause 3)
- [ ] Treat IP mappings as exclusive (cause 6)
- [ ] Sort the "blocked by the foreground window" reports into by-design and defect (cause 9)
- [ ] Restart the clipboard listener in place (cause 10)
- [ ] Paint device tiles that are missing from the status reply, and explain the colours (cause 14)
- [ ] Restart the service-mode processes when the module is turned off and on (cause 15)
- [x] Save a key entered in the original window (cause 13, #51305)

title: Cannot reassign "Shortcut to toggle Easy Mouse" after using "Clear"
body: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel v0.101.2362 ### Installation method GitHub ### Area(s) with issue? Mouse Without Borders ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open PowerToys Settings and go to Mouse Without Borders. 2. Set a shortcut for Shortcut to toggle Easy Mouse. 3. Verify that the shortcut works correctly. 4. Click the pencil icon to edit the shortcut. 5. Click the ✕ Clear button. 6. The shortcut is successfully cleared and becomes unassigned. 7. Try to assign a new shortcut by pressing a valid key combination, such as Ctrl+Alt+M, Shift+M, or another supported combination. 8. The shortcut editor does not detect or accept any key input, and the shortcut cannot be assigned again. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior After using ✕ Clear, the shortcut should become unassigned, but the shortcut editor should continue to accept keyboard input so that a new shortcut can be assigned. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The ✕ Clear operation itself works correctly and removes the existing shortcut. However, after clearing the shortcut, the shortcut editor stops accepting all keyboard input. No key combination is detected, including combinations using Win, Shift, Ctrl, or Alt. The shortcut cannot be assigned again through the settings UI. This issue occurs only when an existing shortcut is cleared using ✕ Clear. The following operations continue to work normally: - Assigning a shortcut to a field that was originally unassigned. - Changing an existing shortcut directly to another shortcut without using ✕ Clear first. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file [PowerToysReport_2026-10-07-15-17-07.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33141399/PowerToysReport_2026-10-07-15-17-07.zip) ### Additional Information - Windows display language: Japanese - Keyboard layout: US keyboard - The shortcut worked normally before it was cleared. - The issue appears specifically after using the ✕ Clear button. ### Other Software _No response_

title: [New PowerToy] Automatic Japanese IME on/off based on what is being typed (romaji vs. English words)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

A module that watches typing and automatically switches the Japanese IME between Japanese input (hiragana) and direct English input, so the user never has to press 半角/全角 (Hankaku/Zenkaku) or 英数/かな.

- While the user types in romaji (e.g. "kyouha"), the text is composed as Japanese ("今日は").
- When the typed sequence is clearly an English word or code-like token (e.g. "GitHub", "push", "npm install", "localhost"), it is committed as-is in half-width alphanumerics.
- Mixed sentences such as "今日は GitHub に push した" can be typed without any manual mode switching.
- Optional: insert a half-width space around English words (configurable, off by default).
- Per-app exclusion list and an easy toggle, like other PowerToys modules.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Japanese developers and office workers constantly mix Japanese and English terms (product names, commands, code identifiers). Today they must toggle the IME mode many times per sentence, and frequently end up with output like "ぷsh" or "ｇいてゅｂ" and have to retype it.

This is especially common in chat tools, commit messages, issue trackers and AI assistant prompts.

### Supporting information

- Related but different requests: #14850 and #47427 (manual conversion between keyboard layouts, not IME mode detection), #33774 (key mappings per IME).
- Third-party open-source tools that do this already exist, but because such a tool must read all keystrokes system-wide, many users (and corporate IT policies) are only comfortable using it if it is a signed, first-party Microsoft component. This is the main reason for asking for it in PowerToys or in Microsoft IME itself.

title: Advanced Paste: OpenAI /v1/moderations returns HTTP 403 while inline moderation succeeds
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

Microsoft PowerToys version: 0.101.2522 Release channel: Stable

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Advanced Paste

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PowerToys 0.101.2522 from the Microsoft Store.
2. Open PowerToys Settings > Advanced Paste.
3. Configure the OpenAI provider and select the gpt-4o model.
4. Copy some text to the clipboard.
5. Open Advanced Paste and select an AI Paste action.
6. The AI Paste operation fails with the following error:

   "OpenAI request failed with status code: 403"

I independently tested the same OpenAI API key and Project outside PowerToys.

The results were:

- POST /v1/moderations → HTTP 403 Forbidden
- POST /v1/chat/completions → HTTP 200 OK
- POST /v1/chat/completions with inline moderation
  (moderation.model = "omni-moderation-latest") → HTTP 200 OK

The inline moderation request returned valid moderation results using omni-moderation-latest.


### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Advanced Paste should successfully perform the requested AI action when the OpenAI API key, Project, and model are valid and the required moderation functionality is available.

In particular, Advanced Paste should not fail solely because the direct /v1/moderations endpoint returns HTTP 403 when inline moderation through Chat Completions or Responses succeeds with the same API key and Project.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Advanced Paste fails with the following error:

"OpenAI request failed with status code: 403"

I investigated the OpenAI API independently using the same API key and the same Project.

The results are:

- POST /v1/moderations → HTTP 403 Forbidden
- POST /v1/chat/completions → HTTP 200 OK
- POST /v1/chat/completions with:
  {"moderation":{"model":"omni-moderation-latest"}}
  → HTTP 200 OK

The successful inline moderation request returned valid moderation results for both the input and output, using omni-moderation-latest.

This indicates that omni-moderation-latest itself is available and working, while the direct /v1/moderations endpoint returns 403.

PowerToys Advanced Paste v0.101.2522 uses PromptModerationService, which directly calls /v1/moderations with omni-moderation-latest. As a result, this endpoint-specific 403 prevents AI Paste from working.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OpenAI Support was contacted about this issue.

They confirmed that omni-moderation-latest itself is available, and recommended sharing this issue with the PowerToys developers because PowerToys currently calls the /v1/moderations endpoint directly.

The important distinction is:

- Direct /v1/moderations → HTTP 403 Forbidden
- Chat Completions → HTTP 200 OK
- Chat Completions + inline moderation using omni-moderation-latest → HTTP 200 OK

The successful inline moderation request returned moderation results for both input and output.

Request ID for the successful inline moderation request:
req_a13942a3cc5d4571a3dc07a26c66ca68

Based on the PowerToys source code, PromptModerationService directly uses omni-moderation-latest through /v1/moderations.

Therefore, I would like to ask whether PowerToys could support inline moderation through Chat Completions or Responses instead of relying exclusively on the direct /v1/moderations endpoint.

No API key or other credentials are included in this report.

### Other Software

OpenAI API

title: Keyboard Manager - Device-specific remapping
body: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement Bind the key remaps to a specific keyboard-device, or provide flag to use the remap only for internal (laptop) keyboards. Alternatively, provide some sort of switchable "profiles" so user can create different remaps and switch between them ad-hoc. ### Scenario when this would be used? I have Dell Pro 14 Plus laptop where F11 and F12 keys sharing the same physical keys with Home and End (F11/Home, F12/End). By default Function keys are used w/o the FN key (as i use them often) but I use Home/End more often than F11/F12, so i created keyboard remaps where F11 -> Home and Home -> F11, same for F12<->End to be able to use Home/End without FN key. This works flawlessly until I connect my laptop to external keyboard, which has separated keys for F11/12 and Home/End. Here suddenly the remapping is contra-productive as pressing F11 sends Home and pressing Home sends F11. The desired state is to have the remap only active if either no external keyboard is connected OR if the button is pressed on a specific (internal) keyboard (not sure if this is even possible to distinguish which KB device sent the key-press?) ### Supporting information _No response_

title: Shift + shake to merge File Explorer windows into tabs
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I'd like to hold Shift while dragging and shaking a File Explorer window by its title bar to bring all open File Explorer windows into that window as tabs.

Any existing tabs in the other windows should come across too. The window being shaken should stay active, with its current tab still selected.

It would work like the familiar window shake gesture, but holding Shift would merge Explorer windows instead of minimising other windows. A configurable keyboard shortcut for the same action would also be useful.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I often end up with several File Explorer windows open while working across different folders. Once things get cluttered, I'd like to gather them into one window without dragging each tab across individually.

Holding Shift and shaking the window I want to keep would be a quick, easy way to tidy things up while keeping all my folders open.

### Supporting information

The idea builds on the existing title bar shake gesture, so it would feel familiar. Holding Shift makes it a deliberate action and keeps it separate from the normal shake behaviour.

This could be an optional PowerToys feature, with settings to enable the gesture and choose a keyboard shortcut.

title: CmdPal-Dock Remember monitor settings for each monitor setup
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

For the CmdPal-Dock, ensure that when switching between monitor setups, that the settings for each monitor are remembered per setup.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When working directly on a desktop, I have 3 monitors available, but when working remotely via RDP, I only have two monitors available. It would be helpful if the CmdPal-Dock settings remembered which monitor to display the dock on in each of any number of setups.

title: CmdPal-Dock: Option to mirror docks across multiple monitors
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Rather than have separate instances of the CmdPal-Dock on each monitor, allow the option to duplicate / mirror one dock on one or more other monitors. Add an option when selecting each monitor if it should mirror another monitor and specify which other monitor. Mirroring would then inherit the same position and settings of the source monitor.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Sometimes it helps just to have quick access to a few things, but if I have to move the mouse way over the otherside of my screen to get to a dock on a different monitor, then that is no longer quick. Sure I can duplicate a dock manually, but then any changes have to be duplicated as well.

### Supporting information

Example useage:
+ Monitor 1 (Primary) has the dock defined
+ Monitors 2 & 3 both mirror Monitor 1
+ Monitor 4 has it's own dock
+ Monitor 5 has no dock
+ Monitor 6 mirrors Monitor 4

title: CmdPal Dock clock drifts behind system time (per-minute timer never re-aligns)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the Clock band in the Command Palette Dock (seconds off, i.e. per-minute cadence).
2. Leave Command Palette running for a few days (here: started 2026-10-03 10:50, observed 2026-10-06 00:48, ~2.6 days).
3. Compare the dock clock with the taskbar clock / `Get-Date` around a minute change.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The dock clock flips to the new minute together with the system clock.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The dock clock lags behind by up to ~50 seconds. Screenshots of the dock taken with timestamps:

| System time | Dock shows |
|---|---|
| 00:48:49 | 00:47 |
| 00:49:21 | 00:48 |
| 00:49:41 | 00:48 |
| 00:50:01 | 00:49 |
| 00:50:21 | 00:49 |

So the dock now updates somewhere around second ~50 of each minute instead of at second 0. The system time itself is correct (w32tm last sync 00:47:33 against time.windows.com).

This is not the same as #46192: the fix from #48253 (9449ae3) is included in 0.101.2362.0.

### Likely cause

`NowDockBand.ConfigureTimer()` aligns only the **first** tick to the minute boundary. `Timer_ElapsedFirstMinuteTick` then switches to a fixed `Interval = 60000` with `AutoReset = true` and never re-aligns. `System.Timers.Timer` does not keep phase: each tick lands a few ms late (timer resolution, thread-pool scheduling), and the error accumulates. Over ~3,800 ticks (2.6 days), ~13 ms per tick already adds up to the ~50 s observed. Sleep/resume and system time changes would shift the phase further, and nothing corrects it afterwards.

### Suggested fix

Recompute the interval to the next minute boundary on every tick instead of using a fixed 60 s interval, e.g.:

```csharp
private void Timer_Elapsed(object? sender, ElapsedEventArgs e)
{
    UpdateText();
    if (!_timeWithSeconds)
    {
        var now = _clock();
        _timer.Interval = 60_000 - ((now.Second * 1000) + now.Millisecond) + 50; // small margin past the boundary
    }
}
```

Optionally also call `UpdateText()` plus re-align on `SystemEvents.TimeChanged` and on resume (`PowerModeChanged`/`Resume`).

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_Not attached_

### Additional Information

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, laptop. Command Palette process uptime at observation time: ~2.6 days.

### Other Software

_No response_

title: FancyZones: Hyper-V Virtual Machine Connection guest resolution doesn't follow the zone size
body: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362 stable ### Installation method WinGet ### Area(s) with issue? FancyZones ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run PowerToys as administrator. VMConnect's process is elevated, so FancyZones doesn't drag it otherwise 2. Connect to a Hyper-V VM (Windows 11 guest) with Virtual Machine Connection (vmconnect.exe) in an enhanced session. In this mode, resizing the window by dragging its border changes the guest resolution to fit the window. 3. Shift+drag the VMConnect window into a FancyZones zone whose size differs from the current window size. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The guest resolution changes to fill the window, the same as after resizing the window by its border or snapping it with Windows Snap (dragging it to a screen edge). ### ❌ Actual Behavior The window is resized to the zone, but the guest keeps its previous resolution. If the zone is larger than the window was, the rest of the window stays empty (white). If it is smaller, the guest display is cut off. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information - OS: Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, build 26200 - Running as admin: Yes This was reported before in #4336, which was closed as Resolution-External, and in #10827, which was closed as a duplicate. Hyper-V Connection is still listed under [Applications that can't be zoned](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/powertoys/fancyzones#applications-that-cant-be-zoned) in the FancyZones docs. The last comment on #9040 describes the same symptom. The cause is the order of window messages, and FancyZones can fix it on its side. **What happens** - In an enhanced session, VMConnect applies a new window size to the guest only when a move/size loop ends (`WM_EXITSIZEMOVE`), and only if the client size changed since the loop started (`WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE`). A resize outside a move/size loop only re-lays out VMConnect's own menu and status bar. The guest display keeps its size, which leaves the empty area. - Windows Snap by mouse works because Windows applies the snap rectangle before the drag's move/size loop ends. VMConnect sees `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE`, then the size change, then `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE`. - FancyZones snaps only after the loop has ended. It learns about the drop from `EVENT_SYSTEM_MOVESIZEEND` and then calls `SetWindowPlacement`. By then VMConnect has already handled `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` with an unchanged size. - Windows' own snapping from the Snap Layouts flyout (hovering the maximize button) has the same problem, because it doesn't involve a move/size loop either. **How I confirmed it** I resized the VMConnect window from a script: - `SetWindowPos` alone: the window is resized, the guest resolution doesn't change. This is the same result as with FancyZones. - The same `SetWindowPos` with `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE` sent before and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` sent after it: the guest resolution follows the window. **Proposed fix** When a snap ends a mouse drag, FancyZones sends `WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE` before and `WM_EXITSIZEMOVE` after applying the zone, so the app sees the same sequence as with Windows Snap. I tested this with a Hyper-V VM and will open a PR. **Note on elevation** On my machine VMConnect's process token is elevated (at medium integrity level). FancyZones checks token elevation, so it only drags VMConnect when PowerToys runs as administrator. Otherwise it shows the "can't drag elevated window" notification. ### Other Software Hyper-V Virtual Machine Connection (vmconnect.exe) 10.0.26100.9278, enhanced session, Windows 11 guest

title: Several modules are forcibly re-enabled on every restart/logon
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362 stable

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

General

### Steps to reproduce

I don't know how to describe the reproduction well, but my setup is the following:

- Enabled: Find My Mouse, Colour Picker, Screen Ruler, Shortcut Guide, Always On Top, File Explorer Addons, File Locksmith
- Crucially **disabled**: Awake, Command Palette, Mouse Highlighter
- Rest of modules are disabled as well unless they've been added since I last went through all of them some versions back

Every single time I logout of my user account and/or (re)start my system, the three modules highlighted above as absolutely **disabled** show up again. I don't know 100% that it's _just_ those three but those three are extremely noticeable (Awake and Command Palette have tray icons & Mouse Highlighter is very annoying with its yellow circles on *every click*).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Modules I disabled stay disabled

### ❌ Actual Behavior

At least Awake, Command Palette, and Mouse Highlighter re-enable themselves forcibly on every relog/restart.

There may be more modules exhibiting this behaviour but those aren't as intrusively obviously enabled.
