title: CmdPal: Icons (13/n) - Add smooth dynamic icon updates
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Support smooth updates to list-item icons without a visible flash between frames.

Keep the current icon visible while its replacement loads, then display the new image when ready. A newer update should not have to wait for an earlier load to finish, and late results should never overwrite a newer displayed frame.

The behavior should also preserve icons during theme changes while correctly handling cleared icons, failed loads, and rows recycled for different items.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Currently, these updates can cause visible flashing. Smooth replacement would make progress indicators and other frequently updated status icons easier to follow.

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: CmdPal: Split disk usage dock band
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Disk usage is a big fat dock band forcing 3 items (Read, Write and Active Time) and wasting space on the dock.

Split it into separate dock bands so user can choose what they want to see

### Scenario when this would be used?

UX

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: Creating keyboard keypress + mouse key or wheel action in the Keyboard Manager
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The Keyboard Manager is missing a great opportunity by not supporting mouse actions alongside keyboard keypresses. E.g., when I press "V" on my keyboard with my left hand and rotate my mouse wheel with my right hand, it could be mapped to change the sound volume. This would open a plethora of new opportunities.

### Scenario when this would be used?

The combo keyboard keypress + mouse wheel or key action could be mapped to anything the Keyboard Manager already maps to. E.g., a keyboard shortcut + mouse left-click could launch an application, etc.

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: [FancyZones] Resize a window by dragging a single edge, snapping that edge to a zone boundary
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

While resizing a window by one of its edges (or a corner), snap the dragged edge to the nearest zone boundary of the active FancyZones layout when the mouse button is released. Only the edge being dragged moves. The other edges stay where they are. No other windows or zones are resized.

Original request https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/9146 incorrectly marked as duplicate.

This is **not** asking for:

- any other windows be resized
- any zones be resized or modified
- snapping to other windows
- snapping to to screen edges

Existing unrelated issues:

- https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/254
- https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/8

### Scenario when this would be used?

Manually resizing windows

### Supporting information

Original request and discussion: 

- #9146

The interaction described above was clarified in that thread, including feidaman's comment that only the dragged border should snap and that the nearest boundary line should be highlighted.
Related:

- #22057
- #1557

title: TextExtractor intermittently misrecognizes lowercase “k” in Czech text
body: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel v0.101.2712.0 ### Installation method Microsoft Store ### Area(s) with issue? TextExtractor ### Steps to reproduce I use PowerToys Text Extractor with Czech-language text. Display the original Czech text containing for example “Masarykova univerzita”. Activate Text Extractor and select the text. Paste the extracted text into a text editor and compare it with the original. The "k" is generated like "l<" ina many cases. The issue is intermittent and may not occur on every attempt, but it is very often with a blue background, white font. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The lowercase letter “k” should be recognized correctly. The expected text is: Masarykova univerzita ### ❌ Actual Behavior The lowercase letter “k” is frequently recognized incorrectly. In this example, the “k” in “Masarykova” was replaced with the two characters “l<”, producing: Masaryl

Reliability

title: Adding an App Hopper
body:
### __Description of the new feature / enhancement__

While the new **Window Hopper** tool is great, I really wouldn't mind having the opposite of it as well: an **App Hopper**.

Pressing a shortcut would make you **switch focus from the currently-active program to the other programs**, sorted by most recently active. It would work like alt-tab or Window Hopper when the shortcut is pressed. 

If the hopped-to program had several windows then it would default to focusing on the most recently-used window.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When I'm switching between several browser windows and now suddenly want to go to Discord without having to press alt-tab 5 times. But there can be MANY use case scenarios.

### Supporting information

Maybe it could be called the Program Hopper. 

Importantly, this **shouldn't be a new PowerToy** but both the Window Hopper and this App Hopper should be **combined into one single "Hopper" PowerToy**. There you could set all the settings for both Window Hopper and for App Hopper, **including** setting each of them on/off independently. 

There should be an off-by-default option to only show program icons and not previews of the window that will be selected when you're App Hopping.

title: Adicionar Agrupamento em Abas com Funcionalidade Nativa de Tela Dividida
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

A funcionalidade proposta usaria como referência o comportamento do software "Groupy 2", que permite arrastar e agrupar janelas do Windows em separadores (tabs) num único bloco principal. No entanto, o PowerToys expandiria essa referência adicionando um recurso fundamental que o Groupy 2 não possui: a capacidade de dividir a área de visualização dentro desse mesmo grupo. O utilizador poderia pegar numa aba e fixá-la lado a lado com outra dentro da mesma janela contêiner. O comportamento esperado é que os comandos da janela principal (minimizar, maximizar, restaurar e mover) controlem todo o grupo em simultâneo. Se houver duas janelas divididas lado a lado neste grupo, clicar em minimizar recolheria ambas com um único clique. #

### Scenario when this would be used?

Para utilizadores avançados, a gestão individual de janelas exige cliques excessivos e quebra a produtividade. Um cenário prático é para operações de mercado "Traders" em cenário de múltiplas contas é necessário manter duas ou mais instancias do Profit ou MetaTrader abertas lado a lado. Atualmente, o Windows obriga a minimizar cada gráfico de forma independente. Com este recurso, seria possível agrupar os terminais na mesma janela (como no Groupy 2), dividi-los lado a lado para visualização simultânea e, ao precisar limpar a área de trabalho, minimizar todas as plataformas como se fossem um único programa. 

Claro isso se aplica a multiplanos cenários, imagine varias arquivos de planilhas diferentes para agrupadas podendo alterna-las entre abas. 
[https://1drv.ms/v/c/fd0b5146bb1c804b/IQBCpba7bJWBRpTH3acv2o8_AfOIudUJlDBQSdNOjzz8w0o?e=mZ5aEa]

Tentei anexar o vídeo mas falhou. 

### Supporting information

A referência principal de usabilidade em abas é o "Groupy 2" da Stardock, que prova a enorme utilidade de agrupar janelas no Windows, mas falha por não permitir visualizar duas abas simultaneamente na mesma tela. A referência para a divisão interna seria o navegador Microsoft Edge, que introduziu o recurso "Tela dividida" (Split screen), permitindo colocar duas páginas lado a lado dentro da mesma janela de forma nativa. Unir a mecânica de abas do Groupy 2 com a divisão de tela do Edge a nível do sistema operativo seria uma inovação indispensável para a produtividade no Windows.

title: [Keyboard Manager] Backup/restore omits editorSettings.json, leaving new editor settings stale
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 — Stable; new WinUI 3 editor enabled (useNewEditor: true). Restored backup manifest: v0.100.2.

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager, Settings

### Steps to reproduce

Installation details: machine-wide installation under `C:\Program Files\PowerToys`, installed from [GitHub release v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/tag/v0.101.2362.0). Version/channel and installation details match my existing report #50933.

**Observed restore scenario:**

1. The destination PC already has a new Keyboard Manager editor configuration in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\Keyboard Manager\editorSettings.json`, with `useNewEditor: true`.
2. Restore a PowerToys backup whose global Open app shortcut has different Chrome arguments and launch options from that existing editor configuration.
3. PowerToys restores `Keyboard Manager\default.json` and restarts.
4. Compare the restored runtime shortcut with the same global shortcut in `editorSettings.json`.

For the global left Ctrl + left Shift + N shortcut, the observed post-restore values were:

| Setting | Restored runtime `default.json` | Existing `editorSettings.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome arguments | `--profile-directory="Profile Local" https://www.google.com/` | `--profile-directory="LocalProfile" https://www.google.com/` |
| Already running | `runProgramAlreadyRunningAction: 1` (Start another) | `IfRunningAction: 0` (Show window) |
| Window visibility | `runProgramStartWindowType: 3` (Maximized) | `Visibility: 0` (Normal) |

The restore log specifically records `Keyboard Manager\default.json` being updated from backup. The Keyboard Manager engine subsequently logged launching Chrome with the restored `Profile Local` arguments, confirming that the **runtime restore succeeded**.

The extracted backup manifest lists `default.json` but does not list `editorSettings.json`. The existing editor file retained its older save timestamp and values.

**Deterministic filter test, run separately without changing live settings:**

The installed `WinUI3Apps\backup_restore_settings.json` includes `*Keyboard Manager\default.json` and generic `*settings.json`, but no explicit pattern for `editorSettings.json`.

This PowerShell test uses the same wildcard-to-regex conversion as the backup implementation:

```powershell
$path = 'C:\Example\Microsoft\PowerToys\Keyboard Manager\editorSettings.json'
$regex = '^' + [regex]::Escape('*settings.json').Replace('\*', '.*') + '$'
[regex]::IsMatch($path, $regex) # False
[regex]::IsMatch($path, $regex, [System.Text.RegularExpressions.RegexOptions]::IgnoreCase) # True
```

Testing that path against **every installed include pattern** also returned no match.

The actual restore and saved-file mismatch were inspected. A separate clean-install UI reproduction and a save-from-stale-editor overwrite test were not performed.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

After restoring a backup, the new Keyboard Manager editor should agree with the restored runtime mappings and launch options.

Backup/restore should either preserve the required new editor state or reliably reconcile existing editor state with the restored runtime configuration.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The runtime settings restore successfully, while the separate persisted new editor settings remain stale. This leaves two conflicting saved representations of the same shortcut and creates a risk that a subsequent editor save could restore old values. That overwrite risk has not been tested in this report.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToys-KeyboardManager-backup-sanitized-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32935374/PowerToys-KeyboardManager-backup-sanitized-evidence.zip)

### Additional Information

- Windows 11 Home, 26H2, OS build **26300.9550**, 64-bit.
- New editor enabled: `useNewEditor: true`.
- Inspection and filter test performed October 1, 2026.
- Workaround used: with editors closed, back up both files and correct only the affected shortcut's arguments and launch options in both saved representations. Unrelated mappings were preserved.
- Attached a focused, sanitized evidence ZIP containing the pre-fix affected-shortcut fields, relevant official-report log excerpts, and installed backup include filters. This is not the complete unmodified bug-report ZIP. The official report was generated after the workaround; pre-fix values come from preserved originals. Unrelated settings, personal paths, and system inventories were omitted.

**Likely cause:**

1. [Backup include rules in v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/backup_restore_settings.json) omit an explicit `editorSettings.json` pattern. The same rules are present in v0.100.2.
2. [IsIncludeFile / GetSettingsFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/SettingsBackupAndRestoreUtils.cs#L526-L567) use `Regex.IsMatch` without `IgnoreCase`. The capital **S** in `editorSettings.json` therefore prevents a match with lowercase `*settings.json`.
3. [SettingsManager.LoadSettings in the installed release](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Settings/SettingsManager.cs#L50-L75) imports native mappings when the editor file does not exist, but reads the existing editor file when it is present.

The filter omission is reproduced directly; the explanation of how it causes the stale editor state follows from the inspected files and release source.

Please consider explicitly including the editor file with suitable restore semantics, and/or reconciling editor state after a runtime configuration restore. Merely creating another standard backup still excludes the editor file under these rules.

### Other Software

Google Chrome (used for the Open app shortcut).

title: Keyboard Manager incorrectly flags global and app specific shortcut remaps as duplicates
body: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.101.2362.0 — Stable; new WinUI 3 editor enabled (useNewEditor: true) ### Installation method GitHub — installed from [GitHub release v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/releases/tag/v0.101.2362.0). ### Area(s) with issue? Keyboard Manager ### Steps to reproduce Installation details: machine-wide installation under C:\Program Files\PowerToys; installed from the GitHub release linked above. An existing configuration has three mappings with the trigger Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Left) + N (162;160;78): | Scope | Action | | --- | --- | | Global | Open Chrome | | code.exe | Remap to Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Right) + N | | parsecd.exe | Remap to Ctrl (Left) + Shift (Right) + N | 1. Open this existing configuration in the new Keyboard Manager editor. 2. Edit the global Open app mapping. 3. Keep the trigger unchanged and leave Only apply to a specific app unchecked. 4. Observe the Duplicate remapping validation error. The observed screenshot shows the error in Edit remapping, with Allow chords checked. This configuration previously worked; the exact last working version is unknown. Suggested minimal reproduction: one global shortcut mapping and one app-specific override of the same trigger, then edit the global mapping. This reduced two-entry case has not been tested separately. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior Allow a global shortcut mapping and app-specific overrides with the same trigger. In a matching app, the app-specific mapping should take precedence; elsewhere, the global mapping should apply. This behavior is described in the [Keyboard Manager engine documentation](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/doc/devdocs/modules/keyboardmanager/keyboardmanager.md): app-specific shortcut handling runs before global shortcut handling so the app-specific variant takes precedence. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The editor displays: > Duplicate remapping — This key or shortcut is already remapped. There is exactly one mapping per scope for this trigger. Both default.json and editorSettings.json confirm these distinct scopes; all three editor entries are active. ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information Windows 11 Home, 26H2, build 26300.9550, 64-bit. Machine-wide installation under C:\Program Files\PowerToys; installed from GitHub release v0.101.2362.0. Evidence: user-supplied screenshot and read-only inspection of the current configuration. No mappings were changed during investigation. No separate runtime test or preview-version test was performed. **Likely cause:** [ValidationHelper.IsDuplicateMapping in v0.101.2362.0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2362.0/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs#L202-L209) uses this app-scope predicate: ```csharp string.IsNullOrEmpty(settings.Shortcut.TargetApp) || string.IsNullOrEmpty(appName) || settings.Shortcut.TargetApp == appName ``` When editing a global mapping, appName is empty, so matching triggers from every app scope count as duplicates. Here, the count is three and exceeds the edit-mode tolerance of one. **Existing reports and fixes checked:** #48749 concerns entries being duplicated on save, rather than this global/app-scope false positive. #49710 was closed by merged PR #50265, which changes edit-mode identity exclusion and filters inactive entries. However, [the current main-branch implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs#L209-L225) still has the same empty-app OR predicate. That related fix does not address this scope comparison. Suggested correction: compare normalized application scopes for duplicate detection, preserving global mappings and app-specific overrides as distinct while rejecting duplicate triggers within the same scope. Relevant configuration excerpt (optional launch arguments omitted): ```json { "remapShortcuts": { "global": [{ "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 1, "runProgramFilePath": "C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe" }], "appSpecific": [ { "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "newRemapKeys": "162;161;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 0, "targetApp": "code.exe" }, { "originalKeys": "162;160;78", "newRemapKeys": "162;161;78", "exactMatch": false, "operationType": 0, "targetApp": "parsecd.exe" } ] } } ``` ### Other Software Google Chrome, Visual Studio Code (code.exe), and Parsec (parsecd.exe). Their versions were not collected; the observed failure is editor validation. ### Screenshot

title: Workspaces: launch automatically at Windows sign-in, with configurable start delay
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Workspaces can already start a group of apps with saved position, size, window state (e.g. maximized), CLI arguments and admin rights. What is missing is a way to start a workspace automatically at Windows sign-in, with a start delay.

Proposal:

1. A per-workspace option "Launch at sign-in" (e.g. next to "Create desktop shortcut" / "Move existing windows").
2. A configurable start delay, either per workspace (e.g. 0 s, 30 s, 1 min, 5 min) or, ideally, per app within the workspace, so that apps start staggered instead of all at once.
3. Optional: an option to start the apps one after another with a fixed interval.

The existing per-app data model (position, state, arguments) would only need one additional field, "delay".

### Scenario when this would be used?

After sign-in, many programs (cloud sync, mail client, messengers, backup tools, CAD/slicer software, music player) start at the same time and compete for disk, CPU and network. The system stays sluggish for minutes, and windows end up in random places.

With Workspaces I can already define where each app should be placed and in which state. But I still have to start the workspace manually after every login. Windows itself offers no good alternative:

- Settings > Apps > Startup and shell:startup only allow enabling/disabling, there is no per-app delay.
- The "Run: minimized/maximized" setting of a shortcut is ignored by many apps.
- The only workaround is a Task Scheduler task (trigger "At log on" + "Delay task for") that launches the Workspaces desktop shortcut. That works, but it is a manual, fragile setup outside of PowerToys and has to be maintained separately for every workspace.

Built-in autostart with delay would make Workspaces a complete replacement for startup scripts: the desktop is usable right after login, the load is spread out, and every app ends up where it belongs.

### Supporting information

Current workaround: create the desktop shortcut for the workspace, then use Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) with trigger "At log on" and "Delay task for" (advanced settings), action = start the shortcut.

Third-party tools such as Startup Delayer offer per-app delays, but they know nothing about Workspaces layouts.

title: CmdPal: discuss driver dependencies for CPU temperature monitoring
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like to add CPU package/core temperature to Command Palette's Performance Monitor after the GPU temperature work in #50915. Before starting that implementation, I would like to discuss whether the required driver or SDK dependencies would be acceptable for PowerToys.

The GPU implementation uses Windows' D3DKMT/WDDM interface and does not require an additional vendor driver or SDK. CPU package/core temperature needs a different approach: I expect it to require vendor-specific hardware access and a supporting driver or SDK dependency. For example, [Intel PCM uses an MSR kernel driver on Windows](https://github.com/intel/pcm/blob/master/doc/WINDOWS_HOWTO.md).

Would a vendor-specific driver or SDK dependency be acceptable for a separate CPU temperature implementation? If so, is there a preferred approach or existing dependency I should use, and any requirements around driver distribution, signing, or administrator privileges?

I have not selected a dependency yet. I would appreciate maintainer guidance here before proceeding with that work.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Users could check CPU package/core temperature alongside the existing performance metrics while running CPU-intensive workloads.

This should report an actual CPU sensor reading. ACPI thermal-zone readings cannot reliably be presented as CPU temperature, as discussed in the review of #48639.

### Supporting information

- #46434 tracks the broader request for temperature readings.
- #48639 attempted an ACPI thermal-zone implementation and was closed without merging.
- #50915 implements GPU temperature through D3DKMT.

This issue is specifically for the CPU implementation and dependency discussion. Please continue that discussion here so the GPU PR can remain focused on its existing scope.

title: Shortcut/s to change profiles in Power Display
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

It would be helpful to be able to select a predetermined display profile with a quick shortcut—whether with a unique shortcut for each profile or with just one shortcut to cycle through profiles and stop at a desired one. This is separate logic from having shortcuts to change different settings for each display (existing issue). As I understand it, it's a more complex task with many variables. But switching profiles doesn't directly connect shortcuts to display settings—just to different menu items in the flyout. Presumably, profile shortcuts could be implemented faster and more easily than display settings shortcuts. Also, when selecting a profile with a shortcut, it's worth popping up the flyout and having the newly selected profile name visible—to know which profile was selected. 

P.S. Visibility of a selected profile name near the profile select menu icon in the flyout has a separate issue ( #50864 ).

### Scenario when this would be used?

I have two displays and 5 different profiles depending on the time of day and light conditions. Each time, I have to do many clicks or key presses to get to the profile-changing menu. It'd be helpful to have something simpler, like one shortcut to switch profiles.

title: [Keyboard Manager] Remapped/disabled shortcut is bypassed when additional keys are pressed simultaneously (e.g. Win + Ctrl + S + D triggers both shortcuts)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Preview

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open **PowerToys Settings** and navigate to **Keyboard Manager**.
2. Click on **Remap a shortcut**.
3. Add a rule to disable a shortcut:
   - **Shortcut:** `Win + Ctrl + D`
   - **Mapped to:** `Disable`
4. Test pressing `Win + Ctrl + D` alone -> The shortcut is successfully disabled (no virtual desktop is created).
5. Now, press and hold `Win + Ctrl + S` and simultaneously press `D` (or press `Win + Ctrl + S + D` at once, which frequently happens during gaming when moving with WASD while crouching with Ctrl).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

`Win + Ctrl + D` should remain disabled/suppressed according to the remap rule. Holding down additional keys (such as `S` for movement) should not bypass the shortcut matcher or leak underlying native Windows shortcuts.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The remapping / disabling rule for `Win + Ctrl + D` is completely bypassed.
Windows receives and triggers both system shortcuts simultaneously:
- `Win + Ctrl + S` is fired (e.g., Windows Speech Recognition opens).
- `Win + Ctrl + D` is fired (e.g., a new Virtual Desktop is created).
Both combinations leak through to the OS during multi-key rollover.

title: Grab and Move - Right-Drag Title Bar - A small enhancement that I think may be nice.
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Perhaps a toggle to enable, but dragging a window's title bar with the right mouse button begins the existing window drag feature (without a modifier key, and without changing window focus). Acorn's RISC OS had this feature which I always thought was nice and is something I've always missed in Windows.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Most of the same scenarios as the existing power toy. You do have to be able to see the title bar to do this, but it saves using the modifier key making it slightly more accessible and intuitive.

### Supporting information

Essentially, I think it could be a really useful feature as it provides the ability to use the Grab and Move without the modifier key, and I don't think right-dragging a title bar would interfere with any other operation. I've vibe-coded a very simple tray application that does just this function and it works great, but then I found Grab and Move and it's better implementation, simply lacking the right-drag option which I think people would benefit from (and an option).

body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

We need a tool that auto-clicks the notification toasts ("notification banners").

Ideally should be able to filter by the toast's caption title (the name of the toast's originator as it appears under "Notifications from apps and other senders" in Settings/Notifications) and the button text, with two or three button texts to click ,in order of preferences, e.g. if a button matches "Text1" then click it, else if a button matches "Text2" then click it, else if a button matches "Text3" then click it.

The understanding is that clicking the button closes/acknowledges the notification by clicking the preferred button. If the button text on the banner does not match any of the ordered presets, do nothing. Extra credits if this works for notifications not shown as banner but in the notification Center only (if that is still a thing)

Obviously the new PowerToy should be based on some sort of hook and not just watch the screen or click blindly, and can also read the button's text in a deterministic manner. Hopefully a [notification listener ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/notification-listener) can do that?

This would help with Very Long (days) running processes that ask the user random questions through toast notifications at random times.

title: Advanced Paste: Advanced AI fails with reasoning models requiring reasoning_effort:none for Chat Completions function tools
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Advanced Paste

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an OpenAI model provider in Advanced Paste → Paste with AI using model gpt-6-luna and a valid OpenAI API key.
2. Leave Advanced AI – Use built-in functions to handle complex tasks disabled.
3. Use Paste with AI. The model works normally.
4. Enable Advanced AI for the same model.
5. Copy some text, open Advanced Paste and make a Paste with AI request.
6. The request fails with OpenAI request failed with status code: 400.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Advanced AI should work with an OpenAI model that supports function tools, or PowerToys should configure the request appropriately for the selected model/API.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

With Advanced AI enabled, OpenAI rejects the request:

> Microsoft.SemanticKernel.HttpOperationException: HTTP 400 (invalid_request_error: )
> Parameter: reasoning_effort
> 
> Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-6-luna in /v1/chat/completions. To use function tools, use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to 'none'.

The same gpt-6-luna provider works when Advanced AI is disabled.

### Cause

The Advanced AI path enables automatic Semantic Kernel function calling:

[https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.100.2/src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/Services/AdvancedAIKernelService.cs](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.100.2/src/modules/AdvancedPaste/AdvancedPaste/Services/AdvancedAIKernelService.cs)

```
return new OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings
{
    FunctionChoiceBehavior = FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto(),
};
```

The provider is registered with AddOpenAIChatCompletion, so this uses OpenAI's /v1/chat/completions API.

Enabling Advanced AI therefore adds PowerToys' built-in actions as function tools. For gpt-6-luna, the Chat Completions API rejects function tools when reasoning is enabled/defaulted and requires either:

- reasoning_effort: "none"; or
- use of the /v1/responses API.

This also appears to remain applicable to the current main implementation, which still uses AddOpenAIChatCompletion and FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto() for the Advanced AI path.

### Possible short-term fix

For models that require reasoning to be disabled when combining Chat Completions with function tools, explicitly send:

  "reasoning_effort": "none"

PowerToys currently references OpenAI .NET SDK 2.7.0. Although Semantic Kernel 1.71.0's string conversion only recognises low, medium, high and minimal, the underlying OpenAI SDK exposes a public ChatReasoningEffortLevel(string value) constructor, and Semantic Kernel accepts a ChatReasoningEffortLevel instance directly.

For example, a model-specific proof of concept is:

```
using OpenAI.Chat;

#pragma warning disable OPENAI001
return new OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings
{
    FunctionChoiceBehavior = FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto(),
    ReasoningEffort =
        string.Equals(
            runtimeConfig.ModelName,
            "gpt-6-luna",
            StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
        ? new ChatReasoningEffortLevel("none")
        : null,
};
#pragma warning restore OPENAI001
```
I would not suggest applying reasoning_effort: "none" unconditionally, because models that do not support the parameter may themselves return HTTP 400.

A more general capability-based implementation would avoid hardcoding individual models.

### Longer-term fix

For newer reasoning models, using OpenAI's Responses API for the Advanced AI/tool-calling path may be preferable. The API error explicitly recommends /v1/responses when combining function tools with reasoning.

That would allow Advanced AI to retain reasoning rather than disabling it solely to remain compatible with /v1/chat/completions.

### Related issue

This is related in nature to #49838, but appears to be a different problem:

#49838 concerned PowerToys explicitly setting an incompatible reasoning_effort value for ordinary custom actions. In this case PowerToys does not explicitly set ReasoningEffort; the failure occurs specifically when Advanced AI enables function tools for gpt-6-luna through /v1/chat/completions.

title: [Feature Request] Add Customizable Windows Profiles to PowerToys
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

# [Feature Request] Customizable Windows Profiles

## Description

It would be great if PowerToys could provide a **Windows Customization Profiles** feature that allows users to save and quickly switch between different Windows setups.

For example, a user could create profiles such as:

### 💻 Coding

* Dark/light theme
* Wallpaper
* Accent color
* Preferred window layout
* Selected applications
* Monitor arrangement

### 🎮 Gaming

* Gaming wallpaper
* Dark theme
* Gaming-related applications
* Preferred window arrangement

### 📚 Study

* Minimal wallpaper
* Light theme
* Browser/PDF applications
* Preferred window arrangement

Users could switch between these profiles from PowerToys or Command Palette.

## Possible activation methods

Profiles could be activated:

* Manually from PowerToys
* Through a keyboard shortcut
* From Command Palette
* When a specific application launches
* At a specific time
* When a monitor/device is connected

For example:

```text
VS Code opens
      ↓
Activa
```


### Scenario when this would be used?

Users often have different Windows setups for different activities, such as coding, studying, gaming, designing, or giving presentations.

For example, a user could create a **Coding** profile with a specific wallpaper, theme, accent color, window arrangement, and preferred applications. They could then switch to a **Gaming** or **Study** profile when needed instead of manually changing each setting.

This would be especially useful for users with multiple monitors or different workflows throughout the day.


### Supporting information

The proposed feature could allow users to create, save, and switch between customizable Windows profiles from PowerToys or Command Palette.

Each profile could contain selected settings such as wallpaper, Windows theme, accent color, window layouts, monitor configuration, and optionally applications to launch.

For example:

**Coding Profile**

* Dark theme
* Coding wallpaper
* Preferred accent color
* Custom window layout
* VS Code, Terminal, and browser

**Study Profile**

* Light theme
* Minimal wallpaper
* Split-screen layout
* Browser and PDF reader

Users should be able to choose which settings are included in each profile rather than having every setting changed automatically.

This could also integrate with PowerToys Command Palette and keyboard shortcuts for quick profile switching. Future versions could support automatic activation based on application launches, time, or connected monitors/devices.

title: [Settings/Runner] Failing to load a module will wipe its entry in settings
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.102 (current main)

### Installation method

Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

Settings, General

### Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure PowerToys is not running
2. Rename a PowerToys' application module exe or dll (in this example the **File Locksmith** exe)
3. Start PowerToys
4. Exit PowerToys

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The application's enabled/disable setting is unaffected by this temporary issue with its start up.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Its entry is removed from the **settings.json** file entirely.

The next time it can be loaded by Runner, its enabled setting is written **as its default**, wiping any previous user preference. This can look to the user as if a tool they've deliberately disabled is being forced back on.

This also affects Settings and Quick Access, where the module is set back to its default and any attempt to change the setting will be reverted when navigating away:

### Settings

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4eb59677-588b-4064-b4f9-111bd2ce7537

### Quick Access

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/004b2021-38c4-477b-a940-37a19a7a5e27

## Context Menus
This **also** also affects context menu entries.

### Entries appearing even if the tool has been set to disabled

(I think this is how it happens, I'm not 100% sure of the full route yet.)

1. Windows calls `IExplorerCommand::GetState()`

```cpp
   IFACEMETHODIMP ExplorerCommand::GetState(IShellItemArray* psiItemArray, BOOL fOkToBeSlow, EXPCMDSTATE* pCmdState)
   {
       *pCmdState = FileLocksmithSettingsInstance().GetEnabled() ? ECS_ENABLED : ECS_HIDDEN;
       return S_OK;
   }
```

2. `GetEnabled()` reads directly from **settings.json**. In File Locksmith's code:

```cpp
json::get(modulesEnabledState, L"File Locksmith", settings.enabled, true);
```

3. If there was a previous issue starting File Locksmith, the setting has been removed and so is not found. The default is used, which is **true**. The menu entry is displayed despite the user disabling it.

title: Keyboard Manager new editor: no way to map a shortcut to media keys (e.g. Play/Pause Media)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Microsoft PowerToys version
0.101.2362

Installation method
Microsoft Store

Area with issue?
Keyboard Manager

Description
In the new "Add new remapping" editor, choosing Action → "Remap to key or shortcut" only shows a "Press to start recording keys" box. There is no drop down to pick keys such as Play/Pause Media, and media keys often can't be captured by pressing them. This makes it impossible to map a trigger to a media key in the new editor. The old editor had a key drop down that included these keys, and it works there.

Steps to reproduce

Open Keyboard Manager and go to the new "Add new remapping" dialog.
Set Trigger to "Key or shortcut" and record any shortcut. In my case this was the Copilot key, which sends Win (Left) + Shift (Left) + F23.
Set Action to "Remap to key or shortcut".
Try to select Play/Pause Media as the target.

Expected behavior
The Action side offers a drop down of keys, as the old editor does, including media keys such as Play/Pause Media, so the target can be chosen without pressing a physical media key.

Actual behavior
Only "Press to start recording keys" is shown. There is no drop down, so Play/Pause Media can't be chosen. Pressing a physical media key to record it is unreliable. The only workaround I found was to create the remap in the old editor.


Suggested fix
Add the per-key drop down to the Action side of the new editor. This could probably be extended to have the same functions as the old editor

### Scenario when this would be used?

This is relevant for any scenario where one would want a key rebound to a function different to just a key on the keyboard, and this would make it match the old editor. 

### Supporting information

_No response_

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add an option to Light Switch such that when Light Switch enables/disables dark mode, it will also:

1. Enable/Disable Edge's "Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents" (enable-force-dark) Experiments flag when Light Switch enables/disables dark mode
2. Ask the user if it is OK to restart Edge in order for the enable-force-dark flag to take effect

### Scenario when this would be used?

When a user wants to 

1. view web pages that do not automatically switch to dark mode when the Edge browser itself is configured to use dark mode, but 
2. wants pages to resume being displayed in light mode when Edge is configured to light mode

For example, learn.microsoft.com continues to display pages in light mode even when Edge itself is configured to use dark mode. If the user manually uses the enable-force-dark flag, learn.microsoft.com will display pages in dark mode, even when Edge itself is configured to use light mode.

title: CmdPal: custom monitor names and stable default names in Dock settings
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Let users rename monitors in Command Palette's Dock settings, with the same name shown in the on-screen identification label. For example, I could name a monitor `Desk monitor` or `Wireless display`.

There should also be a way to restore the default name. If a monitor has no hardware-friendly name, give it a saved label such as `Display A` instead of using a Windows display number that can change after reconnecting.

### Scenario when this would be used?

I use a Miracast display that Windows can assign a different display number after reconnecting. Even when its Dock settings are preserved, a changing display name makes it harder to recognize in Dock settings. Hardware model names can also be less useful than names based on where I use each screen.

Custom names and stable defaults would make it easier to pick the right monitor when configuring its Dock.

### Supporting information

I opened #50842 with an implementation before opening this issue. I'm adding the feature request here as requested so we can discuss the behavior.

The PR includes a before/after screenshot and keeps the name changes separate from monitor identity matching.

title: Mouse Without Borders: hotkey machine switch doesn't transfer copied files or large clipboard content
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Preview

### Installation method

Machine-wide installer

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. On machine A, copy a file, or more than 1 MB of text.
2. Within 30 seconds, switch to machine B with its Ctrl+Alt+F1..F4 hotkey.
3. Paste on B.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The content is pasted, as it is when you switch by moving the mouse to B.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

B pastes its previous clipboard content.

### Additional Information

Mouse switches trigger the fetch of announced clipboard data in `Event.PrepareToSwitchToMachine`. Hotkey switches (`MachineStuff.SwitchToMachine`) don't. Found by reading the source; not the general failure tracked in #45825.

title: docs: broken image link in tools/project_template/README.md (example_settings.png removed in 2021)
body:
### Describe the bug

`tools/project_template/README.md` references a screenshot that was removed from the repository almost five years ago:

Line 50:
```markdown
![Image of the Options](/doc/images/settings/example_settings.png)
```

- Target path (root-relative): `doc/images/settings/example_settings.png` → **HTTP 404**
- The `doc/images/` directory exists but does not contain a `settings/` subdirectory.
- Git history: the file was deleted in "remove legacy settings docs (#14709)" (2021-12-03), but the reference in the project template README survived.

When reading the README on GitHub, the "Here's an example of what the settings look like in the Settings screen" section renders as a broken image.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/tools/project_template/README.md
2. Observe the broken image below "Here's an example of what the settings look like in the Settings screen:".
3. `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/PowerToys/main/doc/images/settings/example_settings.png` → 404

### Expected behavior

The section either shows the screenshot or does not reference a missing file.

### Suggested fix

Either remove the image line, or replace it with a current screenshot of the settings screen committed under `doc/images/`.

### Additional context

Found during a systematic documentation-rot audit of open source repositories (<https://codebyaurora.com/docrot/>).

title: Feature Request: Dedicated Standalone Screen Drawing/Annotation Utility (Separate from ZoomIt)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I am requesting a dedicated standalone screen drawing/annotation feature in PowerToys that functions independently of ZoomIt. 

The proposed feature should:
1. Allow users to enter a free-form "Draw Mode" anywhere on the screen using a clean, customizable shortcut.
2. Provide simple on-screen or quick keyboard controls to change line colors and brush thickness.
3. Automatically clear all annotations and reset the cursor state completely upon pressing the shortcut again or hitting 'Esc'.
4. Include support for drawing perfect straight lines (e.g., by holding Shift) for professional presentation callouts and technical charting.


### Scenario when this would be used?

This feature is highly requested for two major everyday workflows:
1. Live Presentations & Education: Instantly highlighting or pointing out specific elements on the screen to an audience without needing full screen magnification or dealing with ZoomIt's broader presentation configurations.
2. Financial Charting & Trading: Quickly drawing free-hand patterns, support/resistance levels, or trendlines over real-time live trading charts, and instantly resetting the screen once the technical analysis or pattern identification is complete.

Currently, ZoomIt bundles drawing with magnification behaviors which often creates configuration friction or causes compatibility/performance issues on certain laptop displays. A separate, lightweight utility dedicated entirely to screen annotation would be much more reliable and streamlined.


### Supporting information

I attempted to use ZoomIt for this purpose, but it failed to function properly on my laptop hardware. Having a modular, standalone application specifically built for screen drawing would provide a lightweight, modern, and robust solution for power users who don't need or want the full ZoomIt overhead.

title: Shortcuts to change brightness etc. of monitors in Power Display
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Right now, there is a Power Display flyout that could be called with a shortcut. Then, to move sliders—like brightness—of every display, one has to use a mouse. It'd be helpful if +/- step changes of those sliders were connected to shortcuts (not to use a mouse, but to change the brightness of a selected display using the keyboard). If it could be done even without calling the flyout first, but directly having a set of shortcuts for every display, that would be even better. E.g., you press a shortcut to change the brightness; the flyout pops up and shows the change of the corresponding slider position while the display has its brightness changed—everything with just one shortcut press.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Always and every day—to change a display's brightness with a shortcut, without having to open the flyout and use the mouse.

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: GAMEPAD SHORTCUTS SUPPORT
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Hi Guys

Been using Powertoys on my PC for a long time and loved it. I recently bought the XBOX ALLY X and with the XBOX mode also available on desktop PC I think this is a good time to introduce some features to make it work better during XBOX mode.

I have a Flydigi vader 5 Pro which supports **dongle** and **bluetooth** as well. With the dongle mode you can use the Flydigi App to map keyboard keys to the controller. I usually set the Shortcut on PowerToys to a specific key (F3..) then apply that key to the controller with the Flydigi App. Everything works great right?... _Thats only using the dongle_.

IF i setup the controller or any Gamepad through BLUETOOTH, we do not have a way to set the shortcuts on PowerToys to a gamepad button because PowerToys doesn't recognize Gamepads. It would be great if We could set the same Shortcuts that we created in PowerToys and when it prompts us to press the keyboard button to attach it to... we could instead press the Gamepad button.


### Scenario when this would be used?

This would solve major problems in XBOX MODE with Gamepads when we need to set TASK VIEW shortcuts to a specific button or the Xbox Gamebar shortcut to another.

For example, The Flydigi Vader 5 Pro has Gamebar mapped to the Home button, but it doesnt have **_Task View_** pre mapped on the controller so there is no way to switch between apps when using a Gamepad in XBOX MODE. I think this is a major request since future XBOX consoles will be PCs.

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: Windows virtual desktop switch flash/overlay disappeared after enabling PowerToys Snap and/or Workspaces
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

V0.96.1

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

After enabling the Snap Pages / Layout Design feature in PowerToys, the flash/overlay message that Windows normally shows when switching between virtual desktops with Ctrl+Win+Right/Left Arrow stopped appearing. Before enabling those PowerToys feature, the overlay displayed correctly.

Steps to reproduce:

Enable the Snap Pages / Layout Design feature in PowerToys.
Press Ctrl+Win+Right Arrow (or Left Arrow) to switch virtual desktops.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The native Windows overlay indicating the desktop switch should appear.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The overlay no longer appears.

I disabled the "Override Windows Snap" setting in PowerToys, but the overlay still doesn't appear. I'm confident this is related to PowerToys/Snap in general, but I haven't been able to pinpoint which specific setting is causing it.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

OS Name	Microsoft Windows 11 Pro
Version	10.0.26100 Build 26100

Powertoys V0.96.1

title: [Mouse Without Borders] Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature / Settings.exe and MWB binaries are signed with different certificates (v0.101.2652.0+)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2652.0 (updated from 0.100.2)

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install / update to PowerToys 0.101.2652.0 (per-user, x64) on Windows 11 25H2 (26200.9550; also reproduced on 26200.9445).
2. Open Settings > Mouse Without Borders.
3. Click "New key" to generate a new security key, or try to connect to another machine.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

A new security key is generated and MWB settings sync with the running MWB process.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Nothing happens. The Settings log repeats the following about every 0.5 s (11,240 times in one day), starting from the very first launch after the update:

```
[Error] MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs::GetSettingsSyncHelperAsync::368
    Couldn't create SettingsSync: System.UnauthorizedAccessException: Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature
```

It happens both with "Use Service" on (MWB running as LocalSystem) and off (MWB running as the user).

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OS version: Windows 11 25H2 26200.9550 (x64)
Running as admin: Yes

### Analysis
The Authenticode signer certificates differ between Settings and the MWB binaries in the same 0.101.2652.0 install:

| File | Signer thumbprint | Serial |
|---|---|---|
| PowerToys.exe | AB172913A2960A224809EE8A0C371CD47A079B72 | 330000021D4D19C84ED70F574800000000021D |
| WinUI3Apps\PowerToys.Settings.exe | AB172913A2960A224809EE8A0C371CD47A079B72 | 330000021D4D19C84ED70F574800000000021D |
| PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe | 1D77A9B9E8FE2075D9AD15123257FB90DB0DA4A1 | 330000021CFACDC59BE82F7EC400000000021C |
| PowerToys.MouseWithoutBordersHelper.exe | 1D77A9B9E8FE2075D9AD15123257FB90DB0DA4A1 | 330000021CFACDC59BE82F7EC400000000021C |
| PowerToys.MouseWithoutBordersService.exe | 1D77A9B9E8FE2075D9AD15123257FB90DB0DA4A1 | 330000021CFACDC59BE82F7EC400000000021C |

- Both certificates are `CN=Microsoft Corporation`, issued by `Microsoft Code Signing PCA 2024`. `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` reports `Valid`, and the chain builds with `X509RevocationMode.Offline`.
- Across the whole install directory, all files are FileVersion 0.101.2652.0 (built 2026-09-23), but 371 files are signed with `AB1729…` and 196 files with `1D77A9…`.
- The installer I used is the official release asset: `PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2652.0-x64.exe`, SHA256 `0D2BEF1B473F332477BF58426FE09E81439B240687073CA38FB03BDE447A1666`, which matches both the asset digest and the hash table in the release notes.
- In `NamedPipePeerVerification.cs` at tag v0.101.2652.0 (added in #50480, shipped since v0.101.2572.0), `MeetsSigningPolicy` requires `HaveSameTrustedMicrosoftSigner(ownImagePath, peerImagePath)` when the caller has an embedded signature, and the signers are compared as leaf certificates: `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals(firstSigner.RawData, secondSigner.RawData)`. Settings (`AB1729…`) therefore rejects the MWB process (`1D77A9…`) as `untrusted-signature`.
- In 0.101.2362.0, `PowerToys.exe`, `PowerToys.Settings.exe`, and `PowerToys.MouseWithoutBorders.exe` are all signed with `1D77A9…`, and MWB works.

### Workaround
Downgrade to 0.101.2362.0 (uninstall, remove the leftover `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PowerToys` folder, reinstall 0.101.2362.0).

### Suggestion
Either sign all binaries of a release with the same certificate, or compare the signer by a stable identity (for example, the issuing CA chain plus the subject) instead of the leaf certificate.

### Related
- #50480 (introduced the settings-sync peer verification)
- #49949 (Validate settings sync peers)
- #50615 (Settings rejected as `not-microsoft-signed`; different cause, same area of signature verification)

### Other Software

_No response_

title: ## Mouse Jump preview window does not respond to mouse clicks in v0.101.2362.0
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Utilities

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PowerToys **0.101.2362.0**.
2. Enable **Mouse Jump**.
3. Press `Shift + Alt + A`.
4. The Mouse Jump preview window appears normally.
5. Click any location in the Mouse Jump preview window.


### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Clicking a location in the Mouse Jump preview should move the mouse cursor to the corresponding location, as expected from the Mouse Jump functionality.


### ❌ Actual Behavior

The Mouse Jump preview window appears normally, but **mouse clicks have no effect at all**.

Clicking anywhere in the preview does not move the cursor and does not appear to trigger any action.

There is:

* No error message
* No warning
* No crash
* No visible indication of an error

The Mouse Jump preview simply remains unresponsive to mouse clicks.


### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[PowerToysReport_2026-09-26-01-28-01.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32673702/PowerToysReport_2026-09-26-01-28-01.zip)

### Additional Information

## Mouse Jump preview window does not respond to mouse clicks in v0.101.2362.0

### Microsoft PowerToys version

**0.101.2362.0**

### Release channel

Preview

### Installation method

WinGet update

### Area(s) with issue

Mouse Utilities / Mouse Jump

### Windows version

* Windows 11 Pro
* Version 25H2
* OS Build 26200.9457

### Hardware

* CPU: Intel Core i5-12400
* GPU: Intel Arc A380
* RAM: 32 GB
* Displays: 3

### Display configuration

The PC uses three displays.

* Display 1 and Display 3 are duplicated/mirrored.
* Display 2 is positioned to the right of the duplicated displays.

### Mouse Jump configuration

* Mouse Jump: Enabled
* Activation shortcut: `Shift + Alt + A`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install PowerToys **0.101.2362.0**.
2. Enable **Mouse Jump**.
3. Press `Shift + Alt + A`.
4. The Mouse Jump preview window appears normally.
5. Click any location in the Mouse Jump preview window.

### Expected behavior

Clicking a location in the Mouse Jump preview should move the mouse cursor to the corresponding location, as expected from the Mouse Jump functionality.

### Actual behavior

The Mouse Jump preview window appears normally, but **mouse clicks have no effect at all**.

Clicking anywhere in the preview does not move the cursor and does not appear to trigger any action.

There is:

* No error message
* No warning
* No crash
* No visible indication of an error

The Mouse Jump preview simply remains unresponsive to mouse clicks.

### Reproducibility

The problem was **100% reproducible** with PowerToys 0.101.2362.0.

### Regression test

I downgraded PowerToys from **0.101.2362.0** to **0.100.2** using the official PowerToys installer.

With PowerToys **0.100.2**, using the same Mouse Jump configuration and the same hardware/display configuration:

1. Press `Shift + Alt + A`.
2. Mouse Jump opens normally.
3. Click a location in the preview.
4. The mouse cursor moves to the clicked location correctly.

The behavior therefore changes between **0.100.2** and **0.101.2362.0**.

### Important comparison

The only change made between the failing and working tests was:

* Uninstall PowerToys 0.101.2362.0
* Install PowerToys 0.100.2

No Windows settings or other system settings were intentionally changed between the tests.

This makes the version difference particularly useful for reproducing the regression.

### Additional information

PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 was installed/updated through WinGet.

PowerToys 0.100.2 was installed using the official PowerToys installer.

I do not know whether PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 was running with administrator privileges.

No error dialog, warning, or crash occurred when the mouse clicks failed.

### Summary

**0.101.2362.0:**
Mouse Jump opens, but mouse clicks in the preview window do nothing.

**0.100.2:**
Mouse Jump opens and mouse clicks correctly move the cursor to the selected location.

The issue appears to be a regression introduced between these versions.


### Other Software

_No response_

title: Alt + KEY Shortcuts Function Unexpectedly
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2652 (preview)

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

Create a shortcut with Alt + J as Trigger, Down key press as Action

Open notepad and add a few lines, then move to the top of the file. Press Alt + J

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The cursor should move down a line as the down key is pressed

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The Alt menu is triggered, displaying the key presses required to open the File, Edit, View menu etc.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

I realize that this may be an accessibility thing, but if I specifically go out of my way to create a shortcut overriding Alt + J then I understand that I lose the ability to hit that combination for Alt menus. As it stands, Alt chords are not really useful.

Ideally if in my example I press Alt + F, it would still open the file menu.

I have gotten this to work in my own keyboard shortcut software by sending the following inputs when I see that a shortcut has been triggered:

1. Dummy key (key code 0xFF) down
2. Dummy key up
3. Trigger key(s) up (in this case J)
4. Modifier key(s) up (in this case Alt)
5. Action key(s) down (Down in this case)
6. Action key(s) up
7. Modifier key(s) down (So that Alt is still being held down after the shortcut fires)
8. Dummy key down
9. Dummy key up

This allowed the Alt menu to work with other keys, while preventing it from appearing for bound Alt key chords. This sequence may or may not cause issues in certain cases in your software, but if it does maybe it could be special cased specifically for Alt key chords bound to key press actions.

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

2. Go to the encryption key section
3. Manually type security key + device name
4. Click "Connect"
5. Fields are wiped instantly, no connection happens, no error shown, typed values are lost

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

- Manually entered field values must NEVER be cleared automatically by the app, regardless of connection outcome.
- Connection attempt should proceed (port is confirmed reachable), or show a clear error, and values should stay in the fields so the user can retry or fix them.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

User-entered data is wiped immediately, connection drops silently, feature unusable. No log file found to attach — would be happy to provide one if the app produced it.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

v0.101.2362 windows 11

### Description
In Mouse Without Borders, in the encryption key section, entering a value in the security key field and device name field and clicking the inline "Connect" button immediately WIPES both fields without connecting and without any way to retry with the same values.

**This is the core problem: fields the user manually typed must never be cleared automatically, especially not on a failed/incomplete action.** Losing manually entered data with no confirmation and no way to recover it is a basic UX violation, not just a connection bug.

- Disabled Windows Firewall entirely — same result.
- Test-NetConnection 192.168.1.137 -Port 15101 -> succeeds (TcpTestSucceeded: True), so the target port is reachable and it's not a network/firewall issue.

3. Manually type security key + device name
4. Click "Connect"
5. Fields are wiped instantly, no connection happens, no error shown, typed values are lost

- Manually entered field values must NEVER be cleared automatically by the app, regardless of connection outcome.

title: Automated per-app single key remapping & UX metadata/preset enhancements
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Currently, PowerToys Keyboard Manager restricts per-app remapping to the "Remap Shortcuts" module, which strictly validates input to require a modifier key (e.g., Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win). Users cannot directly assign a single physical key (e.g., End) to execute an app-specific action (e.g., Ctrl+W in chrome.exe). While a manual two-step workaround exists (mapping the single key to a complex dummy shortcut globally, then mapping that dummy shortcut to the target action per-app), this creates significant friction.

I am requesting an automated bridge for this workaround, alongside several cohesive UX improvements to modernize the Keyboard Manager module:

Automated Single-Key Per-App Routing: Allow users to select a single key in a per-app context. The UI should silently abstract the manual workaround by automatically generating and assigning an internal dummy shortcut (e.g., an unused Virtual Key sequence) to route the single keypress to the target app.

Interactive Capture UX: Ensure the physical Select keystroke capture button is consistently available across all input fields so users are not forced to scroll through the VK dropdown list when configuring app-specific rules.

Terminology & Disclaimers: Provide inline tooltips explaining technical terms like "Chords" (two-step key sequences) and "VK Codes" (Virtual Key codes). Additionally, include inline warnings clarifying that active-window hooking (GetForegroundWindow checks on WH_KEYBOARD_LL) introduces minor input latency, explicitly advising against using per-app single-key remappings for latency-critical applications like competitive gaming.

Metadata Fields: Introduce Created Date/Timestamp and Notes/Description fields for every active remapping rule to document the business logic or purpose behind specific custom mappings.

Export/Import Support: Enable saving and loading configurations as .json or .md files for deployment across workstations and sharing with colleagues.

Community Presets / Command Palette: Integrate a repository of popular productivity remappings that can be applied via checkboxes or deployed dynamically via PowerToys Run.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This functionality addresses standard productivity workflows where a user wants to repurpose a single, accessible hardware key (like End, Insert, or a dedicated macro key) to perform a specific function (like closing a tab or muting audio) exclusively within a target application (like Chrome or Teams), without breaking the key's native functionality system-wide.

The metadata, export capabilities, and clear terminology allow power users to document complex mapping logic, share standardized workflows across a corporate team or multi-device setup, and prevent configurations from becoming "black boxes" months after creation.

### Supporting information

Note regarding template constraints: While this issue contains multiple feature requests, they collectively address a single overarching objective: eliminating the UX friction of the Keyboard Manager's current input validation rules and bridging the gap between power-user capabilities and non-power-user accessibility.

The underlying system architecture for the single-key per-app mapping already works via the manual chaining method. Automating the dummy shortcut generation within the UI parser requires no changes to the low-level keyboard hook mechanism itself, keeping performance overhead identical to current implementations. Furthermore, allowing physical key capture in the shortcut fields mitigates user confusion when encountering the VK code dropdown list.

title: Command Palette: single mouse click activates a list item after keyboard navigation, even with "Single click activates" turned off
body:
## Description

With **Settings → Appearance → "Single click activates"** turned **off** (`SingleClickActivates: false`),
a single **mouse click** on a list row should only select the row and show its details; activation
should require a **double click** (or Enter).

After the list has been navigated with the **keyboard** at least once (↓ / ↑ / Page Up / Page Down /
Enter / Space), a subsequent **single mouse click** immediately **activates** the item instead. The
stale "last input was keyboard" state survives until the page is re-created (navigate away and back),
which makes the bug look intermittent.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Confirm "Single click activates" is off. `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Microsoft.CommandPalette_8wekyb3d8bbwe\LocalState\settings.json` contains `"SingleClickActivates": false`.
2. Open Command Palette and get a list of results (any page with a list, e.g. the root list or Search apps).
3. Press **↓** once (or Page Down, or Enter/Space) so the keyboard becomes the last input source.
4. **Single** click a row with the mouse.
   - **Actual:** the item is activated (its command runs / the page is pushed).
   - **Expected:** the row is only selected, and its details pane is shown.
5. Control: leave the page and come back (the page is re-created) — a single click selects again.
   Doing **only** mouse interaction (never pressing ↑ ↓ Page Up Page Down Enter Space) also never
   activates on a single click.

Confirmed on **built-in** pages with no third-party extension involved: the root page (the list of
top-level commands) and the built-in **Search apps** page both activate on a single click after a
keyboard navigation. The same happens on a third-party extension page that uses `ListPage`.

## Root cause (from source, `main`)

`src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/ExtViews/ListItemsView.xaml.cs`:

- `Items_ItemClick` (`:202-226`):
  ```csharp
  if (_lastInputSource == InputSource.Keyboard)
  {
      ViewModel?.InvokeItemCommand.Execute(item);
      return;
  }

  var settings = ...Settings;
  if (settings.SingleClickActivates) { ViewModel?.InvokeItemCommand.Execute(item); }
  else { _scrollOnNextSelectionChange = true; UpdateSelectedItemCommand.Execute(item); Send<FocusSearchBoxMessage>(); }
  ```
  The click is therefore treated as keyboard activation when `_lastInputSource == Keyboard`.
- `MarkKeyboardNavigation()` (`:508`) sets `_lastInputSource = Keyboard`. It is called from
  `Receive(NavigateNextCommand)` (`:533-535`), `NavigatePreviousCommand` (`:552`),
  `NavigateLeftCommand` (`:570`), `NavigateRightCommand` (`:588`), `NavigatePageDownCommand` (`:630`),
  `NavigatePageUpCommand` (`:655`) — all sent by the search bar (`Controls/SearchBar.xaml.cs`) — and from
  `Items_PreviewKeyDown` (`:1169-1174`, Enter/Space).
- `Items_PointerPressed` (`:1167`) is meant to reset it to `Pointer`, but the handler is attached as a
  **plain, non-`handledEventsToo` subscription**:
  - shipped build: `this.ItemView.PointerPressed += Items_PointerPressed;` in the constructor, where
    `ViewModel` is still `null`, so `ItemView` resolves to `ItemsList` — the **GridView never gets the handler**;
  - `main`: XAML attributes `PointerPressed="Items_PointerPressed"` on both `ListView` and `GridView`.

  Rows run with `IsItemClickEnabled="True"` **and** `CanDragItems="True"`, so the pointer press is
  consumed by the item container before it reaches the list view and the reset never happens. Elsewhere
  the codebase deliberately uses `AddHandler(PointerPressedEvent, ..., handledEventsToo: true)` when it
  must observe pointer presses (`Pages/ShellPage.xaml.cs:201`, `Settings/SettingsWindow.xaml.cs:86`).
- The state is per `ListItemsView` instance and is **never** reset on ViewModel change:
  `OnViewModelChanged` (`:821-839`) is commented "Reset latched state" but clears only
  `_forceFirstPending` / `_stickySelectedItem` / `_lastPushedToVm`. `OnUnloaded` (`:100-111`) does not
  clear it either. The only thing that clears it is page re-creation, because
  `Pages/ShellPage.xaml.cs:249-258` navigates the Frame **by type** and
  `ExtViews/ListPage.xaml.cs:36` sets `NavigationCacheMode.Disabled`.

## Suggested fix

Any of these (the first is the smallest):

1. In `OnViewModelChanged`, also reset `_lastInputSource = InputSource.None;`
   (`None` takes the same branch as `Pointer`, so behaviour is unchanged for genuinely pointer-driven clicks).
2. Attach the pointer handler so it is always observed:
   `ItemView.AddHandler(UIElement.PointerPressedEvent, new PointerEventHandler(Items_PointerPressed), true);`
   — and make sure **both** `ItemsList` and `ItemsGrid` get it.
3. Treat a pointer-activated `ItemClick` as pointer input explicitly, instead of relying on a latched field.

## Notes

- Regression of #41101, whose fix came in #41119 ("the `ListView.ItemClick` event doesn't tell us what
  caused the activation, so observe the last user input"). Its acceptance scenario is "Enter still
  activates", which **still
  passes** when the pointer reset stops working: a freshly created page starts at `InputSource.None`,
  which takes the same branch as `Pointer`. That is why the defect can stay hidden for a long time.
- The repro is confirmed on built-in pages (root page, Search apps) as well as on a third-party
  extension's `ListPage`, so this is a host-level defect and not anything extension-specific.

## Environment

- Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200.9457)
- Command Palette: store version **0.11.11762.0**, binary version **0.11.2606.25002**
  (`BuildInfo.xml`: `SemanticVersion="0.11.260625002"`)
- `SingleClickActivates: false`, `ShowAppDetails: false`

title: Mouse Highlighter should scale with DPI not raw pixels
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The Mouse Highlighter circle should automatically adjust its rendered pixel radius based on the active monitor's display scaling (DPI) factor.

Currently, the highlighter radius appears to use a fixed pixel count. On multi-monitor setups where monitors have different zoom levels (e.g., 100% scale on Display 1 vs. 150% or 200% scale on Display 2), moving the cursor from one screen to another causes the highlight circle to visually shrink or grow significantly relative to the rest of the UI elements on that screen.

Proposed Behavior:
Scale the rendering radius dynamically using the current display's DPI scale factor (Radius * (Current_DPI / Base_DPI)) so the highlight maintains a consistent visual scale relative to on-screen UI across all displays.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This is critical for anyone using multi-monitor setups with mixed display scales (e.g., a high-DPI laptop screen paired with standard 1080p/4K external monitors).

Without DPI normalization, the highlighter is either too small to notice on high-density displays or awkwardly oversized on lower-density displays, creating an inconsistent visual feedback experience when presenting, recording video tutorials, or navigating across screens.

### Supporting information

- Observed: Moving the mouse cursor between a 100% scaled monitor and a 150%/200% scaled monitor results in noticeable size discrepancies in the highlight overlay circle.
- Applies to: PowerToys Mouse Utilities -> Mouse Highlighter.
