title: [Awake] Option to automatically lock the workstation on user inactivity while keeping the system awake
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Currently, PowerToys Awake allows keeping the machine awake indefinitely, on a timer, or until expiration, with an option to keep the display on or allow the display to turn off.

However, when a user wants the system to stay awake (for example, to allow long-running background tasks, compilations, or large downloads to complete) while stepping away from their desk, there is currently no option in Awake to automatically lock the workstation after a set duration of user inactivity.

We propose adding an optional setting to Awake: **"Lock screen on inactivity" (or "Auto-lock on idle")**:
- **Settings Toggle**: An optional toggle in Settings (and optionally accessible via the tray flyout) to enable or disable automatic workstation locking on user inactivity.
- **Configurable Inactivity Timeout**: A configurable timeout (in minutes, defaulting to 5 minutes, range 1–120 minutes) determining when the workstation should be locked after user input ceases.
- **Inactivity Detection & Locking**: When enabled, Awake monitors physical user input. If no keyboard or mouse activity is detected for the configured duration, Awake calls `LockWorkStation()` to secure the session while continuously maintaining the awake state (`ES_CONTINUOUS | ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED`), so all background workloads continue uninterrupted.
- **Synergy with Session Lock Detection**: In conjunction with the recently merged PR #49388 (which detects session lock and removes `ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED`), this also allows the display to safely turn off after locking if configured, saving power while keeping background processes active.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Power users and developers frequently run tasks that take hours (compilations, large file transfers, rendering, local training, data migrations, etc.). In office, shared, or home environments with security compliance, leaving an unlocked computer unattended is a security violation and privacy risk.

Currently:
1. If the user relies on Windows native screen timeout + sleep timeout, the machine either goes to sleep (interrupting the long-running task) or requires modifying system power plans back and forth.
2. In many Windows configurations (especially standard S3 desktop setups), when Awake prevents sleep, the Windows "Require sign-in when PC wakes up from sleep" setting never triggers a lock screen when the display turns off, because Windows does not consider the system to have woken from sleep.
3. Enabling Awake with "Keep screen on" leaves the desktop visible and vulnerable to anyone passing by unless the user remembers to manually press Win + L every single time they step away.

With this enhancement, users can set Awake to keep their workloads running while having the peace of mind that their workstation will automatically lock itself after a few minutes of inactivity.

### Supporting information

**Technical feasibility and implementation outline:**

1. **User Inactivity Detection**:
   Using the Win32 API `GetLastInputInfo` (from `user32.dll`), Awake can query the tick count of the last physical keyboard/mouse input without polling hooks or simulating input:
   ```csharp
   [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]
   internal struct LASTINPUTINFO
   {
       public uint cbSize;
       public uint dwTime;
   }

   [DllImport("user32.dll", SetLastError = true)]
   [return: MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.Bool)]
   internal static extern bool GetLastInputInfo(ref LASTINPUTINFO plii);
   ```
   Idle duration is calculated as:
   `uint idleMs = (uint)Environment.TickCount - lastInputInfo.dwTime;`

2. **Session Locking**:
   Using the native `LockWorkStation` API (from `user32.dll`):
   ```csharp
   [DllImport("user32.dll", SetLastError = true)]
   [return: MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.Bool)]
   internal static extern bool LockWorkStation();
   ```
   `LockWorkStation` locks the session immediately without suspending background threads or altering power execution states.

3. **Coordination with Existing Awake Architecture**:
   - `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/AwakeProperties.cs`: Add `AutoLockOnInactivity` (bool, default `false`) and `AutoLockIntervalMinutes` (uint, default `5`).
   - `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/ViewModels/AwakeViewModel.cs`: Expose properties for two-way binding with `SettingsPageControl`.
   - `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/SettingsXAML/Views/AwakePage.xaml`: Add a `SettingsExpander` under `Awake_BehaviorSettingsGroup` with a ToggleSwitch and NumberBox.
   - `src/modules/awake/Awake/Core/Manager.cs`: Implement a periodic check (e.g. 1-second interval) when `AutoLockOnInactivity` is enabled, checking `idleMs >= timeout` and checking that `!IsScreenLocked` (using the session lock detection state from PR #49388) before invoking `LockWorkStation()`.

I am also happy to submit a PR implementing this feature if the team agrees with this proposal!

title: Power Display - Support for transparent overlay window and opacity for additional dimming
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Sometimes the minimum brightness of a monitor is still brighter than preferred. And some applications are brighter than others.

A transparent window with variable opacity overlaid on top of the screen/window can reduce the brightness of a screen *beyond* and DDC/DC brightness control support - or on monitors that do not support DDC/CI.

Suggested details about the proposed implementation:
* Add Overlay Profile support defining overlay transparency percentage increments or specific percentage levels (like how custom VCP names can be defined currently). Default setting would be a 5%, 10% or 25% increment.
* Applying predefined overlay transparency profiles to 1 or more monitors. Overlay will only function on monitors where it has been applied.
* Monitor overlay type 1 - Allow overlay transparency dimming to be applied *after* reaching minimum brightness (for "negative" brightness settings) if enabled
* Monitor overlay type 2 - Allow overlay transparency dimming to be managed separately from monitor brightness
* Monitor overlay transparency would probably be either as negative brightness (type 1) or as a separate setting (type 2) - not both.
* Overlay type and overlay profile application would be implemented under the monitor setting. Presumably a checkbox to enable, a combobox to select type 1 vs type 2, and a combo box to apply the defined overlay profiles.
* Full-screen support and region support (e.g. everything except the taskbar, or for zones defined in fancy zones for e.g. ultrawide monitors)
* Possible overlay application to the current foreground window with hotkeys or even a slider for the current application. That would terminate when the window terminates. I think you can, to a degree, make another window be the parent of your window by obtaining the handle through the Win32 API. So you should be able to capture events on that without too much pain.
* Potential setting for overlay color - helpful sometimes for visibility, though it overlaps with color space and blue/yellow light settings

An initial implementation would be a full per-monitor overlay with 5%, 10% or 25% increments with a separate slider bar (not integrated with brightness). Both the overlay profile and the default overlay transparency setting could be saved in the profile.


### Scenario when this would be used?

Monitors that don't support DDC/CI could still have partial brightness support with a transparent overlay
Monitors with DDC/CI support that are still relatively bright when at 0% brightness could be further dimmed
Setups with multiple monitors from multiple vendors will have different physical brightness values when set to 0% brightness. A transparent overlay could bring the brighter monitors in line with the dimmest ones.

### Supporting information

Parts of this could conceivable be implemented externally. For _window_ and region overlays, it would make as much sense to have that implemented externally as internally - except if you want to share overlay increment profiles between them.

For the monitor-specific overlays, I'd argue that placing it within Power Display makes the most sense. It helps compensate for monitors with poor DDC/CI support, could be enabled on any or all monitors, and could be managed within profiles to give the perfect brightness setting

There are multiple tools that do this already - just like there are tools that do what Power Display does. But there aren't good tools that do both DDC/CI brightness control _and_ transparent overlay control. And Power Display's profile support would make it especially useful.

Fullscreen applications, UAC and lock screens may not be affected by transparent overlays.

Transparent overlays can never fully replace brightness settings, as the backlight is unaffected by the overlay and it can never reach true black. But it can have enough of a difference for people with sensitive eyes or dark environments to make consistent use of it. And the ability to normalize monitor brightness with it is also helpful.

Some sample applications that do things like this could be **darkbright-helper** or **MonitorDimmer** (both on Github). **darkbright-helper** uses the "negative brightness" concept, where it changes hardware brightness until you hit 0, and then when you go lower, it dims by applying a transparent overlay.

title: Active Robocopy on Powertoys
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

### Summary
Add a native PowerToys shell extension/context menu utility (e.g., "RoboCopy / RoboPaste" or "Fast Copy/Paste") that leverages Windows' built-in Robocopy engine to dramatically accelerate multi-threaded file and folder copy operations directly from Windows Explorer.

---

### Target Audience / Use Case
- **Power users & Developers:** Moving large projects, datasets, source code repos, or local backups between drives or network shares (NAS/SMB).
- **Everyday Users:** Transferring huge folders containing thousands of small files without suffering from the single-threaded performance bottlenecks and hanging UI of default Windows Explorer copy/paste operations.

---

### Proposed Solution / Workflow
1. **Right-click Source Folder/Files:** User selects `"RoboCopy (Set Source)"` from the Explorer context menu.
2. **Right-click Target Directory:** User selects `"RoboPaste (Paste with Robocopy)"` from the context menu or empty space background.
3. **Execution:** PowerToys invokes `robocopy.exe` under the hood with configurable high-performance flags (e.g., `/MT:16 /MIR /R:2 /W:2`).

---

### Key Features & Configurable Options (PowerToys Settings)
- **Multi-threading Control:** Ability to specify thread counts (`/MT:8`, `/MT:16`, `/MT:32`).
- **Sync Options:** Toggle between Standard Copy or Mirror Sync (`/MIR`).
- **Retry Logic:** Custom retry/wait timeouts (`/R` and `/W`).
- **UI Progress:** Embedded UI progress bar or overlay window showing real-time transfer stats (Files/Bytes copied, speed, ETA) instead of raw CLI output.
- **Handling Attribute & Permission Preservation:** Option to copy ACLs/Owner info (`/COPYALL`).

---

### Why PowerToys?
While `robocopy.exe` is an extremely fast and powerful built-in tool in Windows, its CLI-only interface prevents general users from leveraging its multi-threaded transfer speeds in daily workflows. Integrating this seamlessly into the Explorer Context Menu via PowerToys would fill a major user productivity gap in Windows File Explorer.

### Scenario when this would be used?

### Scenario when this would be used?

#### Scenario 1: Backing Up Large Projects to a NAS or External Drive
A software engineer or content creator wants to quickly back up a large project directory (e.g., source code repositories, astro-imaging datasets, or virtual machine images) containing thousands of small files from their PC to a Network Attached Storage (NAS) via SMB or to an external SSD. 
- **Current Behavior:** Using default Windows `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+V` takes a long time, hangs on calculating remaining time, and processes files in a single-threaded manner.
- **With PowerToys Feature:** The user right-clicks the project folder, clicks `"RoboCopy Source"`, navigates to the NAS drive, right-clicks, and selects `"RoboPaste Target"`. PowerToys instantly launches a multi-threaded (`/MT:16`) Robocopy process, finishing the backup in a fraction of the time.

#### Scenario 2: Synchronizing Work Folders Between Drives
A developer needs to copy updated build artifacts or working directories across local NVMe/SATA drives or local network locations without re-copying unchanged files.
- **Current Behavior:** Windows Explorer requires copying everything from scratch or prompting to overwrite existing files one by one.
- **With PowerToys Feature:** Using the RoboCopy/RoboPaste menu with `/MIR` (Mirror) or smart resume capabilities, only modified or new files are transferred, skipping identical files automatically.

#### Scenario 3: High-Speed File Transfer without Command Line Friction
A system administrator or IT professional knows Robocopy is significantly faster and more reliable than File Explorer, but opening a terminal, navigating to paths, and manually typing out long, escape-quoted source/destination arguments is tedious.
- **Current Behavior:** Manually writing scripts or typing CLI commands like `robocopy "C:\Path\To\Source" "Z:\Path\To\Dest" /MIR /MT:16`.
- **With PowerToys Feature:** Performs the exact same robust operation seamlessly via two right-clicks directly inside Windows Explorer.

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: [CmdPal Dock] Dock renders empty when bands resolve before DockControl loads (centre visibility never re-evaluated) — hit on every RDP reconnect
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.101.2632

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

Setup: Windows 11 22631, used through Remote Desktop with two 2560x1440 monitors. Dock enabled at the bottom of the primary monitor, ~13 bands pinned in the Center region (installed apps + Windows Terminal profile), Start = Home, End = Performance/Time bands.

Reliable reproduction (no RDP needed):

1. Kill Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe.
2. Relaunch it the way the runner does: explorer.exe x-cmdpal://background (a plain shell:AppsFolder launch behaves the same).
3. Look at the dock.

In roughly 2 out of 3 launches the dock appears as an empty 38 px strip with no bands. The other launches show all bands. Nothing in the settings changes between attempts.

The same thing happens on every Remote Desktop reconnect: Windows renames the displays (\\.\DISPLAY17/18 → \\.\DISPLAY33/34), DockWindowManager tears down the dock window and creates a new one for the renamed monitor, and the new dock comes up empty and stays empty until Command Palette is restarted (with the same 1-in-3 odds) or until edit mode is toggled (see below).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The rebuilt dock shows the pinned bands.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The dock window exists (AppBar reserves space, acrylic strip is drawn) but shows no bands. UI Automation on the PowerDock window shows only the Start and End ListViews at their 48 px MinWidth and no centre region at all (its bounding rect is empty, i.e. collapsed). The view model is fine: the log shows DockViewModel.SetupBands resolving every pinned band except the ones that genuinely no longer exist, and the settings file is intact.

Deterministic workaround, which also points at the cause: right-click the dock background → Edit Dock → Discard. The bands appear immediately (0 → 11 list items in UIA), no restart needed.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

Analysis (v0.101.2632.0 sources)
I believe this is a race in Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Dock/DockControl.xaml.cs:

- The constructor calls UpdateEditMode(false) → UpdateCenterVisibility() → ContentGrid.IsCenterVisible = IsEditMode || ViewModel.CenterItems.Count > 0. At construction time CenterItems is still empty, so the centre region is collapsed.
- CenterItems.CollectionChanged += CenterItems_CollectionChanged is subscribed only in DockControl_Loaded, and DockControl_Loaded does not call UpdateCenterVisibility() itself.
- DockWindowManager.CreateDockForMonitor does window.Show(); viewModel.InitializeBands(); back to back. SetupBands posts the InPlaceUpdateList onto the UI scheduler, so the items frequently land in CenterItems before Loaded fires. Those CollectionChanged notifications are never observed, IsCenterVisible stays false, and nothing re-evaluates it afterwards because later SetupBands passes produce identical lists (no change → no event).
- Anything that fires UpdateCenterVisibility() later fixes it: entering edit mode (UpdateEditMode → UpdateCenterVisibility), or any genuine change to CenterItems (pin/unpin, or an app re-index that swaps the band view models). That matches what I observe.

Suggested fix: call UpdateCenterVisibility() at the end of DockControl_Loaded (after subscribing), or subscribe to CenterItems.CollectionChanged in the constructor.

Note this is separate from #48516 / PR #49814 (monitor identification). That fix is present in this build; it stops the config corruption, but every monitor rebuild still goes through CreateDockForMonitor and therefore hits this race. It may also explain the "bands disappear after Modern Standby, restart brings them back" symptom in #50568, since a wake also triggers WM_DISPLAYCHANGE and a rebuild.

Evidence

title: Keyboard Manager: Support opening multiple URLs with a single shortcut mapping
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Currently, the Keyboard Manager "Open URL" action type supports only a single URL per shortcut mapping. Users who want to open multiple URLs simultaneously (e.g., a set of work-related tabs) must create separate mappings with different shortcut keys for each URL.

Proposed behavior: Allow the "Open URL" action to accept multiple URLs (one per line). When the shortcut is triggered, all listed URLs open at once in the default browser.

The URL input TextBox in the remapping dialog would become multi-line (similar to the existing "Text" action type), and each line would be treated as a separate URL to open. The engine would iterate through each URL and call ShellExecute for each one.

Example:

Shortcut: Ctrl + Shift + W
URLs:

https://mail.google.com
https://calendar.google.com
https://github.com/notifications
Result: All three URLs open in the default browser when the shortcut is pressed.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Scenario when this would be used?
Morning workflow launch: Many power users start their day by opening the same set of websites — email, calendar, project boards, dashboards. Currently this requires either:

Multiple separate KBM shortcut mappings (wastes shortcut combinations)
A browser extension or bookmark folder (not keyboard-driven)
A batch script mapped to a shortcut (extra complexity)
With multi-URL support, a single shortcut like Ctrl+Alt+W could open an entire "workspace" of URLs instantly. This is especially valuable for:

Context switching — Switch between "work" and "personal" tab sets with different shortcuts
Project-specific setups — Open all relevant dashboards/docs for a specific project
Presentation prep — Open demo URLs before a meeting
Development workflows — Open local dev server, API docs, and CI dashboard together

### Supporting information

Technical feasibility
The change is backward-compatible and minimally invasive. The existing uriToOpen string field can store newline-delimited URLs without requiring changes to:

The P/Invoke interop boundary
The C++/CLI wrapper layer
The JSON settings schema (the "openUri" key already stores a string)


Affected module
Keyboard Manager — New Editor UI (KeyboardManagerEditorUI)
Specifically the "Open URL" action type in shortcut remapping

title: Mouse Without Borders - Use Service does not work before Windows login after fresh boot
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362 - Stable

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Two PCs are connected to the same LAN.

MAIN PC:
- Windows 10
- Hostname: HeadOffice-I7
- Physical keyboard and mouse are connected to this PC.

REMOTE PC:
- Windows 11
- Hostname: DESKTOP-BBPG03H
- PowerToys Mouse Without Borders has "Use Service" enabled.
- PowerToys was run as Administrator when enabling the service.

2. Reboot the Windows 11 remote PC.

3. Wait at the Windows login/password screen without logging in.

4. The Windows 11 PC is already connected to the network and responds normally to ping, but Mouse Without Borders cannot control it.

5. At this stage TCP ports 15100 and 15101 on the Windows 11 PC are not listening/reachable.

6. Log into the Windows 11 PC using its local physical mouse/keyboard.

7. Immediately after login, Mouse Without Borders starts automatically, ports 15100 and 15101 become available, and the Windows 10 PC can control it normally.

Important: After Windows has logged in once, pressing Win+L works correctly and Mouse Without Borders CAN control the Windows lock screen.

Already verified:
- Use Service is enabled.
- PowerToys was genuinely running elevated when Use Service was enabled.
- PowerToys.MWB.Service exists and runs as LocalSystem.
- Service startup type is the default DEMAND_START.
- Service binary path is correct.
- The service was deleted and recreated through PowerToys.
- Firewall and network connectivity are working.
- Both PCs communicate normally after login.
- Security key and machine configuration are correct.
- No machine-level PowerToys policy exists under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\PowerToys disabling the feature.
- The Windows 10 PC is already running Mouse Without Borders before login and repeatedly attempts to connect to the Windows 11 PC.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

With "Use Service" enabled, Mouse Without Borders should allow the Windows 10 PC to control the Windows 11 PC at the Windows login/password screen immediately after a fresh boot, before the first user login.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

After a fresh boot, Mouse Without Borders does not work at the Windows 11 login/password screen.

It only becomes available after I log into the Windows 11 PC locally for the first time.

After that first login, Mouse Without Borders works normally, including on the lock screen after pressing Win+L.

This appears very similar to PowerToys issue #29060.

Could you please confirm whether controlling the Windows login screen immediately after a fresh boot is currently supported by Mouse Without Borders Service?

If yes, what should start or trigger PowerToys.MWB.Service before the first user login?

If this is a known bug, is there currently a fix or supported workaround?

title: Improve Command Palette UI: Clarify distinction between “Extensions” and “Manage fallback order”
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

In the PowerToys Command Palette settings, the section "Extensions" contains an entry called "Manage fallback order". From a user perspective, this suggests that the fallback order controls the priority or ordering of all extensions, including third-party plugins.

However, the fallback order only applies to command providers (ShellExecute, PATH, app protocols, Windows apps, PowerToys commands). Plugins such as PaletteShell do not appear in this list because they are not command providers and therefore cannot be prioritized.

This UI structure is confusing. Users expect installed extensions to appear in the fallback list. When they do not appear, it looks like a bug or installation issue. The fact that this is "works as designed" is not obvious. The UI creates an incorrect expectation about what can be configured.

Suggested improvements:

- Split the Extensions section into "Plugins" (non-prioritizable) and "Command providers" (prioritizable).

- Rename "Manage fallback order" to something more precise, such as "Command provider priority" or "Fallback order of command sources".

- Add an explanatory note: "Plugins are functional extensions and do not participate in the fallback order."

- Display plugins separately or in a disabled/greyed-out list to indicate that they cannot be reordered.

Why this matters:
The current UI leads users to believe they are doing something wrong or that the software is malfunctioning. A clearer separation between plugins and command providers would improve usability and prevent misunderstandings.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When users install additional Command Palette extensions (e.g., third‑party plugins like PaletteShell), they expect these extensions to appear in the fallback order list and to be reorderable. The current UI suggests that all extensions are covered by the fallback order, which leads users to believe something is wrong when their plugin does not appear. A clearer UI would help users understand when and why fallback ordering applies.

title: Command Pallette - Installed apps - User defined filters
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The Installed Apps extension in Command Palette indexes every Start Menu shortcut, including many that I never want to launch from the palette. The most common example is uninstaller shortcuts ("Uninstall XYZ", "Uninstall ABC Tool", etc.). They clutter the results and often rank higher than the app I actually want.

Will be nice if there is a setting to the Installed Apps extension where the user can define a list of exclusion patterns. Any app or shortcut whose name matches a pattern is hidden from search results. Or something like this...
```
Uninstall*
*Readme*
*Help*
*Documentation*
```

### Scenario when this would be used?

# Suggested behavior:

- Case-insensitive matching.
- Support for simple wildcards (*), and optionally regex for advanced users.
- Optionally allow matching on the target path as well as the display name (e.g. exclude everything pointing to unins000.exe).
- Changes apply immediately, with no restart required.

# Alternatives considered

- Deleting the shortcuts from the Start Menu folders works, but installers recreate them on updates, and it affects the Start Menu itself, not just Command Palette.
- A per-item "Hide from results" context menu action would also be useful as a complementary feature, but pattern-based filtering scales much better when there are dozens of similar entries.

### Supporting information

AND THANK U!

title: [Screen Ruler] DIP measurement unit cannot be selected
body: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.102 (current main) ### Installation method Dev build in Visual Studio ### Area(s) with issue? Screen ruler ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run PowerToys 2. Enable Screen Ruler 3. Select "Display-independent pixels (DIP)" for the **Extra units of measurement** option ### ✔️ Expected Behavior The value is selected and when opening the tool, the measurements are given in both pixels and DIPs. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The value reverts to showing "Centimeters" immediately. When opening Screen Ruler, measurements are given in pixels and centimeters. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4ede1c0-dd97-4dc7-9b0f-34a9afb25b33 ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information This looks like it's related to the NormalizeUnitsOfMeasureIndex method mapping 4 to 2 (the index of DIPs is 4, and this also corresponds to the legacy enum value of 4): ```csharp internal static int NormalizeUnitsOfMeasureIndex(int value) { return value switch { // Before the units selector was added, this setting stored Measurement::Unit // enum values. Preserve the user's centimetre/millimetre choice during migration. 4 => 2, 8 => 3, >= DefaultUnitsOfMeasureIndex and <= MaximumUnitsOfMeasureIndex => value, _ => DefaultUnitsOfMeasureIndex, }; } ``` Also it looks like the MaximumUnitsOfMeasureIndex wasn't updated when DIPs was added: ```csharp private const int MaximumUnitsOfMeasureIndex = 3; ``` ### Other Software _No response_

title: CTRL+Z stop working if zoomit is active (erroneous association with draw function makes it useless)
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

12.22

### Installation method

Microsoft Store

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

### 🔴 [FIX] ZoomIt hijacking Ctrl+Z (global Undo) even when inactive

If ZoomIt is stealing your global **Ctrl+Z** shortcut (forcing Draw mode or breaking the Undo command in your IDEs, text editors, or graphic software) even when you are not actively using the app, the issue is caused by a low-level keyboard hook regression triggered by empty (0) hotkey values in the registry. 

### 🔍 The Hidden Behavior (Why it breaks after clicking OK):

Comparing the Windows Registry before and after shows that **the registry values remain 100% identical**. The bug does not corrupt the saved data. Instead, it's a runtime memory issue: when you open ZoomIt's Options dialog and click **OK**, ZoomIt destroys and re-registers its low-level keyboard hooks on the fly. 

If the **DrawToggleKey** is unmapped or left at default fallback values, the hot-reload process gets confused and registers a broad listener that intercepts the un-modified, system-wide Ctrl+Z across the entire OS. Furthermore, upon a normal exit, ZoomIt dumps its current memory state, overwriting any external registry modifications you made while it was open. 

### 🛠️ The Definitive Workaround:

To fix this permanently, you must assign a valid, non-zero shortcut to the standalone drawing tool to satisfy ZoomIt's validation engine, and perform a clean cold launch of the process. 

### Option 1: Manual Registry Fix

1. **Close ZoomIt** completely (Right-click its icon in the system tray and select **Exit**).
2. Press Win + R, type regedit, and hit **Enter**.
3. Navigate to: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Sysinternals\ZoomIt
4. Modify the DWORD value **DrawToggleKey** and set it to **34b** (Hexadecimal), which maps it to an innocent shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+L).
5. Relaunch **ZoomIt**. *Note: If you ever open the Options dialog and click OK again, the bug will return until the next clean restart.*

### Option 2: Automated Restart Batch Script

Since ZoomIt overwrites the registry on standard exit and breaks when hitting "OK" in the GUI, you can use this quick automation script. It forcefully terminates the process (preventing the registry overwrite dump), restores the safety key, and performs a clean cold launch. 

Create a Restart_ZoomIt.bat file and paste the following code (adjust the path to your executable if necessary): 

cmd

@echo off
title Restart ZoomIt Fix

echo Force closing ZoomIt...
taskkill /f /im ZoomIt64.exe >nul 2>&1
taskkill /f /im ZoomIt.exe >nul 2>&1
timeout /t 1 /nobreak >nul

echo Restoring DrawToggleKey to prevent Ctrl+Z hijacking...
REG ADD "HKCU\Software\Sysinternals\ZoomIt" /v "DrawToggleKey" /t REG_DWORD /d 843 /f >nul

echo Cold launching ZoomIt cleanly...
start "" "C:\Tools\ZoomIt\ZoomIt64.exe"
exit

Use code with caution.

*(Note: 843 is the decimal equivalent of 34b, which maps to Ctrl+Shift+L and keeps your system's global Ctrl+Z perfectly safe).*

title: Add customizable mouse gestures
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add built-in support for customizable mouse gestures, similar to the functionality provided by third-party tools such as MouseInc and other mouse gesture utilities.

The default activation button should be the right mouse button, since right-button mouse gestures are already a familiar interaction pattern in many mouse gesture applications. Users could hold the right mouse button and move the mouse in different directions to trigger actions.

For example:

Right mouse button + Left → Back
Right mouse button + Right → Forward
Right mouse button + Down → Close the current window
Right mouse button + Up → Maximize the current window

The system could also support more advanced gesture patterns, such as L-shaped, U-shaped, and circular gestures.

The configuration interface should provide functionality similar to established mouse gesture utilities such as MouseInc, including customizable gesture patterns, configurable actions, gesture sensitivity, and application-specific profiles.

Users should be able to assign gestures to common Windows actions, such as:

Back / Forward
Close, minimize, or maximize the current window
Switch between windows or virtual desktops
Open File Explorer, Settings, or other applications
Copy, paste, undo, and other common commands
Execute custom keyboard shortcuts or commands

Gestures should be configurable in Windows Settings, with options to enable or disable mouse gestures, change the activation button, customize gesture patterns and actions, and create application-specific profiles.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Mouse gestures are particularly useful for users who frequently navigate Windows with a mouse. For example, holding the right mouse button and moving the mouse left could perform Back, while moving right could perform Forward. A downward gesture could close the current window, and an upward gesture could maximize it.

This would reduce the need to move the mouse to buttons or repeatedly use keyboard shortcuts, making common actions faster and more accessible. It would also reduce the need to install third-party utilities such as MouseInc just to obtain basic mouse gesture functionality.

title: [Shortcut Guide] Taskbar indicators appear for all apps, instead of only when TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts are defined
body: ### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel 0.102 (current main) ### Installation method Dev build in Visual Studio ### Area(s) with issue? Shortcut Guide ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run PowerToys and enable Shortcut Guide 2. Focus an application which has a manifest that does not define "<TASKBAR1-9>" shortcuts, e.g. Chrome 3. Trigger the Shortcut Guide ### ✔️ Expected Behavior Only the main overlay is shown, displaying the application's shortcuts. ### ❌ Actual Behavior Both the application shortcuts and the taskbar indicators are shown: ### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file _No response_ ### Additional Information This looks like a bug related to `ShortcutGuideActivationAction.ShowFullGuide()` calling `UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout()`. That routine ends with an unconditional: ```csharp this.TaskbarPane.Visibility = Visibility.Visible; ``` Because this is called _after_ `MainPaneControl.Open()` which _correctly_ sets `exposesTaskbarSection` to false via the `SelectionChanged` event raising `SelectedAppTaskbarVisibilityChanged` via `SetNavItems()`, the just-set `Visibility.Collapsed` value is immediately overridden and the indicators are shown. This looks like it came about during the transition from the dual windows solution to the single `OverlayWindow` and it seems to be an 'ensure the taskbar pane visibility/layout is current' insurance, but the unconditional setting of Visibility to Visible behaviour was missed. This is perhaps understandable, as the method name refers to layout not visibility. I just asked a friendly AI to sketch out what the current control flow is for the 'correct' setting of the pane's visibility and it's: ``` App.HandleActivationAsync() ↳ MainPaneControl.Open() ↳ Task.Run(GetAllCurrentApplicationIds) ↳ SetNavItems() ↳ UI control property assignment: WindowSelector.SelectedItem = MenuItems[0] ↳ NavigationView.SelectionChanged event ↳ MainPaneControl reads file, checks ↳ fires SelectedAppTaskbarVisibilityChanged event ↳ OverlayWindow receives event ↳ toggles TaskbarPane.Visibility ``` This is...er, 'non-obvious'; it's no wonder it wasn't spotted and the extra line was added. Business logic shouldn't be triggered as an accidental side-effect of UI control selection. ### Other Software _No response_

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I'd like the ability to let apps keep PC awake to the Awake module. For example, if I add "winword.exe" to the list of apps that'll keep PC awake to the Awake module, the PC won't go to sleep until an app exits or a .EXE is removed from the list.

### Scenario when this would be used?

1. Make sure that the Awake module is enabled.
2. Add a .EXE to the list of apps that'll keep the PC awake.
3. When an app runs, the PC will be kept awake indefinitely.
4. (Optional) Turn on an option to keep screen on.

### Supporting information

Adding an .EXE to the list of apps that'll keep the PC awake will prevent the PC and the screen (if optionally turning an option to keep it on) from going to sleep. If either a user exits an app or a .EXE is removed from the list, the PC will go back to sleep if an app is left running at an idle period of time.

title: [Hosts File Editor] IP validation rebuilds a 665-character Regex on every call
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` @ cb25632f (built from source)

### Installation method

Built from source (GitHub)

### Running as admin

No

### Area(s) with issue?

Hosts File Editor

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Hosts File Editor with a large hosts file (e.g. a few thousand entries — blocklist-style hosts files are commonly this size).
2. Note the time spent parsing/loading.
3. Open the add/edit entry dialog and type into the **Address** field.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Address validation is cheap — it's a regex match against a short string.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Validation is far more expensive than the match itself, because a brand new `Regex` is built for every single call.

### Additional Information

`src/modules/Hosts/HostsUILib/Helpers/ValidationHelper.cs`:

```csharp
public static bool ValidIPv6(string address)
{
    if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(address))
    {
        return false;
    }

    var regex = new Regex("^(([0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}:){7,7}[0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}|...");
    return regex.IsMatch(address);
}
```

`ValidIPv4` has the same shape. Neither instance is cached, so on every call the pattern is re-parsed and a fresh matcher is constructed. The IPv6 pattern is **665 characters**, and that construction dominates — the actual `IsMatch` against a short address is trivial by comparison.

Measuring the two patterns against the same .NET regex engine, constructing per call was about **13× slower** than reusing a single instance. (Absolute numbers include the measurement harness's own overhead, so treat the ratio as the meaningful figure.)

This is a hot path:

- `Entry.OnAddressChanged` calls straight into `ValidIPv4`/`ValidIPv6`, so both run **once per entry** while the hosts file is parsed.
- The same property setter fires on **every keystroke** in the address box of the add/edit dialog.

### Proposed fix

Replace both with `[GeneratedRegex]` partial methods. The source generator emits a cached, specialised matcher at compile time — no per-call construction, no runtime pattern parsing — and avoids the reflection-based construction path, which suits the repo's AOT goals. `[GeneratedRegex]` is already used in `OcrTextFormatter`, `ClipboardItemHelper`, `PowerToysShortcutsPopulator` and `DevRibbonViewModel`.

The patterns themselves would carry over byte for byte, so matching behaviour is unchanged and the existing `ValidationHelperTest` suite still applies.

I have this ready and am happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.

title: [Settings] LanguageHelper.LoadLanguage can leak the language.json file handle on a read failure
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` @ 6896d763 (built from source)

### Installation method

Built from source (GitHub)

### Running as admin

No

### Area(s) with issue?

Settings

### Steps to reproduce

Code-level defect. The leak requires `language.json` to fail mid-read (I/O error, or a truncated/locked file), so there is no clean UI repro.

`src/common/ManagedCommon/LanguageHelper.cs`:

```csharp
try
{
    var inputStream = File.Open(file, FileMode.Open);
    StreamReader reader = new StreamReader(inputStream);
    string data = reader.ReadToEnd();
    inputStream.Close();
    reader.Dispose();

    return JsonSerializer.Deserialize<OutGoingLanguageSettings>(data, ...).LanguageTag;
}
catch (Exception)
{
}
```

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The handle on `language.json` is released on every path, including failures.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

On a read failure the `FileStream` stays open until the finalizer runs, holding a handle on the settings file.

### Additional Information

The stream is opened without a `using`, and `inputStream.Close()` only runs on the success path. `ReadToEnd()` is inside the `try`, so an I/O failure there leaves the stream unclosed while the `catch` silently swallows the exception.

`language.json` is also written by the settings UI, so a stale read handle can make a subsequent write fail.

**Proposed fix.** Replace the manual open/read/close with `File.ReadAllText`, which closes the handle on every path including exceptions. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged — the method still returns `string.Empty` when the file is missing or cannot be parsed.

I have a fix ready and am happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.

title: [Workspaces] Application icon creation leaks GDI icon handles and bitmaps
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` @ 6896d763 (built from source)

### Installation method

Built from source (GitHub)

### Running as admin

No

### Area(s) with issue?

Workspaces

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Workspaces editor with several applications captured.
2. Watch the process's **GDI objects** count in Task Manager (Details tab → add the *GDI objects* column) as application icons are rendered.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

GDI object count stays stable — each icon's native resources are released once built.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The count grows as icons are built and never comes back down. GDI objects are capped per process (10,000 by default), so this accumulates.

### Additional Information

**Root cause.** `src/modules/Workspaces/WorkspacesCsharpLibrary/Models/BaseApplication.cs`:

```csharp
var bitmap = new Bitmap(uri.LocalPath);
var iconHandle = bitmap.GetHicon();
_icon = Icon.FromHandle(iconHandle);
```

Three separate leaks:

1. **Leaked `HICON`.** `Bitmap.GetHicon()` returns a handle the caller owns, and [`Icon.FromHandle`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.drawing.icon.fromhandle) does not take ownership — the docs state the handle must be released with `DestroyIcon`. Both call sites (packaged-app branch and Edge/Chrome PWA branch) store the wrapper in `_icon` and drop the handle, leaking one GDI icon object per application.
2. **Leaked source `Bitmap`s.** The bitmaps decoded from the package logo and from the PWA icon file are never disposed.
3. **Leaked `previewBitmap`.** In `IconBitmapImage`, `Bitmap previewBitmap = new Bitmap(32, 32)` is never disposed — only the surrounding `Graphics` and `MemoryStream` are.

`BaseApplication` implements `IDisposable`, but `Dispose()` only calls `GC.SuppressFinalize(this)` and releases nothing.

Separately, `DrawHelper.SaveBitmap` leaves its `EncoderParameters` (which owns unmanaged memory) undisposed, and it runs once per rendered icon.

**Proposed fix.** Clone the icon and then destroy the handle — the pattern already used in Peek's `BitmapHelper` (`using var icon = (Icon)Icon.FromHandle(hicon).Clone();` … `DestroyIcon(hicon)`) and in the Command Palette toolkit's `ThumbnailHelper` — and dispose the remaining bitmaps and encoder parameters.

I have a fix ready (builds clean, 0 warnings) and am happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.

title: [PT Run][Unit Converter] `sqmi` and `sqmil` expand to invalid units, so square-mile conversions return no result
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

`main` @ 6896d763 (built from source)

### Installation method

Built from source (GitHub)

### Running as admin

No

### Area(s) with issue?

PowerToys Run

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open PowerToys Run.
2. Type `10 sqmi in sqkm`.

Same for `10 sqmil in sqnmi`.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

A conversion result — 10 mi² ≈ 25.9 km².

Other square shorthands (`sqft`, `sqcm`, `sqin`, `sqm`, `sqkm`, `sqmm`, `sqnmi`, `sqyd`, …) all work, so `sqmi` is expected to as well.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

No result at all. The query silently returns nothing.

### Additional Information

**Root cause.** `InputInterpreter.SquareHandler` expands the shorthand with:

```csharp
Regex.Replace(split[1], "sq(s|μm|mm|cm|dm|m|km|mil|in|ft|yd|mi|nmi)", "$1²");
```

.NET regex alternation is **ordered** — it takes the first branch that matches, not the longest. The single-character `m` branch precedes `mi` and `mil`, so those tokens get truncated:

| input | actual | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `sqmi` | `m²i` | `mi²` |
| `sqmil` | `m²il` | `mil²` |

Neither `m²i` nor `m²il` is parseable by UnitsNet, so `UnitHandler.Convert` produces no results and the query returns nothing.

Verified directly against the .NET regex engine.

**Proposed fix.** Reorder the alternation longest-first, so multi-character tokens are tried before their single-character prefixes. I confirmed this changes the output for `sqmi` and `sqmil` **only** — every other token, including compound ones like `cm/sqs`, `BTU/s·sqin` and `cal/h·sqcm`, expands byte-identically.

I have a fix with regression tests ready (full `Community.PowerToys.Run.Plugin.UnitConverter.UnitTest` suite passes, 52/52) and am happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.

title: A tool to allow moving where new notifications display from the primary monitor to a secondary monitor (and perhaps to other positions on the display)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

It can be distracting or annoying to get pop up notifications on the main display, especially if you are sharing your main screen in a virtual meeting. Focus can be used to suppress notifications but there are cases where someone may still want to receive them, but not on the main shared window. You could share a different window but it may not be ergonomic if you are sharing or presenting for a long period and swapping monitor assignments frequently is an inconvenience. You could also reassign the primary display, but that has other knock-on effects for many settings and it may not be desirable.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Anyone who wants to reassign the location of toast notifications could use this in a multi-display setting.

### Supporting information

There are a number of existing requests for such a feature on various forms, reddit, etc. for folks looking for this sort of thing. Other tools proport to have this functionality but in workspace environments having it in powertoys which is often approved, instead of seeking IT approval for some unknown software tool that messes with system-wide notifications is preferable.

I thank those that took the time to read and consider.

title: FancyZones: give windows with no zone history somewhere to land
body:
﻿Right now FancyZones only places a window automatically if it has been snapped before. With "Move newly created windows to their last known zone" on, an app that was previously zoned goes back to its last zone. But the first time you ever open an app, or any app you have never manually snapped, FancyZones does nothing: the window just opens wherever Windows decides to put it, and you drag it into a zone yourself. There is currently no setting anywhere that changes this. For anyone who reinstalls an app, resets their zone history, or just runs a lot of one-off tools and dialogs, this means FancyZones effectively guides only the windows you have already trained it on, and leaves everything else on its own.

I looked through the existing backlog for anything that already covers this and found two issues that are close but not quite the same thing:

- #9527 is about which *layout* gets applied to a monitor or virtual desktop that FancyZones has never seen before. It solves "what grid of zones shows up here" for an unrecognized screen. It says nothing about where an individual window, snapped or not, lands inside whatever layout is already active. A monitor could have a perfectly good layout applied and this proposal would still do nothing, because the gap is per-window, not per-monitor.
- #16964 is about pinning a specific application's remembered zone so it stops drifting between its last few positions. That is a fix for existing history, for apps that already have some. It does not help the very common case of a window with no history at all, which is what this issue is about, and it does not extend to windows generally, only to whichever apps you have explicitly locked.

Both are useful and neither one gives a new window, or one from an app you have never zoned, a default place to go. I think this is worth handling on its own rather than folded into either.

What I would propose, roughly: a per-layout setting, off by default and out of the way (collapsed) so it does not clutter the FancyZones settings page for people who do not want it, that lets you pick either a single zone or a contiguous range of zones as the fallback for that layout. When a window has no last-known-zone to go back to (either because the toggle for that is off, or because this is genuinely the first time), and this fallback is configured and still makes sense for the zone count on that monitor, the window goes there instead of nowhere. If last-known-zone history exists and that toggle is on, history would still win, this is only for the gap that's left over once history has nothing to offer.

I'm not attached to the details here and would rather get the direction right before writing any of it. Two things I'd actually like your input on: does this fit where you want FancyZones settings to go, or do you see this differently? And would you rather this live per layout as I described, or as a single global fallback that applies everywhere regardless of which layout is active? I can see arguments either way and would rather build the one you'd actually want to maintain.

title: Quick-Accent DEactivation key
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

There are 3 ways this could be implemented:

1. **Press the Deactivation Key AFTER down-pressing the letter key.** 
When the Quick Accent popup is activated, pressing a modifier key (like <kbd>Enter</kbd> <kbd>Space</kbd>, or <kbd>Esc</kbd>) should _deactivate_ it, to allow Windows' default Character Repeat behavior to occur. (Note: The modifier key should be intercepted, so e.g. pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> would NOT send the Enter keyevent to any other window.)
2. **Press the Deactivation Key BEFORE down-pressing the letter key.**
To suppress the Quick Accent popup from activating in the first place, press down a modifier key _before_ the letter key, thereby allowing Character Repeat to occur. (The main challenge I see with this option is to find a key that doesn't already send an (important) keyevent when pressed. Perhaps <kbd>CapsLock</kbd>? It would require intercepting the default <kbd>CapsLock</kbd> keyevent so that system's CapsLock state is changed on key*up*, instead of the default key*down*. That way, to perform a normal CapsLock keypress, the user would press and release <kbd>CapsLock</kbd>, like normal; to use it as the QA Deactivation Key, the user would press down <kbd>CapsLock</kbd>, press and hold down a letter key, then release both. When used as the Deactivation Key, the system CapsLock state should not change.)
3. **Triple-press-then-hold a letter key to suppress QA and trigger "character repeat."**
To suppress Quick Accent from activating, the letter key is quickly pressed 3 times and held down on the 3rd press. Unlike options #[]()1 and #[]()2, No separate modifier key is required. Since the point of Character Repeat is to write the same letter many times, this method basically "gets it started" by making the user type the first 2 manually; when the 3rd one is held down, Character Repeat takes over. (I suggested a *triple*-press-and-hold instead of *double-* in order to reduce the likelihood of accidental triggers. For example, typing the word "continuüm" requires the user `press + press-and-hold` the <kbd>U</kbd> key. However, I think it's very unlikely that a user would need to type the same letter 3 times with an accent on only the last one— aka my proposed action, `press + press + press-and-hold`).

### Scenario when this would be used?

Now that there's an option to activate Quick Accent by simply holding down the key without pressing any second key, it totally disables "character repeat," aka the default Windows behavior when holding down a key.

### Supporting information

This could be integrated with #23496, or it could be a separate key.

title: [Build] main CI fails ~80% of runs: 90-minute job timeouts and missing ARM64 PCHs
body:
## Summary

`main`'s CI has been failing most of the time for the past week — 16 of the last 20 runs. The failures look like infrastructure rather than code: **the same commit both passes and fails**, and the two recurring signatures (a 90-minute job timeout, and missing ARM64 precompiled headers across unrelated projects) are not tied to what changed.

I'm reporting this from the outside rather than proposing a fix, since I don't know the agent setup. Happy to be told it's already known and tracked elsewhere — I couldn't find an open issue for it.

## The same commit passes and fails

This is the part that rules out a code cause:

| Commit | Failed run | Succeeded run |
|---|---|---|
| `8e832ee7` | 388732 (30.9 min) | 388719 (53.4 min) |
| `71340eed` | 388644 (33.5 min) | 388617 (59.6 min) |
| `7dd034ff` | 388535 (32.4 min) | 388510 (60.4 min) |

All three failures are the ARM64 PCH signature below.

## Signature 1 — 90-minute job timeout (8 of 16 failures)

> The job running on agent SHINE-OSS-L 5 ran longer than the maximum time of 90 minutes.

Durations tell the story. Successful runs cluster at **53–61 minutes**; the timeouts are runs of the same work that drift past the cap:

| Result | Durations (min) |
|---|---|
| succeeded | 53.4, 58.2, 59.6, 60.4 |
| timed out | 91.1, 91.4, 91.9, 91.9, 92.6, 93.5, 93.9, 97.4 |

Build IDs: 388558, 388599, 388687, 388708, 388716, 388751, 388875, 388936.

A healthy run finishing at ~60 minutes against a 90-minute ceiling leaves only ~50% headroom, so ordinary variance in agent speed is enough to tip a run over. This looks less like "something got slow" and more like the cap being too close to the normal runtime.

## Signature 2 — missing ARM64 precompiled headers (5 of 16 failures)

> `src\modules\FileLocksmith\FileLocksmithCLI\tests\FileLocksmithCLITests.cpp(1,10): error C1083: Cannot open precompiled header file: 'ARM64\Release\FileLocksmithCLI.UnitTests.pch': No such file or directory`

It hits several unrelated projects in the same run — FileLocksmith, AltWindowCycle, Runner — and always fails fast (~30–35 min). Several unrelated projects losing their PCH simultaneously suggests build ordering/parallelism or agent workspace state rather than any one project's configuration.

Build IDs: 388535, 388644, 388732, 388804, 388881.

## Why this is worth fixing beyond the noise

For maintainers a flaky pipeline is cheap — re-queue and move on. For **PRs from forks it isn't**, because the pipeline needs an authorized user to comment `/azp run` before it will start at all. That gating is the right call for untrusted code, but it means an external contributor cannot re-run anything themselves: every retry costs a maintainer's attention.

Concretely, I asked for `/azp run` three times in this repo over the past week (#50352, #49276). One of those runs came back red for a Command Palette throughput test unrelated to the PR's changed files, so that request — and the maintainer's time spent on it — bought no signal at all. With `main` itself red, there's also no green baseline to compare a PR against, so "is this me or is this the pipeline?" takes a build-log dig every time.

## Questions

1. Is the 90-minute cap deliberate, or has the build simply grown into it? Raising it, or splitting the x64/ARM64 legs further, would remove most of these failures outright.
2. Is the ARM64 PCH failure known? Happy to open a separate issue for it if these are better tracked apart.

Data gathered 2026-09-16 from the public build history of the `PowerToys CI` pipeline on `refs/heads/main` (builds 388510–388936).

title: Add a persistent real-time network speed indicator to the Windows taskbar
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like to propose a lightweight PowerToys utility that displays real-time network throughput directly on the Windows taskbar.

The indicator could show both download and upload activity, for example:

↓ 12.4 MB/s   ↑ 2.1 MB/s

The display should represent current network traffic rather than performing an internet speed test. Ideally, users could enable or disable it from PowerToys settings and choose the preferred units (KB/s, MB/s, Mbps, etc.).

The goal is to provide a small, always-visible network activity indicator without requiring Task Manager, a separate application, or an open Command Palette/Dock window.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would be useful during large downloads/uploads, software updates, cloud backups, gaming, streaming, video calls, and general troubleshooting.

For example, when a download suddenly becomes slow, users could immediately see whether the network is actually transferring data without opening another application.

It would also be useful for users on Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or mobile hotspots who want to keep an eye on real-time bandwidth usage throughout the day.

The taskbar is particularly useful for this because it remains visible while working in other applications.

### Supporting information

Similar functionality is available through third-party utilities such as NetSpeedMonitor and TrafficMonitor, but having a lightweight implementation within PowerToys would provide a more integrated Windows experience.

PowerToys already has network monitoring functionality in the Command Palette Dock. This request is specifically for a persistent indicator on the standard Windows taskbar, so users can see current network throughput without opening the Dock or another application.

title: Feature Request: Custom Keyboard Shortcuts for Volume Control
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

**Feature Request: Custom Keyboard Shortcuts for Volume Control**

Please consider adding a feature to PowerToys that allows users to assign custom keyboard shortcuts/keys to control the Windows system volume.

For example, users could configure:

* `F13` → Volume Up
* `F14` → Volume Down
* `F15` → Mute

It would be especially useful for keyboards that don't have dedicated multimedia/volume keys. Users should be able to select any unused key or key combination and map it to **Volume Up, Volume Down, or Mute**.

Ideally, the feature would work globally across Windows, regardless of which application is currently active.

This would make PowerToys much more useful for users with basic keyboards that lack dedicated media controls.


### Scenario when this would be used?

For example, when I am watching YouTube or listening to music, I may want to quickly increase or decrease the system volume without reaching for the mouse or opening the Windows volume control.

If my keyboard has unused function keys, I could assign them to Volume Up and Volume Down and control the volume directly from the keyboard.

### Supporting information

Many keyboards do not have dedicated multimedia or volume control keys. PowerToys already provides useful keyboard customization features, so adding customizable system volume controls would allow users to turn unused keys into volume controls without needing a multimedia keyboard.

It would also be useful for users who have keyboards with programmable or extra function keys.

title: Mouse Without Borders sometimes doesn't reconnect after sleep/resume; "Refresh connections" doesn't recover it
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Preview (Insider)

### Installation method

GitHub (PowerToysSetup-0.101.2362.0-x64.exe), PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders, Settings

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect two machines with Mouse Without Borders (non-service mode).
2. Let one sleep with sign-in required on wake, then wake it and sign in.
3. Sometimes they don't reconnect, and stay disconnected.
4. On the Mouse Without Borders settings page, click **Refresh connections**.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

They reconnect after resume. Failing that, **Refresh connections** reconnects them or shows an error.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

They stay disconnected, and **Refresh connections** does nothing and shows no error. `Win+Ctrl+Alt+R`, the Dashboard's reconnect button, or restarting PowerToys recovers it.

### Additional Information

Windows 11 10.0.26200. From reading the source; line numbers are from `main`, and this code hasn't changed since 0.101.2362.0.

**1. Reconnect can be disabled at the lock screen and never re-armed.** When the network changes, `ScheduleReopenSocketsDueToNetworkChanges` (`InitAndCleanup.cs:253-277`) closes the sockets and sets `Common.Sk = null`. If the desktop is inactive at that moment (the lock screen), it also sets `PleaseReopenSocket = 0`, which stops the retry loop (`frmScreen.cs:427`). `PowerModes.Resume` doesn't re-arm it (`InitAndCleanup.cs:144-154`).

`HelperTimer_Tick` re-creates the sockets on return to the desktop (`frmScreen.cs:357-396`), but only if it closed them itself when the desktop went inactive; that's what resets `SecondOpenSocketTry` (`:332`). If the network handler closes them first, that path is skipped too. So this depends on event order, which fits it happening only sometimes.

**2. Refresh connections fails silently.** MWB's handler (`Program.cs:342`) would recover, so the call isn't arriving. Likely reasons (inferred, not instrumented):

- `IsConnected` (`MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs:318`) can still be true on a pipe broken by suspend, so the dead pipe is reused.
- `Reconnect()` is `void` (`:272`), so a failed call can't report back.
- A failed connection returns a `null` helper (`:371`), and `syncHelper?.Endpoint?.Reconnect()` (`:397`) then silently skips the call.

**Suggested fixes:** re-arm reconnect on resume or when the desktop becomes active again. Have **Refresh connections** signal `Constants.MWBReconnectEvent()` as the Dashboard does (`DashboardViewModel.cs:887`); MWB already listens for it (`CommandEventHandler.cs:33`).

### Other Software

N/A

title: Add configurable Light/Dark Wallpaper and Theme Paths with "Switch appearance + wallpaper/theme" actions
body:
### Summary
﻿
I'd like to request enhanced automation capabilities for the **Light Switch** module in PowerToys. Specifically, I want the ability to configure **absolute file paths** for light/dark wallpapers and light/dark themes, and to have dedicated actions that switch appearance **together with** wallpaper or theme in a single operation.
﻿
### Problem / Motivation
﻿
Currently, Light Switch allows switching between light and dark appearance modes, but:
﻿
- There is no way to specify **which wallpaper** should be applied for each mode.
- There is no way to specify **which Windows theme** (`.theme` file) should be applied for each mode.
- Users who want a fully consistent visual experience must manually change their wallpaper and theme every time the appearance switches, or rely on third-party scripts.
﻿
This is especially frustrating for users who:
﻿
- Use different wallpapers optimized for light vs. dark mode.
- Maintain separate `.theme` files (e.g., `Light.theme`, `Dark.theme`) with matching accent colors, cursor schemes, and sounds.
- Want a "one-click" or fully automatic switch that changes appearance, wallpaper, and theme together.
﻿
### Proposed Feature
﻿
Add the following configuration options to the Light Switch module settings, all accepting **absolute file paths**:
﻿
| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| **Light mode wallpaper path** | Absolute path to the wallpaper image (e.g., `C:\Users\Name\Pictures\light.jpg`) applied when switching to light mode. |
| **Dark mode wallpaper path** | Absolute path to the wallpaper image applied when switching to dark mode. |
| **Light mode theme path** | Absolute path to a `.theme` file applied when switching to light mode. |
| **Dark mode theme path** | Absolute path to a `.theme` file applied when switching to dark mode. |
﻿
And add the following **actions / triggers**:
﻿
| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| **Switch between light and dark appearance + wallpaper** | Toggles appearance mode and simultaneously applies the corresponding wallpaper. |
| **Switch between light and dark theme** | Applies the corresponding `.theme` file (which may also change wallpaper, accent color, etc.). |
﻿
In other words, I'd like to be able to bind a hotkey or schedule that performs any of these combinations:
﻿
1. Switch appearance only (current behavior).
2. Switch appearance **and** wallpaper.
3. Switch theme (which implicitly changes appearance + wallpaper + accent color, etc.).
﻿
### Expected Behavior
﻿
- When the user triggers "Switch between light and dark appearance + wallpaper":
 - The appearance mode toggles (light ↔ dark).
 - The wallpaper is set to the configured path for the new mode.
- When the user triggers "Switch between light and dark theme":
 - The `.theme` file for the new mode is applied via the standard Windows theming API.
- If a path is left empty, that part of the action is skipped gracefully (no error).
- Paths must support environment variables (e.g., `%USERPROFILE%`) or at least be validated as absolute paths.
- Invalid or missing files should produce a non-blocking notification or log entry, not a crash.
﻿
### Alternatives Considered
﻿
- Using a separate AutoHotkey script or scheduled task to change wallpaper/theme — works, but defeats the purpose of having an integrated PowerToys module and adds maintenance overhead.
- Manually switching wallpaper/theme — not practical for frequent switches.
﻿
### Additional Context
﻿
This would make the Light Switch module a complete "appearance automation" solution, covering:
﻿
- System appearance (light/dark)
- Wallpaper
- Windows theme (`.theme` file)

title: Light Switch The following functions are required
body:
### Describe the requested doc changes

﻿
**Title:** [Light Switch] Add "Sunset to Sunrise" mode based on custom geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude)
﻿

---
﻿
### Description
﻿
PowerToys Light Switch currently supports the following switching modes:
﻿
- **Sunset to Sunrise** (based on automatic location detection)
- **Switch between light and dark appearance** (fixed schedule)
- **Switch between light and dark appearance + wallpaper**
- **Switch between light and dark appearance + theme**
﻿
However, the existing **Sunset to Sunrise** mode relies on automatic location detection, which is often inaccurate or completely unavailable — especially on desktop PCs without GPS, on systems with location services disabled, or in regions where Windows location APIs return unreliable results.
﻿
### Proposed Feature
﻿
Add a new mode / option:
﻿
> **Sunset to Sunrise (custom geographic coordinates)**
﻿
This mode would allow the user to manually enter:
﻿
- **Latitude**
- **Longitude**
﻿
…and Light Switch would calculate sunrise and sunset times locally based on those coordinates, then switch between light and dark appearance accordingly.
﻿
### Why this is useful
﻿
1. **Reliability** — Manual coordinates remove dependence on Windows location services, which frequently fail or return incorrect data.
2. **Privacy** — Users who disable location services can still use the sunset/sunrise feature.
3. **Accuracy** — Users can specify the exact city or region they want the schedule based on, even if they are behind a VPN or in a different time zone.
4. **Consistency** — Desktop users without location hardware get the same functionality as laptop/mobile users.
﻿
### Suggested Implementation
﻿
- Add a new option in the Light Switch settings dropdown, e.g.:
 - `Sunset to Sunrise (custom coordinates)`
- When selected, show two input fields:
 - **Latitude** (e.g. `39.9042`)
 - **Longitude** (e.g. `116.4074`)
- Validate input range:
 - Latitude: `-90` to `90`
 - Longitude: `-180` to `180`
- Calculate sunrise/sunset using a standard solar position algorithm (e.g. NOAA solar calculator or similar).
- Optionally, allow the user to pick a location from a searchable city list instead of typing raw coordinates.
﻿
### Alternative / Additional Suggestion
﻿
In the **Switch between light and dark appearance** section (the checkbox-based mode), consider adding a sub-option:
﻿
> ☐ Use latitude/longitude for switching
﻿
This would let users combine a custom schedule with coordinate-based sunrise/sunset switching without creating an entirely separate mode.
﻿
### Additional Context
﻿
This request is similar in spirit to what tools like **Auto Dark Mode** and **Windows Auto Night Mode** already offer, and would bring Light Switch closer to feature parity with those utilities.
﻿

title: Screenshot When an External Display Is Connected
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Windowsノートパソコンに外部ディスプレイを接続しているとき、全画面のスクリーンショットを撮ると、外部ディスプレイとノートパソコンの両方の画面が一緒に撮影されてしまいます。

外部ディスプレイとノートパソコンの画面を個別に選択して、片方の画面だけを全画面スクリーンショットできる機能です

(↓English)
When an external display is connected to a Windows laptop, taking a full-screen screenshot captures both the external display and the laptop's screen.

Is there a feature that allows you to select either the external display or the laptop screen and take a full-screen screenshot of only that screen?


### Scenario when this would be used?

外部ディスプレイとノートパソコンの画面を使い分けているときに使用します。

例えば、外部ディスプレイで作業しながら、ノートパソコン側の画面だけをスクリーンショットしたい場合や、逆に外部ディスプレイに表示している内容だけをスクリーンショットしたい場合です。

現在は全画面スクリーンショットを撮ると、2つの画面がまとめて撮影されてしまうため、片方の画面だけを簡単に撮影できるようにしたい、という用途です。

↓English
This feature would be useful when using an external display together with a laptop screen.

For example, you may want to take a screenshot of only the laptop screen while working on the external display, or capture only the content shown on the external display.

Currently, a full-screen screenshot captures both screens together, so the purpose is to make it easy to capture only one of the two screens.

title: Window Hopper to switch between windows in FancyZones
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

1. Have the option to allow Window Hopper to switch between current active windows in a FancyZones zone, instead of switching through the windows of the current active application. (i.e. do the active application belongs to any zone? if yes, what other windows are currently docked in that zone, then show the selection pane for those windows instead)
2. Only display the selection pane within that specific zone, so as to not disrupt the vision of other open windows in other zones.
3. Option for other animation style for the selection pane perhaps.

### Scenario when this would be used?

When you have a stack of windows inside a certain zone?

### Supporting information

How I imagine Window Hopper could integrate with FancyZones intuitively:
1. Have shortcut keys to activate between the numbered FancyZones using the keyboard number row keys.
2. Have shortcut keys to rotate through the windows in that zone, like the current default `Alt` + `~` shortcut.

title: Window edge-hide / auto-hide (dock to screen edge and slide out, like WinAutoHide)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add a new PowerToys module (or a mode within FancyZones) that lets any window "dock" to a screen edge and automatically hide itself, leaving only a thin strip (a few pixels) visible at that edge. When the user moves the mouse cursor onto that strip, the window should slide back into full view; when the cursor/focus leaves it again, it should automatically slide back into its hidden, edge-docked state after a short, configurable delay.

Requested capabilities:
- Choose which edge (left / right / top / bottom) a window docks and hides to.
- A hotkey to toggle edge-hide on the currently active window (in addition to, or instead of, dragging it to the edge).
- Configurable auto-hide delay and reveal-trigger sensitivity (how much of the window stays visible as a "handle", how long the mouse must hover to reveal it).
- Correct behavior across multiple monitors and different DPI scaling settings.
- The docked window keeps running normally (not minimized) while hidden, so notifications/background activity are unaffected.

This is conceptually similar to how the Windows taskbar itself can auto-hide, but generalized to any window the user chooses.

### Scenario when this would be used?

As a power user I regularly keep secondary windows open that I only need to glance at or interact with occasionally — chat apps, monitoring/dashboard tools, reference documents, media players, to-do lists — but that otherwise permanently occupy screen space or get buried under other windows. This is especially painful on smaller or single-monitor setups, and even on multi-monitor setups it's useful to reclaim space on a monitor without fully closing or minimizing (and losing track of) a window.

Third-party AutoHotkey-based tools like WinAutoHide already implement exactly this workflow: pin a window to an edge, it slides mostly off-screen, and reappears when you touch that edge with the mouse. Having this built into PowerToys — with a proper settings UI, multi-monitor/DPI awareness, and no dependency on installing/trusting an unsigned third-party script — would fit naturally alongside FancyZones and other window-management utilities already in PowerToys, and would remove the need for power users to rely on unmaintained external tools for something this fundamental to window management.

### Supporting information

Reference implementations of this exact interaction already exist as third-party AutoHotkey scripts, which demonstrates demand and gives a working model for the UX:
- https://github.com/BoD/winautohide (original WinAutoHide)
- https://github.com/hzhbest/winautohide — "Hide any window to your selected side of screen with hot keys. Repop hidden window by cursor touching that side."
- https://github.com/windwhim/winautohidev2 (another maintained fork)

These require installing AutoHotkey separately and are not actively maintained/code-signed, which is exactly the kind of gap PowerToys is meant to fill for power users on Windows.

title: FancyZones: allow deploying layouts (custom layouts, templates, hotkeys, default layouts) through Microsoft DSC
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Since #49427, `PowerToys.DSC.exe` can deploy Keyboard Manager remappings through the `Microsoft.PowerToys/KeyboardManagerProfile` resource. FancyZones has the same gap: the `Microsoft.PowerToys/FancyZonesSettings` resource only manages the settings in `settings.json` (activation, appearance, behavior), while the layouts themselves are stored in separate files under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\PowerToys\FancyZones\` and can only be created in the FancyZones editor:

- `custom-layouts.json` (canvas and grid layouts)
- `layout-templates.json` (zone count and spacing of the built-in templates)
- `layout-hotkeys.json` (quick layout switch keys)
- `default-layouts.json` (layouts applied to new horizontal and vertical monitors)

### Scenario when this would be used?

- Setting up a new developer machine with `winget configure`, including the window layouts and the quick layout hotkeys, without opening the FancyZones editor.
- Keeping a fleet of machines on a standard set of layouts with `dsc config set`, and detecting drift with `dsc config test`.
- Exporting the layouts of a reference machine with `PowerToys.DSC.exe export` and reusing them in a configuration document.

### Supporting information

_No response_
