title: [FancyZones] Conditional layouts based on currently open applications
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add support for conditional or application-aware FancyZones layouts, where FancyZones automatically selects and applies a layout based on the combination of applications currently open.

For example:

If Chrome + VS Code are open: Side by Side

If Chrome + VS Code + Terminal are open: : Chrome 50%, the rest 50% terminal on top VSCode bottom

If another application such as Teams is opened, a different four-window layout could automatically be applied.

Users could define rules such as:

WHEN:
    chrome.exe
    Code.exe

USE:
    Layout A

WHEN:
    chrome.exe
    Code.exe
    WindowsTerminal.exe

USE:
    Layout B

FancyZones would re-evaluate the rules whenever a relevant application is opened or closed.

More specific rules should take priority. For example, Chrome + VS Code + Terminal should take precedence over Chrome + VS Code when all three applications are running.

Optionally, rules could also support window titles so that multiple windows belonging to the same application can be positioned differently.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would be useful when the preferred desktop layout changes depending on the applications being used.

For example, a developer may want different layouts for:

- Development: VS Code + Browser + Terminal
- Debugging: VS Code + localhost browser + Terminal
- Database work: VS Code + database client + Terminal
- Meetings: Teams + Browser + Notes

Currently, users need to manually switch FancyZones layouts or reposition windows when their workflow changes.

With conditional layouts, opening or closing an application could automatically reorganize the desktop into the appropriate layout.

The important distinction is that the layout is selected based on the combination of applications currently open, rather than permanently assigning a particular application to a particular zone.

### Supporting information

Conceptually, the feature would work like this:

Chrome + VS Code
        ↓
     Layout A

Chrome + VS Code + Terminal
        ↓
     Layout B

Chrome + VS Code + Terminal + Teams
        ↓
     Layout C

This could build on the existing FancyZones layout editor rather than introducing a completely separate window-management system.

Users could continue designing layouts using the current visual editor, with an additional rules section where they specify which applications activate each layout.

An advanced version could also support matching individual windows using properties such as window title.

For example:

Process: chrome.exe
Title contains: localhost

could be treated separately from:

Process: chrome.exe
Title contains: ChatGPT

This would make FancyZones behave more like a rule-driven dynamic window manager while preserving the existing FancyZones workflow.

title: Ability to hide/show the Command Palette dock with a keyboard shortcut
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

The ability to bind a keyboard shortcut to hide/show the Command Palette dock. For example, when bound to Ctrl+Alt+Shift+D (which shouldn't be the default shortcut due to conflicts with AltGr in some setups), the dock would toggle its visibility completely. This is separate from auto-hide since the dock will not appear until you use the keyboard shortcut again, effectively disabling it.

### Scenario when this would be used?

In my case, I use the keyboard shortcut to enable the dock when working on a project, and use the keyboard shortcut to disable the dock while playing a game (since I would not want it to appear while playing), eliminating the need to open PowerToys settings to disable it manually. It also removes clutter when I'm not working on a project and doing something else (e.g. Browsing the web).

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: [Command Palette] Investigate native HTML-only clipboard conversion after WinUI startup
body:
## Summary

Investigate the Command Palette clipboard-history extension's HTML-only conversion path following the Advanced Paste crash fixed in #50504.

**Status: potential exposure, not a reproduced Command Palette crash.** Advanced Paste's native conversion failure was reproduced on Windows 10 and Windows 11. Sharing a native API call is not sufficient to establish that Command Palette has the same failure.

## Known evidence

`GetClipboardTextOrHtmlTextAsync` in the clipboard-history extension still passes HTML clipboard content to `Windows.Data.Html.HtmlUtilities.ConvertToText`:

https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/bbe8649dee33a5771fbae361e1969cd82c0c719f/src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.ClipboardHistory/Helpers/ClipboardHelper.cs#L219-L236

The Advanced Paste investigation found a native fail-fast after WinUI startup, through `HtmlUtilitiesFactory::ConvertToText`, EdgeHTML/URI initialization, and `iertutil!CreateUriPriv`. Replacing that native path with managed conversion fixed the Advanced Paste reproduction without modifying application compatibility declarations.

Review follow-up: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/50504#discussion_r3984740187

## Investigation

1. Exercise Command Palette's real clipboard-history workflow with HTML-only CF_HTML, explicitly verifying that no plain-text clipboard format is present.
2. Test after normal WinUI startup on Windows 10 and Windows 11; capture the native call stack if the process terminates. Do not infer reproduction from Advanced Paste results.
3. Preserve plain-text precedence and distinguish valid empty fragments from malformed clipboard metadata.
4. If the defect reproduces, evaluate sharing a managed renderer with Advanced Paste in a separately scoped change, including dependency, trimming/AOT, and deployment implications. Do not simply add HtmlAgilityPack to every ManagedCommon consumer.

## Completion criteria

- Record a reproducible Command Palette failure and regression coverage, or evidence explaining why its runtime context is unaffected.
- If a fix is needed, demonstrate normal HTML-only clipboard behavior without native startup prewarming, manifest changes, or input fallbacks.
- Keep changes to shared conversion APIs and consumer dependencies explicit and reviewed.

title: Awake: Simplified Chinese timed-mode label misleadingly suggests a repeating action
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2.0 (installed executable ProductVersion; release channel not independently verified)

### Utility with translation issue

Awake

### 🌐 Language affected

Simplified Chinese (zh-CN)

### ❌ Actual phrase(s)

按时间间隔保持唤醒

English source: `Keep awake for a time interval`

Resource key: `Awake_TemporaryKeepAwakeSelector.Content`

Source: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw

### ✔️ Expected phrase(s)

保持唤醒一段时间

### ℹ Why is the current translation wrong

“按时间间隔” suggests the interval between repetitions of an action, rather than the duration of a continuous state. It can therefore make this option sound like it performs a wake-up action periodically.

This mode instead keeps the computer continuously awake for one selected duration. When that duration expires, it stops keeping the computer awake and normal power-plan behavior resumes.

“保持唤醒一段时间” expresses this meaning more naturally and clearly in Chinese. The adjacent duration controls let the user specify how long.

title: Command Palette Dock does not reuse Miracast monitor settings after reconnect
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2492.0 - Preview (Insider)

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Command Palette

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect a second Windows PC as a wireless display using Miracast / Windows **Projecting to this PC**.
2. Use **Extend** mode and keep the wireless display as a secondary monitor.
3. Enable Command Palette Dock on that monitor and add some dock items.
4. Disconnect the wireless display.
5. Reconnect the same device through Miracast, keeping it as a secondary monitor. In this setup, Windows assigns a different GDI source name after reconnecting.
6. Check the Dock and open Command Palette Dock settings.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The Dock should remain enabled on the same monitor and reuse its existing items and settings after reconnecting, even when Windows changes its GDI source name from, for example, `\\.\DISPLAY12` to `\\.\DISPLAY13`.

The visible display number may change; the persisted monitor configuration should still be associated with the same device.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The Dock disappears from the reconnected wireless display. A new disabled monitor configuration with empty item lists is created under the new GDI name, while the previous enabled configuration remains in settings under the old name.

The relevant entries in my Command Palette `settings.json` are:

| MonitorDeviceId | Enabled | Saved dock items |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `\\.\DISPLAY12` | `true` | 5 items in EndBands |
| `\\.\DISPLAY13` | `false` | StartBands, CenterBands and EndBands are empty |
| `\\.\DISPLAY14` | `false` | StartBands, CenterBands and EndBands are empty |

The old configuration has not been deleted; it is no longer associated with the reconnected monitor.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

Not attached. Focused API diagnostics and the relevant configuration entries are provided here.

### Additional Information

#### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, version `10.0.26300`.
- PowerToys `0.101.2492.0`, Preview (Insider), per-user installation.
- Command Palette package `0.12.12491.0`; product version `0.12.260906001-experimental`.
- Two active monitors: the built-in display and the Miracast secondary display.
- Wireless display adapter name: `Miracast display port driver V3`.

#### Device identity

Before and after reconnecting, this command returned the same PnP instance IDs:

```powershell
Get-PnpDevice -PresentOnly -Class Monitor |
    Select-Object Status, FriendlyName, InstanceId
```

```text
Built-in display: DISPLAY\BOE0D55\4&2878F4BF&0&UID8388688
Wireless display: DISPLAY\LEN4094\3&2E422DE1&1&UID256
```

A subsequent native API query mapped the currently connected `\\.\DISPLAY14` to the `LEN4094` device interface shown below.

#### Identified API argument error

[`MonitorService.BuildDisplayInfoMap`](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2492.0/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Services/MonitorService.cs#L244-L257) passes a non-null topology pointer while requesting only active paths:

```csharp
var topologyId = default(DISPLAYCONFIG_TOPOLOGY_ID);

result = PInvoke.QueryDisplayConfig(
    QUERY_DISPLAY_CONFIG_FLAGS.QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS,
    ref pathCount,
    paths,
    ref modeCount,
    modes,
    ref topologyId);
```

The [QueryDisplayConfig API documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-querydisplayconfig#remarks) requires `currentTopologyId` to be `NULL` for `QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS`; otherwise the function returns `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`. A zero-valued variable passed by reference is still a non-null pointer.

On this machine, a read-only native API comparison produced:

| Flags | currentTopologyId | Return value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS` | Pointer to a zero-initialized topology ID, as in the current code | `87 / ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` |
| `QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS` | `NULL` | `0 / ERROR_SUCCESS` |

With `NULL`, both active display paths were returned, and the source-name and target-name queries succeeded. The wireless display returned:

```text
GDI source name:   \\.\DISPLAY14
monitorDevicePath: \\?\DISPLAY#LEN4094#3&2e422de1&1&UID256#{e6f07b5f-ee97-4a90-b076-33f57bf4eaa7}
monitorFriendlyDeviceName: empty
```

`EnumDisplayDevicesW(..., EDD_GET_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NAME)` returned the same device interface path. The friendly name is empty, but `monitorDevicePath` is available.

The failing call returns an empty display-info map before the target-device-name queries are reached. [`EnumerateMonitors`](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/v0.101.2492.0/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Services/MonitorService.cs#L155-L163) then falls back to the volatile GDI name as `StableId`.

When the secondary monitor reconnects under a new GDI name, [`MonitorConfigReconciler`](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/071c25e115e8097117e26f6fcfe9901301307f7a/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/Settings/MonitorConfigReconciler.cs#L141-L193) creates a new disabled, empty configuration and retains the old one. Retrying the same invalid argument combination or debouncing display-change events cannot correct this error.

#### Proposed fix and verification scope

Use the existing five-argument overload in `Microsoft.Windows.CsWin32` `0.3.269`, which supplies a null native `currentTopologyId` pointer:

```csharp
result = PInvoke.QueryDisplayConfig(
    QUERY_DISPLAY_CONFIG_FLAGS.QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS,
    ref pathCount,
    paths,
    ref modeCount,
    modes);
```

Remove the unused `topologyId` variable. This should allow the existing hardware-path identification and legacy GDI-to-device-path migration to operate. A standalone C# comparison using the repository's CsWin32 version was compiled and run: the current six-argument overload returned 87, and the five-argument overload returned 0 and the device paths for both active monitors.

I would like to contribute a small PR for this fix and extend the existing reconnection test to cover a changed GDI name with an unchanged stable device ID.

The native API comparison above has been performed; a patched PowerToys build and reconnect test have not yet been performed. The device path itself also needs to be captured before and after reconnecting to confirm persistence through that cycle.

The same `MonitorService.cs` file is present in the inspected `main` commit [`071c25e`](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/commit/071c25e115e8097117e26f6fcfe9901301307f7a) and preview tag `v0.101.2512.0`. This is source verification, not an application reproduction on that newer preview.

Related: [#48516](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/48516) and the merged display-topology fix [#49814](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/49814). The invalid `currentTopologyId` argument remains in the inspected code after that fix.

### Other Software

Windows **Projecting to this PC** / Miracast, using the `Miracast display port driver V3` adapter.

title: [New PowerToy] Three-finger drag for Precision Touchpads
body:
## Summary

Three-finger drag on Precision Touchpads: press with three fingers and move to
emulate holding the left mouse button — drag windows, select text, resize.
This is the single most-requested macOS trackpad behaviour missing on Windows.

**This is not another feature request. It's an offer to implement it, together
with the author of the existing MIT-licensed implementation.** I'm asking the
team for a go/no-go before either of us writes any code.

## Why this is different from the previous requests

Three-finger drag has been asked for since 2021 and every issue is now closed:

| Issue | Outcome |
|---|---|
| #14525 (9 👍) | Closed as duplicate of #4484 — but #4484 is "[Run] Open with a touchpad gesture", a different feature (launching PT Run), so the three-finger-drag discussion effectively ended there |
| #17898, #36929 | Closed, redirected to Feedback Hub |
| #19923, #38368 | Closed at triage |
| #47603 (6 👍) | Open — broader "touchpad gesture customization utility", Needs-Triage |

The reason given in #14525 was:

> I'd look at #4484. Depending on the trackpad, this is enabled via windows
> settings. I'm going to dup this against that.
> As for generic implementation, honestly, i don't think there is an API we as
> PowerToys can hook into as it seems very hardware dependent to enable.

That was a reasonable read in 2021, but it turned out not to hold. There *is* an
API: Raw Input (`WM_INPUT`) against the HID Precision Touchpad usage pages gives
per-contact position and contact-count data without any vendor SDK.
[ClementGre/ThreeFingerDragOnWindows](https://github.com/ClementGre/ThreeFingerDragOnWindows)
has shipped on exactly that since 2022 — MIT, C#/WinUI 3, 1.1k stars — and the
Windows touchpad settings do **not** offer this behaviour, then or now.

## Author is on board, as co-author

I asked Clément Grennerat, TFDOW's author, before bringing this here
([ClementGre/ThreeFingerDragOnWindows#109](https://github.com/ClementGre/ThreeFingerDragOnWindows/issues/109)).
His reply, verbatim:

> As I said in #14525 (comment), I would love to see the Three Finger Drag
> feature to be added to PowerToys.
>
> I think the best way would be for us to do it together and co-author the PR,
> though I will not be available for this until the end of December 2026. This
> should leave us some time to confirm everything with the PowerToys team.

So: original author consenting and co-authoring, MIT throughout (compatible with
this repo), provenance declared up front, attribution in `NOTICE.md` and in the
PR. I've contributed to Keyboard Manager (#49136, #49287, #50265), so I'm
familiar with the module interface, Settings integration, installer and GPO
plumbing in `doc/devdocs/development/new-powertoy.md`.

## Known limitation, stated up front

Raw Input payloads are not uniform across touchpads, and some report inaccurate
contact data. TFDOW cannot support every device and neither could this — that
accounts for a good share of the open issues on that repo. Clément's note:

> TFDOW does not work on all touchpads. Raw Inputs vary between touchpads, and
> some touchpads send inaccurate payloads. Hence the number of issues in this
> repo. I've done the best I could to support tricky touchpads, but there will
> always be edge cases.

I'd rather design for that than discover it in the wild: a detection step at
enable time and an explicit "this touchpad doesn't report usable contact data"
state, instead of a toggle that silently does nothing on some hardware.

## Proposed MVP

- Three-finger (optionally four-finger) press-and-move → left-button drag.
- Settings: on/off, finger count, sensitivity/acceleration, release delay.
- Disabled by default, like every other utility; GPO policy, telemetry, OOBE.
- Unsupported-touchpad detection surfaced in Settings.

## Questions for the team

1. **Are you open to this in principle?** No code will be written before you say
   so, and a "no" now is far more useful than one after implementation.
2. **Shape:** standalone utility, part of Mouse Utilities, or the first piece of
   the broader touchpad utility in #47603?
3. **Elevated windows:** dragging over an elevated window needs the
   input-sending process to be elevated / have UIAccess. How do you want this
   handled given the existing constraints here?
4. **Gesture conflict:** three-finger gestures are bound by Windows to Task View
   / desktop switching. Should the utility offer to remap them, or just document
   the trade-off?
5. **Raw Input ownership:** any known conflicts with modules that already hook
   input?
6. Would you like a spec/dev doc first, before any implementation?

Timeline: Clément is available from the end of December 2026, so there is plenty
of room to settle the design first.

title: DSC App resource does not immediately apply Keyboard Manager enabled state and documentation input structure appears inconsistent
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

v0.101.2362

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Keyboard Manager

### Steps to reproduce

Locate PowerToys.DSC.exe in the PowerToys installation directory.
Check the Keyboard Manager enabled state:
```powershell
$ptdsc = "C:\Program Files\PowerToys\PowerToys.DSC.exe"
$current = & $ptdsc get --resource settings --module App |
    ConvertFrom-Json
$current.settings.enabled.'Keyboard Manager'
```
For example, with Keyboard Manager disabled this returns: False

The relevant part of the returned JSON
```json
{
  "settings": {
    "enabled": {
      "Keyboard Manager": false
    }
  }
}
```

The documented input structure using
```json
{
  "settings": {
    "properties": {
      "Enabled": {
        "KeyboardManager": true
      }
    },
    "name": "App",
    "version": "1.0"
  }
}
```
does not appear to affect Keyboard Manager correctly.

For example, test may report _inDesiredState: true even when Keyboard Manager is currently disabled and KeyboardManager: true was requested.

Instead, get the complete App settings, modify the actual General Settings property, and send the complete object back:
```powershell
$current = & $ptdsc get --resource settings --module App | ConvertFrom-Json
$current.settings.enabled.'Keyboard Manager' = $true
$config = $current | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 30 -Compress
& $ptdsc test --resource settings --module App --input $config
```
This correctly reports:
```
"_inDesiredState": false
```

when Keyboard Manager is currently disabled. Apply settings by following script
```
& $ptdsc set --resource settings --module App --input $config
(& $ptdsc get --resource settings --module App | ConvertFrom-Json).settings.enabled.'Keyboard Manager'
```
The result is now: True

so the persisted setting was successfully changed.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

After `PowerToys.DSC.exe set` changes the Keyboard Manager enabled state, the running PowerToys instance should immediately apply the new state, similarly to changing the toggle from the PowerToys Settings UI.

If Keyboard Manager is changed from disabled to enabled, the Keyboard Manager engine/service should start.

If it is changed from enabled to disabled, it should stop.

The documented DSC example should also match the input structure expected by the current DSC implementation.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

The persisted App General Settings value changes successfully:

"Keyboard Manager": true

but the running PowerToys instance does not immediately enable Keyboard Manager.

PowerToys reports that the Keyboard Manager service is stopped, even though the persisted enabled state is now true.

Restarting PowerToys causes the persisted setting to be read and Keyboard Manager starts correctly.

Therefore the current behavior appears to be:

PowerToys.DSC.exe set
    -> General Settings are persisted
    -> "Keyboard Manager" becomes true
    -> running PowerToys Runner is not notified
    -> Keyboard Manager remains stopped
    -> restarting PowerToys makes the setting take effect

The following sequence works:

1. Get the complete App settings.
2. Change: `$current.settings.enabled.'Keyboard Manager' = $true`
3. Use DSC set to save the complete settings object.
4. Force-stop the PowerToys Runner.
5. Start PowerToys.exe again.

After restarting PowerToys, Keyboard Manager is enabled and works normally.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

OS version: Win 11 Pro 25H2 26200.9445
System Language: Japanese
User Installation
Running as Admin

### Other Software

_No response_

title: [Mouse Jump] - performance, reliability, maintainability improvements
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Incorporate a number of reliability, performance, and maintainability improvements from the upstream FancyMouse codebase. This includes rendering optimizations, architectural cleanup, UI refactoring, bug fixes, and code quality enhancements, with no intended changes to core user-facing functionality.

Changes in the upstream are:

* **WinUI3 Controls** - the previous UI contained the entire preview window visualisation within a single rendered bitmap image. This is replaced with a structured hierarchy of WinUI3 controls (e.g. each background image, bezel and screensho) is a separate WinUI control, allowing for future effects like a highlight or emphasis effect on the screenshot the mouse is currently hovering over.

* **Parallel Capture** - add a "screen capture" pipeline that captures screenshots in parallel rather than one-at-a-time - significantly reduces wait time for screenshots to complete on multi-monitor systems

* **Progressive Screenshots** - background screen capture - if any screenshots take longer than 250ms to load, the preview form shows a blurred version of the *previous* screenshot instead. The blurred image is cross-faded into the actual screenshot for that screen once it's available. This reduces the "flashing" effect of the existing approach that shows a blank coloured "background" rectangle that transitions immediately to the latest screenshot. In most cases the screen is unlikely to have changed significantly (except for e.g. streaming video) so the blurred image presents an early low-fidelity visualisation of the screen while the actual capture is being completed.

* **Cancellation** - added cancellation tokens to cancel screen capture and rendering if the activation hotkey is pressed repeatedly. Previously an activation would run to completion and show the form briefly before closing and servicing the next activation - it now cancels the previous activation and starts the next one mmediately.

* **Opt-In Telemetry** - added a **local file-based logging** telemetry function that is **off** by default (can be enabled manually in the config file). This drops out structured events with performance timings onto the local file system and can be used as an additional information source to diagnose issues that can't be easily diagnosed from the log file alone. **Does not automatically ship telemetry logs anywhere when enabled - only persists to disk**

* **PInvoke Rewrite** - hand-written ```DllImport``` and ```LibraryImport``` methods replaced with CsWin32 for better standardisation
 
* **Maintenance** - lots code quality improvements - general refactoring, disposing GDI resources properly, removing dead code, adding / improving / rewording xmldocs and comments, tweaks, nips and tucks

### Scenario when this would be used?

Improves performance for all users.

### Supporting information

_No response_

title: PowerToys Run: Additional 0.86.0.0 log for known 0x80263001 desktop composition crash
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.86.0.0

### Installation method

PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

PowerToys Run

### Steps to reproduce

Unable to reproduce consistently.

The issue occurred while PowerToys Run was running. At approximately 12:49:40 on September 8, 2026, PowerToys Run encountered a fatal COM exception indicating that Windows desktop composition was disabled.

The PowerToys Run log also shows several UWP/package indexing errors before the crash, including an invalid/missing installation path for WhatsApp Desktop and a missing AppxManifest.xml.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

PowerToys Run should continue functioning normally when Windows desktop composition/DWM is temporarily unavailable or changes state.

It should handle the condition gracefully rather than terminating with an unhandled exception.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

PowerToys Run encountered the following fatal exception:

System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (0x80263001):
{Desktop composition is disabled}
The operation could not be completed because desktop composition is disabled. (0x80263001)

The relevant stack trace is:

at Standard.NativeMethods.DwmExtendFrameIntoClientArea(IntPtr hwnd, MARGINS& pMarInset)
at System.Windows.Shell.WindowChromeWorker._ExtendGlassFrame()
at System.Windows.Shell.WindowChromeWorker._UpdateFrameState(Boolean force)

    IntPtr hwnd,

    Delegate callback,
    Object args,
    Int32 numArgs)

    Object source,
    Delegate callback,
    Object args,
    Int32 numArgs,
    Delegate callback)

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

### Additional Information

Environment reported by the log:

Version: 0.86.0.0
OS Version: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
IntPtr Length: 8
x64: True
CLR Version: 8.0.10
Wox version: 0.86.0.0

Fatal exception timestamp:

09/08/2026 12:49:40

PowerToys Run was launched with:

C:\Users\Aryan\AppData\Local\PowerToys\PowerToys.PowerLauncher.dll -powerToysPid 15760 --started-from-runner

The log shows additional package/indexing errors before the crash.

For WhatsApp Desktop (5319275A.WhatsAppDesktop), PowerToys Run repeatedly reported:

System.ArgumentException
The parameter is incorrect.

The specified path is too short. It must have at least 1 character.

It later reported that the package manifest could not be found:

Could not find file
'C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\5319275A.WhatsAppDesktop_2.2634.101.0_neutral_~_cv1g1gvanyjgm\AppxManifest.xml'.

There were also errors involving Microsoft Copilot package resources and retrieving the description for Windows Media Player.

Despite these indexing errors, PowerToys Run continued initialization and reported:

Indexed 1128 win32 applications

The Program plugin initialization took approximately:

Win32Program index cost: 28584ms
Total initialize cost for <Program>: 29069ms
App.OnStartup - Startup cost: 33438ms

The fatal 0x80263001 exception occurred later at 12:49:40.

I am including these preceding indexing errors because it is unclear whether they are related to the desktop-composition failure.

### Other Software

No known third-party software confirmed to be responsible.

Related issues

This error appears to have been reported previously in PowerToys, including:

#42526 — same 0x80263001 error and the same DwmExtendFrameIntoClientArea / WindowChromeWorker stack pattern.
#42616 — PowerToys Run crash with the same exception.
#45563 — PowerToys crash when desktop composition is disabled.
#46224 — PowerToys Run crash after system instability with UWP indexing errors.
#48357 — newer report on Windows 11 Build 26200, also involving 0x80263001.

These reports have generally been classified as duplicates. This report is being submitted to provide an additional occurrence from PowerToys 0.86.0.0, along with the complete log and the preceding UWP/package-indexing errors.

Could the attached log be reviewed to determine whether these additional indexing errors or the long PowerToys Run initialization are relevant to the 0x80263001 desktop-composition failure?

title: [Feature]: App-level Alt+Tab — the other half of Window Hopper (working MIT reference implementation)
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Window Hopper (0.101) solved the **inner** half of window switching: ``Alt+` `` now cycles through the windows of the app you are already in. The **outer** half is still missing — `Alt+Tab` in Windows remains window-level, so with N windows of one app open you still have to walk through all of them to reach a *different* app.

Proposal: an **app-level `Alt+Tab`** — one entry per application, MRU/Z-order ordered, using the same overlay UI.

The part I would most like the team to consider is the **contract between the two layers**, not the UI:

| Shortcut | Layer | Set |
|---|---|---|
| `Alt+Tab` | application | one entry per app (this proposal) |
| ``Alt+` `` | window | windows of the focused app (Window Hopper, shipped) |

Both layers should key off **the same application identity**: the process image path, with the UWP resolution that `RealProcessImagePath()` already implements in `src/modules/AltWindowCycle/AltWindowCycle.cpp` — when the top-level window belongs to `ApplicationFrameHost.exe`, resolve to the hosted `Windows.UI.Core.CoreWindow`'s real process, otherwise every packaged app collapses into one group.

Because both layers key on the same identity, an app is never listed in both places, and the two shortcuts stay strictly complementary instead of drifting apart. That shared key is, in my experience, the only thing that actually needs to be agreed on for the two features to coexist.

**Reference implementation:** https://github.com/informalgit/AppHopper (MIT, single-file C#, no dependencies, builds with the .NET Framework compiler already in Windows). It deliberately does *not* implement ``Alt+` `` and defers to Window Hopper for it; it is the "outer half" only.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Six File Explorer windows, a browser and a terminal are open. To get from Explorer to the browser, `Alt+Tab` costs as many presses as there are Explorer windows in front of it, and the target moves every time. With an app-level `Alt+Tab` it is one press, and ``Alt+` `` (Window Hopper) handles "which Explorer window" afterwards.

This is the split macOS has shipped for years (`Cmd+Tab` = apps, ``Cmd+` `` = windows), and it is what people have been asking for here since #20115, #358 and #493. Now that Window Hopper has landed, the missing piece is precisely the other half of that split.

### Supporting information

**Why this is not a duplicate of #20115:** that issue (and #358, #493) are *requests*. This one ships a working, MIT-licensed implementation that already runs alongside Window Hopper, and it proposes the specific shared-identity contract that lets the two features coexist.

**Things that cost real time to discover** while building the reference implementation (Windows 10 22H2, single machine — worth re-validating on your side):

1. `SetForegroundWindow` can return `TRUE` while silently failing to move focus for UWP `ApplicationFrameWindow`s. The activation path has to re-read the actual foreground window and verify, with `SwitchToThisWindow` as the escalation step.
2. `DwmRegisterThumbnail` works fine on **minimized** windows — DWM keeps the last presented frame. Skipping them via `IsIconic` leaves most tiles empty on a typical desktop.
3. `AttachThreadInput` is a synchronous cross-thread call and can block for hundreds of milliseconds (Explorer's window thread especially). Keep it off the hot path, or hide the overlay before taking it.
4. Z-order rank must increment for *every* enumerated top-level window, including the ones that get filtered out, or equal ranks make the ordering unstable and the list reshuffles.
5. Windows carrying `WS_EX_APPWINDOW` need their own entry — grouping purely by exe otherwise absorbs owned dialogs into their owner's entry, making them unreachable by switcher.

**Known limits of the approach:** a user-mode switcher cannot cover the secure desktop, UAC prompts, or full-screen exclusive applications, and it does not replace the system task switcher — those cases have to fall through to Windows.

Happy to open a PR, contribute the grouping/eligibility logic, or help write a spec if the team is interested in any form of this.

title: [Power Display] Samsung Odyssey G7 can enter persistent abnormal state after DDC/CI power-state interaction
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

0.101.2492.0

### Installation method

GitHub

### Area(s) with issue?

Power Display

### Steps to reproduce

**Hardware**

- Samsung Odyssey G7 27-inch
- Model: C27G75TQSN / LC27G75TQSNXZA
- Firmware: M-TG700CCAA-1016.1
- EDID / Power Display name: LC27G7xT (SAM105C)
- Windows monitor path: `\\?\DISPLAY#SAM105C#5&265f4cc1&0&UID37121`
- Normal connection: DisplayPort, 2560x1440 @ 240 Hz

**Original occurrence — I do not recommend intentionally reproducing this on a primary monitor**

1. The monitor was operating normally immediately beforehand, including its physical JOG/OSD controls and Infinity lighting.
2. Power Display's monitor power controls were used, including the advertised `Off (Hard)` state.
3. Immediately afterward, the monitor entered a persistent abnormal state:
   - black/inert LCD
   - no OSD
   - no monitor-generated no-signal screen
   - physical JOG control no longer responded normally
   - only a brief teal/rear-light flash was seen on power reconnection
4. Normal unplug/replug, source reconnects, and extended unpowered waits did not recover it.
5. Power Display and other Windows DDC tools no longer exposed a usable live monitor target.

**Independent recovery evidence**

The exact monitor was then connected directly to a CachyOS Linux laptop over HDMI.

Linux still identified the exact EDID and DDC bus.

The monitor advertises DDC/CI VCP 0xD6 Power Mode values:

- `0x01` On
- `0x04` Off (DPM)
- `0x05` Off (Hard)

A single bounded exact-target DDC/CI write was issued:

`VCP 0xD6 = 0x01 (On)`

No automatic retry was used.

The monitor immediately turned on.

Afterward:

- monitor-generated no-signal graphics returned
- HDMI operation returned
- DisplayPort operation returned
- DDC/CI communication materially improved
- the monitor later returned to normal JOG/select behavior
- the monitor's own OSD `Reset All` was completed successfully
- normal 2560x1440 @ 240 Hz operation returned
- firmware remained M-TG700CCAA-1016.1

**Second occurrence after full recovery / factory reset**

1. The monitor had been fully recovered and was operating normally again.
2. While attempting to disable Power Display, Power Display was interacted with/opened again.
3. Immediately around that interaction:
   - the monitor's Infinity/teal lighting changed/went off
   - inward JOG/select stopped responding normally
   - directional JOG movement continued to work
   - the Windows picture remained stable
4. Removing all DP/HDMI/USB data cables did not immediately clear the monitor-side state.
5. After exiting PowerToys and performing a complete isolated AC/DC monitor power removal, normal inward JOG/select behavior returned.

I am **not** claiming that the available logs prove which exact DDC transaction caused the second occurrence. The temporal association is strong, but the precise mechanism remains unresolved.

### Expected Behavior

Power Display should not leave a DDC/CI-capable monitor in a persistent abnormal state requiring an external DDC wake or complete monitor controller depower to recover.

For monitors that advertise `Off (Hard)`, possible safeguards could include:

- allowing `Off (Hard)` to be hidden or disabled
- a warning before using hard-off states
- compatibility handling for monitors known not to recover reliably

This appears related to #50208, which requests the ability to disable some Power Display power-state options, including `Off (Hard)`.

### Actual Behavior

On this Samsung Odyssey G7, the original Power Display hard-off interaction was immediately followed by a severe persistent monitor failure state.

A later Power Display interaction after complete recovery/factory reset was followed by a second abnormal monitor-control episode affecting Infinity lighting and inward JOG/select behavior while video output remained alive.

This appears to be a Power Display / Samsung G7 DDC/CI compatibility or safety problem.

The available evidence does **not** establish whether the underlying defect is specifically:

- PowerToys DDC/CI handling
- Windows monitor/DDC API behavior
- Samsung monitor firmware behavior
- or an interaction between those components

### Diagnostic information

Power Display reports the monitor capability string including:

`D6(01 04 05)`

Power Display configuration captured in the diagnostic report includes:

- `restore_settings_on_startup: false`
- `max_compatibility_mode: false`
- no Power Display profiles
- no custom VCP mappings

A relevant Power Display log entry for the exact monitor is:

`Failed to read VCP 0xD6, error code: -1071241847`

The signed decimal value corresponds to:

`0xC0262589`

`ERROR_GRAPHICS_DDCCI_INVALID_MESSAGE_COMMAND`

Current Power Display source is also relevant here: the DDC/CI discovery path initializes power-state support by reading VCP `0xD6` when the monitor advertises power-state capability. This means normal monitor discovery can exercise a D6 read even when restore-on-startup is disabled.

That source-code observation does **not** prove that the D6 read caused the second occurrence; it only identifies a concrete Power Display code path corresponding to the logged D6 read failure.

### Attachments

Attached diagnostic artifacts:

[PowerToysReport_2026-09-07-16-47-26.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31930589/PowerToysReport_2026-09-07-16-47-26.zip)

SHA-256:

`3FAC763FC622169A81348CC3C8EB070B98E8E92137FACADA7E43FA1F2F549804`

This official PowerToys report was generated after Power Display had been disabled and retains the historical incident-period Power Display logs.

Additional curated evidence:

[G7-PowerDisplay-curated-public-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31930588/G7-PowerDisplay-curated-public-evidence.zip)

This contains the relevant Power Display JSON/log material and recovery logs with unnecessary machine-identifying material removed.

I can also provide the Linux ddcutil recovery log, before/after photos, and a more detailed timeline if maintainers need them.

### Other Software

No third-party Windows monitor-management application was required to trigger the failure.

Linux DDC tooling was used only after the original failure in order to recover the monitor.

title: Switch Apps on Fancy Zones Easily
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

It would be useful to be able to swap the positions of applications between zones on the FancyZones layout screen using a quick sequence of clicks, similar to how Samsung or Xiaomi handle their split-screen views.

### Scenario when this would be used?

In many messaging applications, the text input bar is typically located at the bottom of the screen, which can be quite uncomfortable during long work sessions. Thanks to this feature, you can modify the app's layout and move the messaging area to the top, making it more comfortable to use with just a couple of clicks at the junction between the two areas.

title: [PowerToys Run][Unit Converter] Degree unit parsing fails under Turkish culture
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

PowerToys main branch, commit 5c33f0023

### Installation method

GitHub, Dev build in Visual Studio

### Area(s) with issue?

General, PowerToys Run

### Steps to reproduce



1. Set the Windows culture/region to Turkish (`tr-TR`).
2. Open PowerToys Run.
3. Enter a Unit Converter query using uppercase temperature names, for example:
   `%% 5 CELSIUS in FAHRENHEIT`
4. Observe that the conversion does not produce the expected result.


### ✔️ Expected Behavior




`CELSIUS` and `FAHRENHEIT` should be recognized case-insensitively and converted to the internal UnitsNet names:

- `DegreeCelsius`
- `DegreeFahrenheit`


### ❌ Actual Behavior



`DegreePrefixer()` lowercases the tokens using `CultureInfo.CurrentCulture`.

Under `tr-TR`, uppercase `I` is converted to the dotless `ı`, so:

- `CELSIUS` becomes `celsıus`
- `FAHRENHEIT` becomes `fahrenheıt`

Neither value matches the fixed English tokens `celsius` and `fahrenheit`, so the parser fails to recognize the units.

The existing mixed-case test covers this behavior under the default culture, but there is no culture-scoped regression test for `tr-TR`.


### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information


The affected code is:

- `src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Community.PowerToys.Run.Plugin.UnitConverter/InputInterpreter.cs`
- `src/modules/launcher/Plugins/Community.PowerToys.Run.Plugin.UnitConverter.UnitTest/InputInterpreterTests.cs`

The proposed fix is to use `ToLowerInvariant()` for these internal unit tokens.

### Other Software

_No response_

title: PTB Export/Import from CLI
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Command line options to import and export `.ptb` setting backups.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Backing up and restoring PowerToys settings currently requires either using the buttons in the GUI or messing with the WinGet DSC yaml thing. The former, naturally, is not accessible from the CLI, and the latter can be overkill if PowerToys is the only thing being set up this way. While the `.ptb` backup is technically just a zip file and could be manually extracted into the settings folder, this is undocumented and overall just not ideal. Much better than `Expand-Archive -Path "PowerToysBackup.ptb" -DestinationPath "$env:LocalAppData\Microsoft\PowerToys" -Force` would be some variation of `powertoys.exe --import PowerToysBackup.ptb`.

### Supporting information

Related issue: #4649

title: Tiling windows
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I would like to request a dynamic tiling window management feature for Microsoft PowerToys that provides a workflow similar to modern Linux tiling environments, including those found in **Omarchy**.

While **FancyZones** is an excellent manual window layout tool, it requires users to define zones ahead of time. A dynamic tiling manager would automatically arrange windows, continuously reflow layouts, and enable efficient keyboard-driven window management without manual zone configuration.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This feature would be most valuable for users who work with multiple windows throughout the day and prefer a keyboard-driven workflow. Key audiences include:

Developers and software engineers

- IT professionals and system administrators
- Security analysts
- Data engineers and analysts
- Technical support teams
- Multi-monitor power users
- Users transitioning from Linux environments such as Omarchy, Hyprland, i3, and Sway

By automatically organizing windows and reducing manual resizing and positioning, a dynamic tiling manager can improve productivity, maintain workspace consistency, and help users stay focused on their work rather than window management.

### Supporting information

[Omarchy (Hyprland-based)](https://omarchy.org/manual/)

User Manual: Omarchy Manual
Explains the user experience, keyboard-first workflow, workspaces, and automatic tiling behaviors.
Particularly useful: Windows place themselves and workspace management concepts.

Hyprland
Dynamic tiling compositor used by Omarchy.
Excellent reference for:
- Window tree management
- Dynamic layouts
- Floating windows
- Multi-monitor support
- Workspace handling

Komorebi (Windows)
- Open-source tiling window manager built specifically for Windows.
- Demonstrates how dynamic tiling can be implemented using the Win32 APIs without replacing the Windows shell.
- Likely the closest architectural reference for a PowerToys implementation.

GlazeWM (Windows)
- Another Windows-native tiling manager with BSP layouts, workspaces, and keyboard-driven controls.
- Good reference for user experience and configuration design.

FancyWM
- Demonstrates a more Windows-native approach while integrating with virtual desktops and existing shell components.

title: Fancy Zones - Shareable Profiles
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I find Fancy Zones useful and productivity enhancing.  I also find the setup to get the exactly as I wish to be cumbersome (could use help from copilot - separate issue).  If I could share Fancy Zone profiles with colleges and friends, I think the overall productivity would be greatly enhanced as some people will be frustrated out of trying.

Further if copilot could integrate into Power Toys , then I could just ask something like "Split my screen in 3 equal vertical columns with zero pixel bezel and then create one horizontal split 1/3 of the way down from the top" or any number of similar request.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would be incredibly helpful for setting up your screen environment to rotate between tasks as well as training and sharing between colleagues and new entrants to the task.

### Supporting information

I've had multiple colleges interested in using Fancy Zones, but low patience for setting up and configuring them for some of our standardized tasks.

title: Advanced Paste: Foundry Local provider shows no models – empty Service URL with Foundry Local 0.10.x
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

Release v0.101.2362.0

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Advanced Paste

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Foundry Local (current release): `winget install Microsoft.FoundryLocal `→ installs `0.10.3.0`
2. Verify install: `Get-AppxPackage *FoundryLocal*` → confirms single clean install, `Microsoft.FoundryLocal_0.10.3.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`
3. Start server and load a model with the new CLI:
```
   foundry server start
   foundry run phi-4-mini
```
→ Model loads successfully, interactive chat works (confirmed via `Chatting model (phi-4-mini)` prompt and correct responses)
4. Open PowerToys Settings → Advanced Paste → Foundry Local provider configuration
5. Dialog shows "Keine Modelle heruntergeladen" / "No models downloaded" and prompts to run Foundry Local, despite the model being loaded and the server running
6. PowerToys log (`AdvancedPaste/Settings` log, `[FoundryClient]/[FoundryLocal]` entries) shows:
```
   [FoundryLocal] Checking availability
   [FoundryLocal] Initializing provider
   [FoundryLocal] Service URL: 
   [FoundryClient] Listing catalog models
   [FoundryClient] Error listing catalog models: An invalid request URI was provided. Either the request URI must be an absolute URI or BaseAddress must be set.
   [FoundryLocal] Found 0 catalog models
   [FoundryLocal] Available: True
   [FoundryClient] Listing cached models
   [FoundryClient] Error listing cached models: An invalid request URI was provided. Either the request URI must be an absolute URI or BaseAddress must be set.
```


### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Advanced Paste's Foundry Local provider configuration should detect the running server and loaded model (`phi-4-mini`), matching the behavior of the `foundry` CLI and a direct call to the local OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`Service URL:` resolves to an empty string, so every subsequent call (`ListCatalogModels`, `ListCachedModels`) fails with "An invalid request URI was provided. Either the request URI must be an absolute URI or BaseAddress must be set." `IsAvailable` still reports `True`, but the provider shows zero models, so no Foundry Local model can be selected or used in `Advanced Paste`.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

[Log_2026-09-04.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31814121/Log_2026-09-04.log)

### Additional Information

Foundry Local `0.10.x` replaced the previous service-based architecture with a new SDK-based CLI/daemon (per the [Foundry Local CLI 0.10.0 release notes](https://github.com/microsoft/Foundry-Local/releases/tag/cli-preview-0.10.0): "the first release of the new CLI built on the Foundry Local SDKs, replacing the earlier service-based CLI"). It looks like the `Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local` SDK version PowerToys currently references cannot resolve the service endpoint/port from this new architecture, leaving `FoundryLocalModelProvider._serviceUrl` empty (`src/common/LanguageModelProvider/FoundryLocalModelProvider.cs`).

This may be a distinct/newer issue from #45340 (fixed by #45362), which addressed a 400 Bad Request with the older `0.8.119` service-based build on a fixed port — that fix does not seem to cover the `0.10.x` rearchitecture.

### Other Software

- Foundry Local: `0.10.3.0` (package `Microsoft.FoundryLocal_0.10.3.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`)
- Model tested: `phi-4-mini` (`phi-4-mini-instruct-openvino-npu:4`), Intel NPU via OpenVINO
- OS: Windows 11 24H2

title: CmdPal: dock band buttons stop working after the host releases the extension — clicks fall back to opening the palette, extension is never re-activated
body:
### Environment

- Command Palette standalone dev build `0.12.12365.0` (`Microsoft.CommandPalette_8wekyb3d8bbwe`)
- Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, build 10.0.26200
- Extension: an out-of-proc COM extension providing **dock bands** via `GetDockBands()` ("Virtual Desktops 2.0", built on the CmdPal extension template, `Shmuelie.WinRTServer` as the COM host)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install an extension that provides dock band items (each item's command executes on click).
2. Use the dock band — clicks work (desktop switching, in this case).
3. Leave the system alone for a while. At some point the host **releases the idle extension**: the extension receives `IExtension.Dispose()`, and its out-of-proc process exits cleanly (no crash entries in the Application event log — this is the normal OOP COM lifecycle).
4. Click a dock band button.

### Expected behavior

The host re-activates the extension's COM class and executes the command — or, at minimum, refreshes/removes the stale band so the user isn't clicking dead buttons.

### Actual behavior

The click **opens the main palette window** instead of running the command. The stale band keeps being rendered indefinitely, and nothing re-activates the released extension:

- dock band clicks keep opening the palette (observed repeatedly over hours);
- opening the palette and searching still shows the extension's top-level commands (served from the host's cache) even though the backing extension process is gone — `Process.GetProcessesByName` on the extension executable shows no process;
- the extension process is **not** re-spawned by any of these interactions; only restarting the CmdPal host brings the band back to life (host start → extension activated → band works again).

### Notes

Idle release itself is fine — that's the normal OOP COM server lifecycle, and our server exits when the last reference is dropped. The gap is that **dock bands have no re-activation path** once the host has released the extension: the band UI outlives the COM object it is bound to. Either dock band clicks should trigger re-activation of the extension, or the host should drop stale bands when it releases one.

Happy to provide more diagnostics (DebugView traces from the extension, a repro build, etc.).

title: [Command Not Found] Eager Import-Module in $PROFILE adds ~200-400ms to shell startup latency
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.101.2362.0 - Preview (ARM64)

### Installation method

WinGet

### Area(s) with issue?

Command not found

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable **Command Not Found** in PowerToys Settings.
2. PowerToys appends the following block to PowerShell `$PROFILE`:
   ```powershell
   #f45873b3-b655-43a6-b217-97c00aa0db58 PowerToys CommandNotFound module
   Import-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.CommandNotFound
   #f45873b3-b655-43a6-b217-97c00aa0db58
   ```
3. Open a new PowerShell 7 session or benchmark module import time:
   ```powershell
   Measure-Command { Import-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.CommandNotFound }
   ```

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

Enabling Command Not Found should have near-zero overhead on interactive shell startup when valid commands are run. Heavy module dependencies should be deferred until an unrecognized command is actually executed.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

`Import-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.CommandNotFound` runs synchronously at shell startup. Because `Microsoft.WinGet.CommandNotFound.psd1` declares `RequiredModules = @(@{ModuleName = 'Microsoft.WinGet.Client'; ...})`, it synchronously loads `Microsoft.WinGet.Client`, manifests, and binary assemblies on **every single shell launch**.

On modern systems (including ARM64 Copilot+ PCs and x64), this adds **~200–400 ms** to `Loading personal and system profiles took ...` on every terminal tab open, even though 99.9% of shell commands are valid.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Suggested Fix / Optimization:**
Instead of injecting eager `Import-Module`, configure a lazy handler in `$PROFILE` using `$ExecutionContext.InvokeCommand.CommandNotFoundAction`:

```powershell
#f45873b3-b655-43a6-b217-97c00aa0db58 PowerToys CommandNotFound module
$ExecutionContext.InvokeCommand.CommandNotFoundAction = {
    param($cmdName, $eventArgs)
    $ExecutionContext.InvokeCommand.CommandNotFoundAction = $null
    Import-Module -Name Microsoft.WinGet.CommandNotFound -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
#f45873b3-b655-43a6-b217-97c00aa0db58
```

This reduces startup latency from ~250ms to **0 ms**, deferring the heavy module and `Microsoft.WinGet.Client` import until the user actually types an unknown command.

- OS: Windows 11 (Build 26100 / 28000 ARM64)
- PowerShell: 7.4+ / 7.6.5
- PowerToys: 0.101.x

### Other Software

_No response_

title: EdgeSwipe, a Win8 inspired gesture-based app switcher
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

EdgeSwipe would allow users to swipe inward from the left edge of the screen to quickly return to the most recently used application. Continuing the gesture or swiping again could allow users to browse through other recently used applications before releasing to activate the selected window.

The utility should support touchscreens and compatible precision touchpads, with configurable options for enabling or disabling the gesture, selecting which applications are included, supporting multiple monitors and virtual desktops, and avoiding conflicts with full-screen applications or existing Windows gestures. A configurable keyboard shortcut could provide an alternative for systems without reliable edge-swipe support.

This would provide a fast, customizable alternative to Alt+Tab, Task View, and taskbar-based application switching while restoring a convenient interaction pattern that many Windows 8 users found effective.

This was one of the highlights of the Win 8.x experiment and it's a shame many people didn't get to use this fantastic bit of UX. 

### Scenario when this would be used?

A user is working between two or more applications—for example, Microsoft Teams, a web browser, and a document editor—and wants to quickly return to the application they were using previously.

Instead of pressing Alt+Tab, opening Task View, or moving the pointer to the taskbar, the user swipes inward from the left edge of the screen. Releasing the gesture immediately activates the most recently used application. If the user wants to switch to another recent application, they can continue swiping or repeat the gesture until the desired application is selected.

This would be particularly useful for:
- Touchscreen and 2-in-1 device users.
- Users working with a mouse who want a quick alternative to keyboard shortcuts.
- Tablet-style workflows where reaching the taskbar is inconvenient.
- Users frequently switching between a primary application and a reference application.
- Users who liked the Windows 8 left-edge app-switching workflow and want a modern, configurable equivalent.

### Supporting information

This proposal is inspired by the left-edge app-switching gesture that was available in Windows 8 and Windows 8.1. In that experience, swiping inward from the left edge allowed users to return to the previous application or browse recently used applications.

The proposed PowerToy would not need to modify the Windows shell. It could operate as an optional background utility with user-configurable gesture detection and behavior.

Potential implementation considerations include:
- Detecting touch and precision-touchpad edge gestures reliably.
- Supporting multiple monitors and different display scaling settings.
- Avoiding conflicts with existing Windows, OEM, and application-specific edge gestures.
- Handling full-screen applications, games, and virtual desktops.
- Providing a keyboard shortcut as an alternative when edge detection is unavailable.
- Respecting accessibility settings and allowing the feature to be disabled completely.
- Limiting the initial version to switching to the most recently used application before adding a visual recent-app selector.

Related Windows terminology includes “switch between apps,” “recent apps,” and “swipe in from the left edge.” The proposed name is **EdgeSwipe**, with the descriptive subtitle **“A gesture-based recent-app switcher for Windows.”**

title: FancyZones: PriorityGrid falls back to Grid at 11 zones, so the editor preview and the snapped layout disagree
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

Current `main` (verified against `LayoutConfigurator.cpp` at HEAD)

### Installation method

GitHub

### Running as admin

No

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the FancyZones editor and create a template layout using **Priority Grid** with **11 zones**.
2. Note the layout the editor previews.
3. Apply it, then drag a window and snap it.

The editor previews the hand-designed 11-zone priority layout. The engine snaps windows to a plain grid instead.

At 10 zones or fewer the two agree, so this only shows up at exactly 11.

### Expected Behavior

The window snapping should use the same PriorityGrid layout the editor previewed, for every zone count the editor offers it for.

### Actual Behavior

The engine falls back to `Grid` at 11 zones, so the editor preview and the snapping behavior disagree.

### Cause

`src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/LayoutConfigurator.cpp`:

```cpp
// line 13
// PriorityGrid layout is unique for zoneCount <= 11. For zoneCount > 11 PriorityGrid is same as Grid
FancyZonesDataTypes::GridLayoutInfo predefinedPriorityGridLayouts[11] = { ... };

// line 391
constexpr int predefinedLayoutsCount = sizeof(predefinedPriorityGridLayouts) / sizeof(FancyZonesDataTypes::GridLayoutInfo);
// line 392
if (zoneCount < predefinedLayoutsCount)
    return CalculateGridZones(workArea, predefinedPriorityGridLayouts[zoneCount - 1], spacing);
return Grid(workArea, zoneCount, spacing);
```

`predefinedLayoutsCount` is 11, so `zoneCount < 11` accepts 1 through 10 and indexes 0 through 9. `predefinedPriorityGridLayouts[10]`, the 11th hand-designed layout, is never reached.

Three things say `<=` was intended:

- The comment on line 13 says the layout is unique for `zoneCount <= 11`.
- The array is sized 11, so index 10 exists and is otherwise dead.
- The C# editor uses the opposite comparison. `src/modules/fancyzones/editor/FancyZonesEditor/Models/GridLayoutModel.cs:447`:
  ```csharp
  if (TemplateZoneCount <= _priorityData.Length)
  {
      Reload(_priorityData[TemplateZoneCount - 1]);
  ```

So the editor and the engine disagree on the boundary, which is what makes it user visible rather than just dead code.

`zoneCount - 1` is 10 at `zoneCount == 11`, which is in bounds for an 11-element array, so accepting 11 does not introduce an out-of-range read.

### Other Software

I would like to fix this if you agree with the diagnosis. It looks like a one-character change on line 392 plus a unit test in `FancyZones.UnitTests` covering the 11-zone boundary, but I did not want to open a PR without checking first, per the contributing guidance.

title: FancyZones Issue with msedge.exe Apps
body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version and release channel

0.100.2

### Installation method

WinGet, PowerToys auto-update

### Area(s) with issue?

FancyZones

### Steps to reproduce

As I understand it, FancyZones tracks the "last known zone" by the application's underlying process executable rather than the specific window title. Because all Edge Progressive Web Apps (PWAs) run through msedge.exe (or msedge_proxy.exe), FancyZones sees every single one of those apps as the exact same program. Whenever you launch one, the window manager routes it to the zone occupied by whichever msedge.exe window was moved last.

I have a dozen or so PWAs installed and when I launch one, it will frequently launch to the location of the previous PWA opened.  I'm not sure if it's possible, but storing the specific PWA window location based on either a browser application ID (--app-id) or the AUMID (MSEdge.pwa_<hash> would ensure a unique ID for each PWA and force them to launch in the correct location.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

When I open a PWA app, FancyZones should launch the app in the last known location of that specific App.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

When I open a PWA app, FancyZones is launching the app in the last known location of another PWA app.

### Upload Bug Report ZIP-file

_No response_

### Additional Information

Win 11 Pro 25H2
AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX
96GB RAM, 16GB dedicated to GPU
3 Displays, each is a Dell S2721DS

### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Fix recent history provider-aware and use it for recommendations that will replace Recent commands.

CmdPal history stores only CommandId, but command IDs are not unique across extensions. This can attribute usage to, display, or execute the wrong provider’s command.

- Store and resolve history using (ProviderId, CommandId). 
- Migrate legacy ID-only entries only when the match is unambiguous.
- Use the corrected history for a simple local frecency recommender based on usage count and recency.

title: [LightSwitch] Proposal: Follow Ambient Light mode driven by the ambient light sensor
body: ### Description of the new feature / enhancement ## Summary We have designed and implemented a new **`FollowAmbientLight`** schedule mode for the Light Switch module that switches between the light and dark themes based on **real-time ambient light sensor (ALS) illuminance (lux)**, rather than on time-of-day or Windows Night Light state. The implementation also includes a **perceptually-grounded adaptation model** (log-domain smoothing + dual dark/bright adaptation) so switching feels natural instead of flickery. This issue is filed to **share our detailed design and implementation with the PowerToys team for awareness and discussion**. It is not a request to merge specific code — we're happy to align on the approach, naming, and scope, and to follow it up with a PR if the team considers the feature a good fit for PowerToys. ## What we implemented (detailed) Two commits' worth of work, summarized by area. ### A. Core mode and settings (foundation) - New `ScheduleMode::FollowAmbientLight` enum value + `ToString`/`FromString` round-tripping in both `LightSwitchSettings.h` and the module interface (`dllmain.cpp`). - New `ambientLightThreshold` setting: - Default `50`, clamped to `0–100000` (`DefaultAmbientLightThreshold`, `Min/MaxAmbientLightThreshold`). - Added across the service config, the module interface spinners, the IPC/load path, and the C# `LightSwitchProperties`/`LightSwitchViewModel`. - `SettingId::AmbientLightThreshold` added for IPC. - Settings UI: a "Follow Ambient Light" entry in the mode selector, an info card explaining the sensor requirement, and a threshold `NumberBox` with an **Apply** button (the threshold is only persisted on Apply, so users can experiment). ### B. Sensor observation - `AmbientLightObserver` (`AmbientLightObserver.h/.cpp`): a WinRT `LightSensor` wrapper that: - Initializes COM defensively (the host process may already have initialized a different apartment). - Forwards each reading's `IlluminanceInLux` through a `std::function` callback. - Rate-limits via `ReportInterval` (≈2000 ms, clamped to the sensor's `MinimumReportInterval`). - Never lets exceptions escape the `ReadingChanged` handler. - Revokes the subscription in `Stop()`/destructor. - Stays inert and reports `IsSensorAvailable() == false` when no sensor is present. ### C. Classification and adaptation model In `LightSwitchStateManager`: - `OnAmbientLightChange(double lux)` — entry from the observer callback. - `OnAmbientAdaptationTick()` — entry from the service worker loop, so time-driven adaptation keeps progressing while the sensor is silent. - `ReclassifyAmbientLight(double lux)`: - Smooths the raw reading via `UpdateAmbientSmoothing` (log-domain EMA, τ = 10 s). - Advances the dual adaptation model via `UpdateAmbientAdaptation(double logLux)`. - Computes the effective light/dark boundaries in the log domain: - `effectiveLightBoundary = logThreshold + darkAdaptation * 0.30` decades - `effectiveDarkBoundary = logThreshold - lightAdaptation * 0.15` decades - Reclassifies only when the smoothed reading exits the `±0.12` decade hysteresis band. - On a threshold crossing, clears a pending manual override (a crossing is a boundary event that should win over a stale override). - Logs both raw lux and the log-domain values for diagnostics. - Both adaptation models are **reset to zero** when entering or leaving `FollowAmbientLight` (and on day-boundary evaluation), so stale adaptation does not bleed across mode switches. ### D. Service worker integration In `LightSwitchService.cpp`: - Starts/stops `g_ambientLightWatcher` to match whether `FollowAmbientLight` is active (`UpdateAmbientLightWatcher`). - In ambient mode with a known reading, shortens the worker wait to \~5 s (`AmbientAdaptationTickIntervalMs`) so adaptation accrues without relying on the once-per-minute tick — while guarding the minute tick against duplicate runs when the wait is shortened. - Computes `shouldBeLight` in `FollowAmbientLight` from the hysteresis-filtered `isAmbientLightActive` classification. - Cleans up the watcher on worker exit. ### E. Settings UI: live reading display In `LightSwitchPage.xaml` / `LightSwitchPage.xaml.cs`: - A `TextBlock` under the threshold card shows **"Current ambient light: {0:0} lux"**, refreshed from the page's own `LightSensor` subscription (report interval ≈2000 ms). - Marshals sensor events (background thread) to the UI thread via `DispatcherQueue`. - Starts/stops on mode selection and on page `Loaded`/`Unloaded`; idempotent and inert when no sensor is present (the info card already explains the requirement). - Lets users calibrate the threshold against the *actual* current room brightness, which is essential because a fixed default lux value is meaningless without knowing the sensor's reading in the user's environment. ### F. Localization and resources - Added `en-us` resources: the "Follow Ambient Light" selector entry and description, the threshold card header/description (updated to explain the dual adaptation behavior), the **Apply** button, and the live-reading format string `LightSwitch_AmbientLightCurrentReading` = `"Current ambient light: {0:0} lux"`. - Per the contributor guide, **localization is handled by the internal Microsoft team**; we only provided `en-us` strings and would defer other locales to that process. *** ## Files touched Service / module interface: - `LightSwitchService/AmbientLightObserver.h` / `.cpp` (new) - `LightSwitchService/LightSwitchStateManager.h` / `.cpp` - `LightSwitchService/LightSwitchService.cpp` - `LightSwitchService/LightSwitchSettings.h` / `.cpp` - `LightSwitchService/SettingsConstants.h` - `LightSwitchModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp` - `LightSwitchService/LightSwitchService.vcxproj` Settings UI: - `Settings.UI.Library/LightSwitchProperties.cs` / `LightSwitchSettings.cs` - `Settings.UI/SettingsXAML/Views/LightSwitchPage.xaml` / `.xaml.cs` - `Settings.UI/ViewModels/LightSwitchViewModel.cs` - `Settings.UI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw` *** ### Scenario when this would be used? ## Problem and motivation Light Switch currently supports four modes: `Off`, `FixedHours`, `SunsetToSunrise`, and `FollowNightLight`. All four are **time- or state-driven** — none of them react to the *actual* lighting conditions in the room. This leads to mismatches between the active theme and the user's visual comfort in common scenarios: - An office with large windows: a cloudy morning stays "dark-time" by the clock while the room is actually bright, or a sunny afternoon runs past the configured sunset hour. - A user turns a desk lamp on/off in the evening; the theme does not follow until the next scheduled boundary. - Variable weather (cloudy → sunny) changes ambient brightness far faster than sunrise/sunset times move. Many modern Windows devices (laptops, tablets, increasingly desktop monitors) ship with an ambient light sensor that already reports illuminance in lux, and Windows exposes it through the WinRT `Windows.Devices.Sensors.LightSensor` API. Light Switch does not currently use this signal. **Proposal:** Add a mode that switches the theme from the ambient light sensor, with a model tuned to human brightness perception so it does not flicker near the threshold or react to transient brightness dips. *** ## Proposed feature A new `ScheduleMode::FollowAmbientLight` that: - Reads ambient illuminance (lux) from the WinRT `LightSensor`. - Classifies the reading against a user-configurable **ambient light threshold** (default `50` lux, clamped to `0–100000`). - Applies a **hysteresis band** around the threshold so readings hovering near it do not flip the theme repeatedly. - Models **human-eye adaptation** so a dark-adapted user is not flipped to a glaring light theme by a small brightness increase (and, symmetrically, a light-adapted user is not flipped to a dark theme by a brief flicker or passing shadow). - **Degrades gracefully** on devices without a sensor: the mode stays inert and reports "no sensor available" instead of crashing or hanging. - Lets the user calibrate the threshold against a **live lux reading** shown on the settings page. *** ## Design rationale and evidence Per the contributor guide's emphasis on understanding the problem before code, the two non-obvious design choices are grounded in visual-comfort literature and sensor behavior: ### 1. Why the log domain (log10 of lux) Human brightness perception is approximately logarithmic (Weber–Fechner). A fixed linear lux band is not scale-invariant: - At a dim threshold of `50` lux, a `±10` lux band is ±20% — meaningful. - At a bright threshold of `10000` lux, the same `±10` lux band is ±0.1% — smaller than sensor noise, so the theme flickers. - At a very dim threshold, the band can be larger than the threshold itself. By expressing the threshold band and adaptation offsets in **decades** (`log10(max(lux, 1))`), a 2× change in illuminance matters the same at `20` lux as at `20000` lux. The UI keeps showing raw lux to the user; only the internal classification/adaptation model works in the log domain. ### 2. Why smoothing before classification Many ambient light sensor chips quantize readings in fixed `10` lux steps. A classification model fed raw stepped readings oscillates. A short log-domain **exponential moving average (EMA, τ ≈ 10 s)** turns those quantized jumps into a continuous signal **without** adding perceptible lag — because the adaptation model it feeds operates on a 5–15 minute scale, far slower than the EMA. ### 3. Why dual (dark + bright) adaptation Human visual adaptation is asymmetric: - **Dark adaptation is slow** (\~15 minutes to approach full); a user who has been in dim light should not be switched to a glaring light theme by a small, brief brightness increase. So the **light-theme boundary rises** (up to \~0.30 decades ≈ a 2× illuminance) while the environment stays dim, and decays in \~1 minute once it is brighter. - **Light adaptation is fast**, but the symmetric problem exists on the bright side: a light-adapted user should not be flipped to a dark theme by a brief dip (a flickering lamp, a passing shadow). So the **dark-theme boundary lowers** (up to \~0.15 decades ≈ a 1.4× illuminance) while the environment stays bright, and decays in \~1 minute once it is dimmer. Inside the hysteresis band the reading is treated as neutral, so both models relax instead of fighting each other. ### 4. Graceful degradation `AmbientLightObserver` calls `LightSensor::GetDefault()`; if no sensor is present it logs a warning and `IsSensorAvailable()` returns `false`. The service keeps the mode active but inactive, so the rest of Light Switch (manual override, other modes) is unaffected. This avoids the failure mode where a missing sensor degrades the whole module. *** ### Supporting information ## Open questions for the team 1. **Default threshold value.** We chose `50` lux as a reasonable indoor twilight/office-dim value, but the right default likely depends on the devices users actually have. Is there telemetry or a convention to anchor this? 2. **Exposing the log-domain model.** We deliberately kept the UI in raw lux and kept the log-domain model internal, to avoid exposing two mental models. Is that the right call, or would the team prefer to surface the log-domain behavior (e.g., a "sensitivity" control)? 3. **Adaptation constants.** The dark-adaptation accrual (\~15 min), decay (\~1 min), and the bright-side mirror (\~5 min accrual / \~1 min decay, ±0.15 decades) are informed approximations. We'd welcome review against any in-house comfort data. 4. **Sensor availability messaging.** Currently the mode is silently inert without a sensor (with a log line and an info card). Should we also surface a non-blocking in-page notice when the user selects the mode on a sensor-less device? 5. **Naming.** We used `FollowAmbientLight` / `ambientLightThreshold` / `AmbientLightObserver` / `OnAmbientLightChange` for cross-layer consistency (PascalCase for enums/types/methods, camelCase for the persisted config key). We'd confirm these names fit the team's conventions before any PR. *** ## Intent and next steps This issue exists to **inform the PowerToys team of our detailed design and implementation** for an ambient-light-driven Light Switch mode, and to invite discussion on the approach — especially the perceptual model and the open questions above. It is **not** a request to merge the code as-is. If the team agrees the feature fits PowerToys and the approach is sound, we're glad to: - Open a PR against the current `archer-lightswitch-brightness-ambient-lux` branch, - Adjust names, defaults, and structure per review feedback, and - Defer non-`en-us` localization to the internal team. Thank you for considering this.

title: [Feature] UserDllHost.exe Feature Request
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Feature Proposal: UserDllHost.exe — A dedicated CLI utility for hosting and testing DLLs

I'd like to propose a simple, modern CLI utility called UserDllHost.exe designed for developers and power users to execute exported DLL functions directly from the command line.

### Concept & Syntax
Unlike rundll32.exe, which has restrictive function signature requirements and unintuitive syntax, UserDllHost.exe would provide a clean, explicit flag-based interface:

UserDllHost.exe --dll="C:\Path\To\Library.dll" --function="ExportedFunctionName"

### How it works:
1. Launches a user-mode process with standard user permissions.
2. Dynamically loads the specified DLL (via LoadLibrary) and retrieves the target entry point (via GetProcAddress).
3. Executes the function isolated within that host process.
4. Returns explicit error codes and clear CLI output if the file, export, or execution fails.

### Why built-in options (rundll32.exe / dllhost.exe) fall short:
* rundll32 requires a specific CALLBACK signature (`HWND, HINSTANCE, LPSTR, int`), making it unsuitable for quick testing of generic exported C/C++ functions.
* It lacks proper error handling and modern command-line argument parsing.

### Value Proposition:
This tool would significantly streamline quick testing, debugging, and rapid prototyping during Windows software development by eliminating the need to write temporary host applications just to trigger a single DLL export.

I'd love to hear your thoughts on whether this concept could be integrated as a developer tool (e.g., within PowerToys or Windows Developer Mode utilities).

Note: English is not my native language, so I used an AI assistant to structure and translate this proposal.

### Scenario when this would be used?

*(Note: English is not my native language, so I used an AI assistant to structure and translate this proposal.)*

With UserDllHost, the developer can simply open the Terminal or Command Prompt and test any exported DLL function in seconds:

title: Support Customizable Keyboard Shortcuts for Command Palette Input
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Add an option to customize the keyboard shortcuts used in the Command Palette input field.

For example, I'd like to be able to configure shortcuts for:

* navigating between options
* deleting a word
* deleting text to the beginning of the line, etc.

The shortcuts would only apply when the Command Palette input field is focused.


### Scenario when this would be used?

I use keyboard shortcuts heavily when working with PowerToys Command Palette. However, some of the shortcuts used by the input field don't fit my usual workflow, especially for navigating the results and editing the input text.

It would be useful to be able to remap these shortcuts to keys that I'm already familiar with, such as Vim-style or Emacs-style keybindings.

title: Quick Accent: Add a Latin character set
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Quick Accent currently provides character sets for many languages, including Ancient Greek and Proto-Indo-European, but it does not provide a Latin character set.

For Classical Latin, macrons are commonly used in modern educational and scholarly texts to mark vowel length. The core set is:

ā ē ī ō ū ȳ

Most of these characters are already available through other Quick Accent language sets, but ȳ is currently unavailable. This is noticeable in Classical Latin learning materials such as Lingua Latina per se Illustrata (LLPSI), where ȳ occurs in words of Greek origin.

I propose adding a dedicated Latin character set with the following mappings:

A → ā
E → ē
I → ī
O → ō
U → ū
Y → ȳ

Uppercase forms can continue to use Quick Accent's existing uppercase handling.

### Scenario when this would be used?

This would make Quick Accent convenient for typing Classical Latin texts with vowel-length notation, without requiring a separate keyboard layout or character-copying tool.

### Supporting information

_No response_
